meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation when noticing or realizing something.

examples.text: あ、開きました！ありがとうございます。新しい受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Mio, the new receptionist.

examples.text: どうして鏡に眼鏡が……あ！頭の上にあります！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in the mirror... oh! They are on top of my head!

examples.text: あ、待ってください！その通りはここから歩いて五分の近所ですよ！
examples.trans: Oh, wait! That street is right in this neighbourhood, a five-minute walk from here!

meanings.note: Relaxed affirmation or exclamation of realization.

examples.text: ああ、部屋は八室、真鍮の鍵も八つだ。今日は四号室にお客さんが来る。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: ファスナーを見よう……ああ、和子さんのイニシャルがここにある！
examples.trans: Let's check the zipper... yes, Kazuko's initials are right here!

examples.text: 私のスーツケース！上のポケットを開けますね……ああ、赤いリボンです！
examples.trans: My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, my red ribbon!

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of sudden realization or delight.

examples.text: ああっ、その鍵なら机の上にありますよ！
examples.trans: Oh! That key is right on the desk!

examples.text: ああっ、焼きたてのパンのいい香りですね。
examples.trans: Ah, what a lovely smell of freshly baked bread.

あいす.gloss: to love, to care for; (in お付き合いする) to accompany

meanings.note: Written 愛す; five-row (godan) verb variant of 愛する (to love).

meanings.en: to keep company, to go along with (in お付き合いしましょう)
meanings.note: In the polite expression お付き合いしましょう ('let's go together / I'll keep you company'), the sequence あいし comes from 付き合い (association, company) + しましょう (let's do).

examples.text: いいですよ、おつきあいしましょう。
examples.trans: Sure thing, I'll gladly keep you company.

examples.text: 彼は心から映画を愛している。
examples.trans: He loves cinema from the bottom of his heart.

meanings.en: that guy, that fellow, he, she
meanings.note: Informal or rough distal pronoun (written 彼奴) referring to a third person away from both speaker and listener; often conveys familiarity, irritation, or contempt. Pluralized as あいつら.

examples.text: 何なんだよ、あいつら。
examples.trans: What the heck is wrong with those guys?

examples.text: 何だ、あいつ。急に怒り出して。
examples.trans: What's his deal, flying off the handle all of a sudden?

あう.gloss: to meet; to fit, to match; (in 付き合う) to associate with

meanings.note: Written 会う or 逢う; takes the particle に (or と) for the person met.

meanings.en: to match, to suit; (in compounds like 付き合う) to deal with, to associate with
meanings.note: Written 合う; attaches to verb stems to express mutual action, such as 付き合う ('to keep company with, to put up with').

examples.text: こんなやり方してるようじゃ衛星は無理です。もうつきあいきれません。
examples.trans: If you keep acting like this, satellite rights are impossible. I can't deal with you anymore.

examples.text: 明日、駅の前で会いましょう。
examples.trans: Let's meet in front of the station tomorrow.

related.gloss: to associate with, to deal with
to meet by chance, to encounter

meanings.note: This is used as a adj meaning must not.

examples.text: それはとてもあかんです。
examples.trans: It is very must not.

examples.text: もっとあかんしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more must not.

あげくの果て.gloss: in the end, to top it all off

meanings.en: in the end, to top it all off

examples.text: 勝手に衛星にお金をつぎ込んで、勝手にヤクザに借金して、あげくの果てにみんなを売ったんだ！
examples.trans: You poured our money into satellite, borrowed from the yakuza, and in the end sold everybody out!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: After a te-form verb, shows doing an action helpfully for someone else.

examples.text: 床がすり減る前に、美央ちゃん、声をかけて来てあげて！
examples.trans: Mio, go talk to him before he wears out the floorboards!

examples.text: 外の人にはまだ一言も言わないで！まずはあの兄弟に金曜日の午後を過ごさせてあげましょう！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let those brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

meanings.note: Distal demonstrative place pronoun (ko-so-a-do series) referring to a location distant from both speaker and listener, or a place mutually understood in context.
Common colloquial euphemism for the genitals.

examples.text: 村西さん、新会社のビル、あそこで決めていいんですね？全額投資しますよ。
examples.trans: Mr. Muranishi, are we set on buying that building for our new company? It takes all our funds.

examples.text: あそこにも新しい書店ができてます。
examples.trans: A new bookstore has opened up over there as well.

examples.text: じゃあ、あだ名はラグビーでいいか。
examples.trans: Alright then, how about we nickname you Rugby?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Sudden exclamation with a quick catch of breath.

examples.text: あっ、遅かったです！「ありがとうございます」と言って切れました！
examples.trans: Oh, too late! He said 'Thank you' and the line clicked off!

examples.text: 太っ腹だね！……あっ、今、下で中庭の門のベルが鳴らなかった？
examples.trans: Generous! ...Wait, did the courtyard gate bell just ring downstairs?

examples.text: あっ、私の革の手帳！ありがとうございます！ちょうど探していたんです。
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was looking for it right now.

examples.text: そんな君と、世界をあっと言わせたいんだ、俺は。
examples.trans: Together with you, I want to make the whole world gasp in amazement.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Before a time or number, means 'remaining until'; alone or with で, means 'afterward'.

examples.text: しかもその方は、今夜八時にここへ着きます。あと四十分です！
examples.trans: And he arrives here at eight o'clock this evening—in forty minutes!

examples.text: あと三十五分です！ひどい一つ星の口コミを書かれてしまいます！
examples.trans: Thirty-five minutes left! He will write a terrible one-star review!

examples.text: 橋を渡って、右に緑の薬局ですね。そのあとは？
examples.trans: Cross the bridge, green pharmacy on the right. And after that?

meanings.note: Polite second-person pronoun; in Japanese, names and titles are used more often once known.

examples.text: こんにちは！あなたが美央ちゃんね。キッチンの由香だよ。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Mio. I am Yuka from the kitchen.

examples.text: 美央さん、あなたにはおもてなしの才能があります！血圧が救われました！
examples.trans: Mio, you have a true gift for hospitality! My blood pressure is saved!

meanings.note: Plural pronoun for 'you', addressing multiple people.

examples.text: あなたたちは明日来ますか？
examples.trans: Are you all coming tomorrow?

examples.text: これはあなたたちの責任です。
examples.trans: This is your responsibility.

meanings.note: Very polite, deferential form of あなた used by salespeople or service staff.

examples.text: あなた様にお似合いです。
examples.trans: It suits you very well.

examples.text: あなた様のご意見をお聞かせください。
examples.trans: Please let us hear your opinion.

meanings.note: Points to something away from both speakers or known to both.

examples.text: ありがとう、健二さん。あの小さな木の汽車、古くて大切な物に見えましたから。
examples.trans: Thank you, Kenji. That little wooden train looked old and precious.

examples.text: 不思議ですね！あの名札の字、なんだか見覚えがあったんです。
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt strangely familiar to me.

examples.text: とにかく、あの鞄は鍵をかけて大切に保管しておきます。
examples.trans: For now, we will keep that bag safely under lock and key.

examples.text: 時代は変わるってことさ。あの世まで借金持っていくんじゃねえぞ。
examples.trans: Times change, that's what it means. Don't go taking your debts with you to the next world.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Aha, haha (a light, sudden laugh or expression of sudden realization, often conveying amusement or slight embarrassment).

examples.text: あはっ、ばれちゃったか。
examples.trans: Aha, I guess I've been found out.

examples.text: あはっ、面白いね。
examples.trans: Haha, that's funny.

meanings.note: Used with a negative verb or adjective to mean 'not very' or 'not too much' (余り).

examples.text: あまり喜ばないでくださいよ、隆さん。雨の日はやっぱり紙の帳面が一番です。
examples.trans: Do not celebrate too much, Takashi. On rainy days, a paper ledger still wins.

examples.text: このお茶はあまり熱くないので、すぐに飲めますよ。
examples.trans: This tea is not too hot, so you can drink it right away.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of あまり.

examples.text: あまりに突然で驚いた。
examples.trans: It was so sudden that I was surprised.

examples.text: あまりに美しくて言葉が出ない。
examples.trans: It's so beautiful that I'm speechless.

meanings.note: Warm, mildly surprised exclamation.

examples.text: あら、それが月曜日の電車で入れ替わった双子のスーツケースですか？
examples.trans: Oh, is that the twin suitcase swapped on Monday's train?

examples.text: あら、聞いた？昨日はボイラーを直して、今日は兄弟の仲を直すくせに！
examples.trans: Oh, hear that? Yesterday you fixed the boiler, and today you are fixing two brothers!

examples.text: あらまあ、こんなに散らかしてどうしたの。
examples.trans: Oh dear, what happened to make such a mess?

examples.text: あらまあ、すっかり見違えちゃったわね。
examples.trans: My goodness, you look completely different.

examples.text: 冷たい雨の日に温かいお味噌汁を出してもらえるのは実にありがたい。
examples.trans: Being served warm miso soup on a cold rainy day is truly something to be grateful for.

examples.text: 旅先で親切に道を教えていただき、本当にありがたかったです。
examples.trans: I was truly grateful to be kindly shown the way while traveling.

meanings.note: Casual shortened form of ありがとう with the final long vowel dropped. Often followed by sentence-final particles like ね or suffix さん (ありがとさん, 'thanks, pal').

examples.text: ありがとね、気持ちだけで十分よ。お金、大丈夫？
examples.trans: Thank you, sweetheart — the thought alone is plenty. Are you doing okay for money?

examples.text: 長えかくれんぼしやがって。協力ありがとさん。
examples.trans: Quite a long game of hide-and-seek you played. Thanks for the cooperation.

meanings.note: Warm everyday thanks among friends and coworkers.

examples.text: まあ、ありがとう、由香さん。びっくりして手が冷たくなっていたの。
examples.trans: Oh, thank you, Yuka. My hands had turned cold from the surprise.

examples.text: ありがとう、健二さん。あの小さな木の汽車、古くて大切な物に見えましたから。
examples.trans: Thank you, Kenji. That little wooden train looked old and precious.

examples.text: 千円、百円、二百円。一円も狂いなくぴったりです。ありがとう！
examples.trans: One thousand, one hundred, two hundred yen. Exact to the very last yen—thank you!

ありがとうございます.lemma: ありがとうございます

meanings.note: Standard polite expression of gratitude.

examples.text: あ、開きました！ありがとうございます。新しい受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Mio, the new receptionist.

examples.text: ありがとうございます！ここでは下の名前で呼びますか？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we call each other by first names here?

examples.text: お二人とも、どうもありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both very much.

surface: ありがとうございます

ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。.lemma: ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。

examples.text: ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。
examples.trans: Closing phrase.

examples.text: ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。
examples.trans: Closing phrase.

surface: ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。

ありのまま.gloss: as it is, in one's natural state, unvarnished

meanings.en: as it is, in one's natural state, without pretension or disguise
meanings.note: Written 有りの儘; functions as a noun (ありのままを), an adjectival modifier with の (ありのままの姿, 'one's natural form'), or an adverb (often with に).

examples.text: 人のありのままの姿撮って、わいせつなんですか？
examples.trans: Is filming people just as they naturally are really indecent?

examples.text: ありのままを生きたいんです。どうしたらいいですか？
examples.trans: I want to live just as I truly am. What should I do?

related.gloss: just like that, as it is

meanings.note: Used for inanimate things, places, events, and schedules; contrasts with いる for living beings.

examples.text: だって、おいしいコーヒーと温かいパンがあれば仲良くなれるもん！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

examples.text: どうして鏡に眼鏡が……あ！頭の上にあります！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in the mirror... oh! They are on top of my head!

examples.text: おでこの上にちゃんとありましたね。
examples.trans: Right there safe and sound on your forehead.

meanings.en: as it is; one's natural, unaltered state
meanings.note: Often used with に (あるがままに) to mean 'just as one is'.

examples.text: あるがままを受け入れる。
examples.trans: Accept things as they are.

examples.text: あるがままに生きる。
examples.trans: Live as your true self.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something distant from both speaker and listener.

examples.text: 誰もいないよ。あれは四号室のブザーだ。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

examples.text: 受付で「あれ」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'あれ' (that one).

meanings.note: Surprised exclamation when spotting something unexpected.

examples.text: あれっ、カウンターにあるこの小さな茶色い革の手帳は誰のですか？
examples.trans: Wait—whose small brown leather notebook is this on the counter?

examples.text: すみません……あれっ、その声！まさか、ピアノの和子先生ですか！？
examples.trans: Excuse me... wait, that voice! Could it be Miss Kazuko, my piano teacher?!

meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.

examples.text: あんた、面白いね。
examples.trans: You're interesting.

examples.text: あんたも来るの？
examples.trans: Are you coming too?

meanings.note: Casual or blunt plural form of あんた, often used when scolding or addressing a group.

examples.text: あんたたち、静かにしなさい。
examples.trans: You guys, be quiet.

examples.text: あんたたちも一緒に行くの？
examples.trans: Are you guys going too?

あんな.gloss: that kind of, such, like that

meanings.en: that sort of, such, like that
meanings.note: Pre-noun adjectival (連体詞) in the ko-so-a-do series; directly precedes a noun (e.g., あんなこと, あんなもの) to point to something distant or emotionally extreme, often with disapproval or amazement.

examples.text: あんなものを見せて損すんのはお前なんだから。
examples.trans: Showing half-baked work like that only hurts your own name.

examples.text: 大丈夫なんですか？あんなこと言って。
examples.trans: Are you sure it's okay to say something like that?

あんなに.gloss: so much, to that extent, like that

meanings.en: so, to that extent, that much
meanings.note: Adverbial form of あんな; modifies verbs and adjectives to emphasize a high degree or intensity, often expressing surprise or bewilderment.

examples.text: これほどの素材を使って、どうしてあんなにまずい料理が出来上がるのか不思議でしかたがない。
examples.trans: With raw talent this fine, it baffles me how anyone could cook up such a terrible dish.

examples.text: なんであの店はあんなに繁盛してるんだ？
examples.trans: Why on earth is that shop doing such booming business?

あー.gloss: ah, oh, man, ugh (sigh or exclamation)

meanings.note: Informal spoken interjection expressing boredom, exhaustion, exasperation, or sudden realization.

examples.text: シラけたわ、あーつまんねえ。
examples.trans: What a buzzkill—man, this is boring.

examples.text: あー、今日もよく働いたな。
examples.trans: Man, we sure put in a hard day's work today.

meanings.note: This is used as a noun meaning attention.

examples.text: これはいです。
examples.trans: This is attention.

examples.text: そのいを見せてください。
examples.trans: Please show me the attention.

meanings.note: Conjugates on the stem よ- in negative (よくない), past (よかった), and adverbial (よく) forms.

examples.text: はじめまして、由香さん。すごくいい匂いですね！
examples.trans: Nice to meet you, Yuka. Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 皆さん、おはようございます！ようこそ、美央さん。準備はいいですか？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Mio. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 本当にいいんですか？とても素敵で暖かそう！
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and warm!

meanings.note: Polite negative reply or modest deflection of praise/apology.

examples.text: いいえ、ペンと古いレシートが三枚だけです！
examples.trans: No, only a pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: いいえ、隆さん。六号室には一時間前に南から来たご夫婦が入りました。
examples.trans: No, Takashi. The couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

examples.text: いいえ、お気になさらないでください！陽翔さまですね。
examples.trans: Not at all, please do not worry! You must be Haruto.

meanings.note: Written いい加減; na-adjective describing someone who acts sloppily or without proper commitment.

meanings.en: enough, a reasonable degree (especially in いい加減にしろ)
meanings.note: Used adverbially with に to tell someone to stop going too far ('Cut it out! / Enough already!').

examples.text: いいかげんにしろ！聞いてませんよ！
examples.trans: Enough of this! Nobody told me a word about this!

examples.text: あの人、いくら何でもいいかげんすぎない？いろいろ順番おかしいよ。
examples.trans: Isn't that guy way too irresponsible? His priorities are completely backward.

meanings.note: Godan verb; in ～ということ, means 'the fact that...' or 'meaning that...'.

examples.text: それはどういうことですか。
examples.trans: What does that mean?

examples.text: 田中さんという人が来ました。
examples.trans: A person named Tanaka came.

meanings.note: Crisp, polite variant of いいえ used to reply in the negative or modestly deflect praise or concern.
As a noun written 家 (いえ), refers to a physical house or a family lineage.

examples.text: いえ、そんなことはありませんよ。
examples.trans: No, not at all—that's certainly not the case.

examples.text: お怪我はありませんか？——いえ、大丈夫です。
examples.trans: Are you hurt? — No, I'm fine.

いえいえ.gloss: no, no; not at all; don't mention it

meanings.en: no, no; not at all; by no means
meanings.note: Reduplicated form of いえ; used politely to wave off an apology, deflect a compliment, or reassure the listener.

examples.text: いえいえ、今すぐにでも欲しいという意思の表れでございます。
examples.trans: Not at all—it is proof of my determination to have this right away.

examples.text: いえいえ、お礼なんてとんでもないです。
examples.trans: No, no, there's no need to thank me at all.

meanings.note: Polite counterpart of どう, often used when offering tea or asking about a guest's trip.

examples.text: はい、二階の四号室ですね！電車の旅はいかがでしたか？
examples.trans: Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?

examples.text: 素晴らしいご選択です！横に蜂蜜かりんごジャムはいかがですか？
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。
examples.trans: Work is going smoothly.

meanings.note: Asks the number of items counted with つ or general items.

examples.text: 由香さん、そのオーブンでは毎朝いくつシナモンロールとレモンケーキが焼けますか？
examples.trans: Yuka, how many cinnamon rolls and lemon cakes can that oven bake each morning?

examples.text: 受付で「いくつ」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'いくつ' (how many).

meanings.note: Most often heard in the negative 〜てはいけない / 〜ないといけない ('must not' / 'must').

examples.text: 誰かが中庭の鉢植えを世話しないといけないからな。
examples.trans: Somebody has to look after the potted plants in the courtyard.

examples.text: 中を見てはいけませんよ……あ、真ん中のページが開いています！
examples.trans: We must not peek inside... oh, it fell open to the middle page!

いずれ.gloss: eventually, sooner or later; either, which

meanings.en: eventually, sooner or later, in due course
meanings.note: Written 何れ; adverb indicating that something is bound to happen at some point in the future.
In formal expressions such as いずれにせよ ('in any case'), functions as a pronoun meaning 'which' or 'either'.

examples.text: 予言しときますよ。あなたたちは、いずれビデオ市場を独占できる。
examples.trans: Let me make a prediction: your company will eventually monopolize the video market.

examples.text: 本当のことを隠しても、いずれ知られるだろう。
examples.trans: Even if you hide the truth, it will come out sooner or later.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of する used in polite hospitality toward guests.

examples.text: 失礼いたします、和子さん。堂々と事務室へ引き上げます！
examples.trans: Excuse me, Kazuko. I shall retreat to my office with dignity!

examples.text: 「物件売却のお知らせ。中庭八番館を、商業オフィス用として売却いたします。」
examples.trans: 'Notice of Property Sale: Number Eight Courtyard Building is offered for commercial office sale.'

examples.text: 失礼いたします。温かいお茶でございます。焼きたてのレモンケーキもすぐ参りますね。
examples.trans: Excuse me, gentlemen. Here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on its way right now.

meanings.note: Spoken pain exclamation reduced from 痛い ('it hurts!').

examples.text: いたた、踏み台の段で足を滑らせちゃった！
examples.trans: Ouch, my foot slipped on the step of the stool!

examples.text: いたた、棚の角に少しぶつけました。
examples.trans: Ow, I bumped slightly against the corner of the shelf.

いただきます.gloss: thank you for the meal; I accept

meanings.en: thank you for the meal; I accept
meanings.note: Set phrase said before eating or drinking, literally 'I humbly receive'.

examples.text: 嬉しいです！さあ、朝ごはんをしっかりいただきますわ。
examples.trans: How wonderful! Now I am ready to enjoy a hearty breakfast.

examples.text: いただきます、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Thank you for the meal — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: これ、いただきます。
examples.trans: I will take / eat this.

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Polite potential of いただく, used after a te-form verb for courteous requests.

examples.text: 屋根裏の書斎ですか？まず見せていただけますか？
examples.trans: An attic study? May I take a look at it first?

examples.text: 渡しませんよ、由香さん！美央さん、当館の正式なフロントマネージャーとして残っていただけますか？
examples.trans: Hands off, Yuka! Mio, will you stay on as our permanent front-desk manager?

examples.text: いちゃもんつけてんじゃねえよ！
examples.trans: Quit picking a fight over nothing!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

いっか.gloss: is that okay?, will that do? (casual); one family (一家)

meanings.en: is that okay?, will that do?, let's leave it at that (contraction of いいか)
meanings.note: Colloquial spoken contraction of いいか with a geminate stop (っ), used when casually proposing an arrangement or shrugging something off (e.g., まあいっか, 'oh well, whatever').

meanings.en: one family, household, syndicate clan (written 一家)
meanings.note: When written 一家 (いっか), a noun meaning an entire family or a yakuza gang family.

examples.text: あとごはんは当番制でいっか。まずかったらちゃんと言い合おうね。
examples.trans: And let's take turns cooking meals, okay? If something tastes bad, let's tell each other honestly.

examples.text: 細かいことは気にしなくても、まあいっか。
examples.trans: There's no need to sweat the small stuff—oh well, it's fine.

examples.text: いっそ諦めた方が楽かもしれない。
examples.trans: It might be easier to just give up rather than continue.

examples.text: こんなに苦しいなら、いっそ死んでしまいたい。
examples.trans: If it's this painful, I'd rather just die.

examples.text: はい、いってきます。行くぞ！
examples.trans: Yes, off I go. Let's move!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

いってらっしゃい.gloss: have a good day; see you later

meanings.en: have a good day; take care (said to someone leaving)
meanings.note: Standard greeting said by those staying behind when someone leaves home.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、気をつけてね。
examples.trans: Have a good day, take care.

examples.text: いってらっしゃい、早く帰ってね。
examples.trans: See you later, come home early.

meanings.note: Often used as でいっぱいになる ('become full of').

examples.text: 夏になると旅館はお客さんでいっぱいになります。
examples.trans: When summer comes, the inn fills up with guests.

examples.text: かごの中に新鮮なレモンがいっぱい入っています。
examples.trans: Plenty of fresh lemons are packed in the basket.

meanings.note: Question word for time; with だって means 'anytime'.

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 受付で「いつ」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'いつ' (when).

いつか.gloss: someday, one day; the fifth day (五日)

meanings.en: someday, one day, sooner or later
meanings.note: Formed from いつ ('when') + か; refers to an unspecified time in the future (or occasionally in the past, 'some time ago').

meanings.en: the fifth day of the month, five days (written 五日)
meanings.note: Temporal noun written 五日 (いつか).

examples.text: お母さん、私ね、いつかイタリアに留学したいの。
examples.trans: Mother, listen—someday I want to study abroad in Italy.

examples.text: いつかステーキたらふく食べたいですね。
examples.trans: Someday it would be nice to eat our fill of steak.

meanings.note: Indefinite temporal adverb formed from いつ ('when') + でも ('even; any').

examples.text: 窓を大きく開けて、午後のそよ風が入ってきます……いつでもどうぞ、和子先生！
examples.trans: Windows wide open, afternoon breeze coming in—whenever you are ready, Kazuko!

examples.text: お困りのときは、いつでも受付に声をかけてくださいね。
examples.trans: Whenever you need a hand, please feel free to call the front desk anytime.

いつまでも.gloss: forever; as long as you like; indefinitely

meanings.en: forever; as long as you like; indefinitely
meanings.note: Built from いつ ('when') + まで ('until') + も ('even'); means 'for any length of time'.

examples.text: 四号室は、和子さんが望むだけいつまでもお使いください。
examples.trans: Please use Room Four for as long as you wish, Kazuko.

examples.text: 中庭の温かい音楽をいつまでも聴いていたいですね。
examples.trans: I want to keep listening to the warm music in the courtyard forever.

meanings.note: Everyday frequency adverb.

examples.text: 初日はいつも早く歩きます。パソコンはどこですか？
examples.trans: I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: お兄ちゃんは元気で声が大きくて、いつも音階を急いで弾いていたわ。
examples.trans: The older brother was energetic and loud, always rushing through his musical scales.

examples.text: 弾き終わるといつも、「どうして雨の日はピアノの音が温かいの？」って聞くのよ。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he always asked, 'Why does the piano sound warmer on rainy days?'

meanings.note: Refers to any cousin regardless of gender or age.

examples.text: 完全な間違いだったんです！いとこの部屋で開けたら、楽譜と赤いリボンが見えて。
examples.trans: It was a total accident! When I opened it at my cousin's flat, I saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

examples.text: 受付にいとこがあります。
examples.trans: There is cousin at the reception desk.

meanings.note: negative form of いる (iru)

examples.text: 部屋に誰もいない。
examples.trans: There is no one in the room.

examples.text: 彼はまだ来ていない。
examples.trans: He hasn't come yet.

いま.gloss: now, the present moment; living room (居間)

meanings.note: Written 今; used as both a temporal noun (今の時代, 'the present era') and an adverb ('right now'). Also forms part of the greeting ただいま ('I'm home! / Just now').

meanings.en: living room, sitting room (written 居間)
meanings.note: When written 居間, refers to a traditional or family living room.

examples.text: ただいま！今日もお疲れさま。
examples.trans: I'm home! Good job again today.

examples.text: 今から新しい撮影を始めます。
examples.trans: We are starting the new shoot right now.

meanings.note: Casual 'no' or conversational softener when correcting gently.

examples.text: おはよう。いや、まず取っ手を上げて、それから押すんだ。
examples.trans: Morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: 受付で「いや」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'いや' (no).

meanings.note: Warm, slightly bashful conversational interjection.

examples.text: 私ですか？いやあ、時間に正確なのが大好きで！七時十四分は美しい時間です！
examples.trans: Me? Oh, I simply adore punctuality! Seven fourteen is a beautiful minute!

examples.text: いやあ、大切なお客さまにうちの大家さんの悩みを相談するなんてできません！
examples.trans: Oh, I could never trouble a valued guest with our landlord worries!

meanings.note: Standard hospitality greeting to guests entering an inn, café, or shop.

examples.text: いらっしゃいませ！おはようございます。
examples.trans: Welcome! Good morning, madam.

examples.text: いらっしゃいませ！こんばんは。雨の中、どうぞ中へお入りください。
examples.trans: Welcome! Good evening. Please come inside out of the rain.

meanings.note: Respectful counterpart of いる, 来る, and 行く when speaking of guests or elders.

examples.text: お兄さんというものをよく分かっていらっしゃいますね、健二さん。
examples.trans: You understand older brothers very well, Kenji.

examples.text: そんなに昔のことなのに、まだ覚えていらっしゃるんですか？
examples.trans: After all these years, you still remember that?

meanings.note: Used for people and animals, and after a te-form verb for ongoing states or actions.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 誰もいないよ。あれは四号室のブザーだ。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

examples.text: じゃあ、この宿が自分で挨拶しているんですね？
examples.trans: So the inn is saying hello on its own?

いろいろ.gloss: various, all sorts of, in many ways

meanings.en: various, all kinds of, in many ways
meanings.note: Written 色々; used adverbially (often with と) to mean 'in various ways' or as a na-adjective (いろいろな) meaning 'all sorts of'.

examples.text: まあ、俺のシマで飼ってるからな、自由自在だ。そのかわりいろいろと便宜を頼みますよ。
examples.trans: Well, I keep him on my turf, so he's on my leash — in return, I'll count on plenty of favors from you.

examples.text: この書類にはいろいろ契約のことが書いてあります。
examples.trans: All sorts of contract details are written in this document.

examples.text: お湯が沸いたから、そろそろ熱いお茶を淹れよう。
examples.trans: Since the water has boiled, let's brew some hot tea now.

examples.text: 雨が止んだうちに、中庭の落ち葉をきれいに掃いておこう。
examples.trans: While the rain has stopped, let's sweep up the fallen leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Natural groan when wincing from a sudden twist or strain.

examples.text: うう、右の足首を少しひねったみたいです。
examples.trans: Ooh, it seems I slightly twisted my right ankle.

examples.text: うう、この木の箱は思ったより重いですね。
examples.trans: Ugh, this wooden box is heavier than I thought.

meanings.note: Grunt of physical effort when pulling or lifting something stubborn.

examples.text: ううっ、この古い雨戸は重くて動きません！
examples.trans: Ugh, this old shutter is heavy and won't budge!

examples.text: ううっ、もうちょっとで箱が持ち上がります。
examples.trans: Oof, just a little more and the crate will lift.

meanings.note: In exclamations like うそだろ, expresses stunned disbelief ('no way!').

examples.text: 白い紙を開けるぞ……うそだろ！おじいちゃんが彫った木の機関車だ！
examples.trans: Opening the white paper... no way! It is the wooden locomotive Grandpa carved!

examples.text: 受付にうそがあります。
examples.trans: There is lie at the reception desk.

meanings.note: With に after an adjective/verb ('while still warm'), or referring to one's own inn/home.

examples.text: 朝の焼きたてパンだよ！温かいうちに一つ食べて。
examples.trans: Freshly baked morning bread! Have one while it is still warm.

examples.text: うちの横に書いてある文字を見て！「中庭の幅、通りの音、静けさ十点満点中九点！」
examples.trans: Look at the words beside ours: 'Courtyard width, street noise, quietness: nine points out of ten!'

examples.text: うちの中庭が、陽翔さんの……お仕事に静かでよかったです。
examples.trans: We are glad our courtyard is peaceful for your... work.

meanings.note: Used when slipping up or forgetting something without meaning to.

examples.text: うっかり鍵を机の上に置いたまま出かけました。
examples.trans: I accidentally went out leaving the key on the desk.

examples.text: 急いでいて、うっかり別のバスに乗ってしまった。
examples.trans: In my hurry, I accidentally got on the wrong bus.

examples.text: 彼はベッドにうつ伏せになって寝た。
examples.trans: He slept lying face down on the bed.

examples.text: うつ伏せの姿勢は腰に負担がかかる。
examples.trans: Lying in a prone position puts strain on the lower back.

meanings.note: To nod one's head in agreement.

examples.text: 大阪旧市街条例第十四条……そしてここにいる兄は、今うなずいた！
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the {CITY} Old Quarter Act—and my brother here just nodded!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにうなずきます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully nod.

examples.text: うな重を三つ特上でごちそういたしますよ。
examples.trans: Let me treat the three of you to deluxe grilled eel boxes.

examples.text: はいはい、お疲れさま。うな重キャンセル。
examples.trans: All right, good work, gentlemen. Cancel the eel boxes.

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
examples.trans: The plan went well.

examples.text: 彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

うる.gloss: to sell (売る); to obtain (得る); (in うるさい/うっせえ) noisy

meanings.en: to sell, to put on the market
meanings.note: Written 売る; godan transitive verb. Also written 得る (うる/える), meaning 'to obtain' or used after a verb stem to mean 'to be able to'.

meanings.en: noisy, annoying (root of うるさい, contracted in rough speech to うっせえ)
meanings.note: In rough masculine speech, うるさい ('noisy / shut up') contracts to うっせえ.

examples.text: このビデオを全国で売るつもりだ。
examples.trans: I intend to sell this video all across the country.

examples.text: うっせえな、お前らは。静かに食え。
examples.trans: Pipe down, all of you — eat quietly.

related.gloss: to sell well, to be popular

meanings.note: Describes unpleasant noise or commotion.

examples.text: 実は、うるさい一階の部屋は苦手なんです。この空間、すごく気に入りました！
examples.trans: To tell the truth, I dislike noisy ground-floor rooms. I love this space!

examples.text: 今日はとてもうるさいですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very noisy, isn't it?

meanings.note: Written 嬉しい; i-adjective expressing immediate heartfelt joy or gratitude brought about by an event or someone's kindness.

examples.text: 正直、撮影も、ただのお金目当てだったのに、うれしいんだ。
examples.trans: Honestly, I only came to the shoot for the money, yet I feel so happy.

examples.text: うれしいわ。どうぞ召し上がってちょうだい。
examples.trans: I'm so glad! Please, go ahead and help yourself.

meanings.note: This is used as a adv meaning aimlessly.

examples.text: それはとてもうろうろです。
examples.trans: It is very aimlessly.

examples.text: もっとうろうろしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more aimlessly.

meanings.note: Colloquial interjection (often lengthened to うわあ or pronounced with a glottal stop うわっ) expressing sudden surprise, admiration, or dismay.
As a prefix written 上 (うわ-), attaches to nouns such as 上着 ('jacket, outer garment') or 上澄み ('surface layer').

examples.text: うわあ、おいしそう！
examples.trans: Wow, that looks delicious!

examples.text: うわ、もうこんな時間だ。急がないと。
examples.trans: Whoa, it's already this late—we have to hurry.

examples.text: 村西さん、懲役三百七十年といううわさが出ていますが？
examples.trans: Mr. Muranishi, rumors are circulating of a three-hundred-seventy-year prison sentence?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Informal affirmative interjection used with friends, family, or subordinates. Contrast with ううん ('no, uh-uh'), which is longer and spoken with a falling-rising intonation.
As a noun written 運, refers to one's luck or fate (e.g., 運がいい, 'lucky').

examples.text: うん、いいんじゃないか？それでいこう。
examples.trans: Yeah, doesn't that sound good? Let's go with that.

examples.text: ううん、別に何もないよ。
examples.trans: No, nothing happened at all.

examples.text: うーん、どうすればいいか分からないな。
examples.trans: Mmm, I don't know what to do.

examples.text: うーん、少し考えてから返事します。
examples.trans: Well, let me think about it a little before replying.

meanings.note: Brief sound of hesitation or surprise.

examples.text: ええと、ベッドと机と椅子はありますが、枕元のランプがありません。
examples.trans: Let's see: there are a bed, a desk, and a chair, yet there is no bedside lamp.

examples.text: え、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Eh? — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Warm, polite conversational 'yes'.

examples.text: ええ。表の大通りはにぎやかなのに、この中庭では葉っぱと鳥の声だけが聞こえます。
examples.trans: Yes. The main street out front is lively, yet inside this courtyard you only hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: ええ、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Yes — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Emphatic exclamation of surprise.

examples.text: ええっ！走っていたから、包みが全部同じに見えました！
examples.trans: Oh no! Because I was running, all the wrappers looked identical!

examples.text: ええっ、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: What?! — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Quick surprised reaction.

examples.text: えっ、今の音は何ですか？誰かが二回鳴らしましたよ！
examples.trans: Wait, what was that sound just now? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: えっ、でも外側は同じ濃い青ですよ！
examples.trans: Wait, yet the outside is the exact same dark blue!

examples.text: えっ？私の予約に何か問題がありましたか？
examples.trans: Oh? Was there some problem with my reservation?

meanings.note: Conversational filler while checking or thinking (often lengthened to ええと).

examples.text: ええと、ベッドと机と椅子はありますが、枕元のランプがありません。
examples.trans: Let's see: there are a bed, a desk, and a chair, yet there is no bedside lamp.

examples.text: えと、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Let's see — nice weather again today!

えな.gloss: rough adjective ending + particle な (-ee na); placenta (胞衣)

meanings.en: isn't it, man (rough adjective ending -え + sentence-final particle な)
meanings.note: In rough spoken Japanese, i-adjectives ending in -ai or -oi coalesce to -ee (e.g., ひどい → ひでえ, うるさい → うっせえ), followed by the emphatic particle な.
Literary or medical noun written 胞衣 (えな).

examples.text: もうさっさと終わらせましょ、こんな仕事。しかしひでえな、作文かこれ？
examples.trans: Let's just get a job like this over with fast—honestly, what an awful script!

examples.text: うっせえな、お前らは。静かに食え。
examples.trans: Pipe down, all of you — eat quietly.

えむ.gloss: to smile (笑む); M, masochist (エム)

meanings.note: Written 笑む; literary godan verb meaning to smile gently or for flower buds to open (found in compounds like 微笑む, 'to smile').

meanings.en: M, masochist (usually written エム or M)
meanings.note: In colloquial and adult industry contexts, refers to the letter M or a masochistic role/personality (paired with S / エス).

examples.text: 彼女はかすかに笑んでうなずいた。
examples.trans: She smiled faintly and nodded.

examples.text: まとまった金借りてえんだったら、うってつけのヤツがいんだろ。長年のつきあいの。
examples.trans: If you want to borrow a big lump sum, you know the perfect guy—an old acquaintance of yours.

meanings.note: Honorific/beautifying prefix attached primarily to native Japanese nouns and verb stems.

examples.text: お持ちしますよ。おや、中に石でも入っていますか？
examples.trans: Allow me to carry it. Goodness, are there stones inside here?

examples.text: 新鮮なオレンジジュースは、私がお注ぎしますよ！
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice for you!

examples.text: 隆さん、きれいな布と冷たい水をお持ちしました。
examples.trans: Takashi, I brought a clean cloth and cold water.

おい.gloss: hey!, oi!, listen! (rough call for attention)

meanings.note: Informal, predominantly masculine interjection used to call out to someone, get attention, or express irritation.
As a noun, written 甥 ('nephew') or 老い ('aging, old age').

examples.text: おい、どうだった？うまくいったのか？
examples.trans: Hey, how did it go? Did things work out?

examples.text: おい、もう行こうぜ。
examples.trans: Hey, let's get going already.

おいおい.gloss: hey, come on!, hold on!; gradually (追々)

meanings.en: hey, hey!; hold on!; come on!
meanings.note: Reduplicated form of おい; interjection used to protest, calm someone down, or express mild disbelief at someone's words or actions.

meanings.en: gradually, little by little, in due time (written 追々)
meanings.note: As an adverb written 追々, indicates that something will happen step by step later on (or onomatopoeically describes weeping aloud, 'boohoo').

examples.text: おいおい、何が違うんだよ。
examples.trans: Hey, come on, what is the big difference?

examples.text: おいおい、お前どうしたんだよ？
examples.trans: Whoa, hey—what's the matter with you?

meanings.note: Everyday i-adjective for good food and drink.

examples.text: だって、おいしいコーヒーと温かいパンがあれば仲良くなれるもん！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

examples.text: スクランブルエッグがとてもおいしいわ、美央さん。由香さんによろしく伝えてね。
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, Mio. Tell Yuka my compliments!

meanings.note: Warm casual imperative helper; 見ておいで means 'go take a look'.

examples.text: 先にキッチンの様子を見ておいで。
examples.trans: Go check on the kitchen first.

examples.text: 雨が降る前に早く中へおいで。
examples.trans: Come inside quickly before it rains.

meanings.note: Exclamation of recognition, mild surprise, or approval, often used casually by men
Informal affirmative response or acknowledgment

examples.text: おお、そうか、それはよかった。どんなところが？
examples.trans: Oh, is that right? That's great. Which part in particular?

examples.text: おお、来てたのか、チュウさん。
examples.trans: Oh, so you're here too, Mr. Chu.

meanings.note: Casual greeting to someone returning home or coming back to a group (short for お帰(かえ)りなさい)

examples.text: おかえり。出所祝いだ。
examples.trans: Welcome back. Consider this a release celebration.

examples.text: おかえり、パパ！今日のご飯は何？
examples.trans: Welcome home, Dad! What's for dinner today?

meanings.note: Polite set greeting used when someone returns home, to an office, or from a long absence (kanji: お帰りなさい)

examples.text: もう二度と会えないと思ってました。おかえりなさい。
examples.trans: We thought we would never see you again. Welcome home.

examples.text: おかえりなさい。外の風、冷たかったでしょう。
examples.trans: Welcome home. The wind outside must have been cold.

meanings.note: Used in the polite apology ご迷惑をおかけしました ('sorry for causing trouble').

examples.text: ご迷惑をおかけしました、健二さん。一週間も鞄を守ってくれてありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Sorry for the trouble, Kenji. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.

examples.text: 受付におかけがあります。
examples.trans: There is causing at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Credits a positive outcome to someone's help (おかげで / おかげさまで).

examples.text: 皆さんのおかげで、この旅が救われましたわ。
examples.trans: Thanks to all of you, my whole trip is saved.

examples.text: おかげさまで、今夜はぐっすり眠れそうです。
examples.trans: Thanks to your kindness, I think I will sleep soundly tonight.

examples.text: よかった！機転のおかげで朝ごはんが助かりましたね。
examples.trans: What a relief! Quick thinking saved breakfast again.

meanings.note: i-adjective (kanji: 可笑しい); describes behavior or situations that feel off or don't add up
Describes something laughable or humorous

examples.text: ずっとおかしいと思ってました。
examples.trans: All these years I thought something didn't add up.

examples.text: 池沢に会ってから様子がおかしいぞ。
examples.trans: You've been acting strange ever since you met Ikezawa.

meanings.note: Used playfully for a chef's non-negotiable kitchen rules.

examples.text: 私のキッチンのおきてをよく聞いてくださいね！
examples.trans: Listen carefully to my kitchen rules!

examples.text: 焼きたてのパンを冷ますのは大切なおきてです。
examples.trans: Letting freshly baked bread cool is an important rule.

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in place

meanings.en: do in advance; keep in place
meanings.note: After a te-form verb (〜ておく), indicates preparing ahead or leaving something safely as is.

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: もう一つの青いスーツケースは、荷物室にしっかり鍵をかけておきました。
examples.trans: I locked the other blue suitcase safely inside our luggage room.

examples.text: とにかく、あの鞄は鍵をかけて大切に保管しておきます。
examples.trans: For now, we will keep that bag safely under lock and key.

meanings.note: Polite prefix お- + しゃべり ('talking'); warm everyday word for relaxed chatting.

examples.text: 午後のお茶を飲みながら楽しいおしゃべりをしました。
examples.trans: We had a cheerful chat over afternoon tea.

examples.text: カフェの隅から楽しそうなおしゃべりが聞こえます。
examples.trans: Happy conversation can be heard from the corner of the café.

meanings.note: Your own uncle when talking to others; address him as おじさん.

examples.text: 思い出しました！私が十歳のとき、おじはここを「冬のお茶の部屋」と呼んでいました！
examples.trans: Now I remember! When I was ten, my uncle called this 'the winter tea room'!

examples.text: おじは毎年、夏に大阪へ来ます。
examples.trans: My uncle comes to Osaka every summer.

meanings.note: Polite word for someone's grandfather or an older man.

examples.text: 大工のおじいさんと孫の兄弟が二人で暮らしていて、お兄ちゃんはピアノ、弟は汽車が大好きだったの！
examples.trans: A master carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the younger brother loved trains!

examples.text: 大工のおじいさん……そして鞄の中には小さな木の汽車！
examples.trans: A carpenter grandfather... and inside the bag, a small wooden train!

examples.text: おじいさんが、粉砂糖のかかった温かいレモンケーキを切ってくれたの！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar!

meanings.note: Affectionate family word for grandfather.

cells: おじいちゃんじゃない

examples.text: それ、おじいちゃんの作業場にあった古い紺色の鞄じゃないか？
examples.trans: Isn't that the old dark-blue bag from Grandpa's workshop?

examples.text: 白い紙を開けるぞ……うそだろ！おじいちゃんが彫った木の機関車だ！
examples.trans: Opening the white paper... no way! It is the wooden locomotive Grandpa carved!

meanings.note: Polite noun from 揃う ('match, be paired'), often with の before a noun.

examples.text: おそろいの白いカップを二つ買いました。
examples.trans: We bought two matching white cups.

examples.text: 姉妹でおそろいの帽子をかぶっています。
examples.trans: The sisters are wearing matching hats.

meanings.note: Colloquial, somewhat rough contraction of おじさん used to refer to or address a middle-aged or older man

examples.text: 逃げろ、おっさん！
examples.trans: Run for it, old man!

examples.text: よう、おっさん、景気はどうだ？
examples.trans: Hey there, old man, how's business going?

meanings.note: Subject-exalting honorific (尊敬語) equivalent of 言う ('to say'); polite stem is おっしゃい- (おっしゃいます).

examples.text: おめでとうございます、隆さん！担当者の方は九号室について何とおっしゃいましたか？
examples.trans: Congratulations, Takashi! What did the clerk say about Room Nine?

examples.text: 和子先生がおっしゃった通り、真ん中のレの音がきれいになりました。
examples.trans: Just as Kazuko said, the middle D note sounds clear again.

meanings.note: Quick exclamation when catching a slip or stumble.

examples.text: 当館では五つ星のサービスが当たり前……おっと！
examples.trans: At our inn, five-star service comes naturally... whoops!

examples.text: おっと、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Whoops! — nice weather again today!

meanings.en: keeping company, going along with, socializing
meanings.note: Found in お付(つ)き合(あ)い (socializing, keeping someone company, or dating)
Written お付(つ)き; a person assigned to attend to an actor, executive, or VIP

examples.text: いいですよ、おつきあいしましょう。
examples.trans: Sure, I'll gladly keep you company.

examples.text: 今夜は最後までおつきあいしますよ。
examples.trans: I'll stick with you until the very end tonight.

meanings.note: Money returned after paying cash.

examples.text: はい、ここです！全部で三千八百円だったので、おつりは千二百円です。
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost three thousand eight hundred yen, so the change is twelve hundred yen.

examples.text: 受付におつりがあります。
examples.trans: There is change at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday word for forehead.

examples.text: おでこの上にちゃんとありましたね。
examples.trans: Right there safe and sound on your forehead.

examples.text: ばっちり清潔です、隆さん！眼鏡もおでこじゃなくてちゃんと鼻の上にありますよ。
examples.trans: Spotless and sharp, Takashi! Even your glasses are on your nose instead of your forehead.

examples.text: おでこから眼鏡を下ろしますね……えっ、「九号室」！？
examples.trans: Let me pull my glasses down from my forehead... wait, 'Room Nine'?!

examples.text: おとなしくしろ！
examples.trans: Pipe down and behave!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite everyday word for stomach (kanji: お腹); commonly used in おなかがすく (to get hungry) and おなかがいっぱい (full)

examples.text: おなかすいた。何か食べに行こうよ。
examples.trans: I'm hungry. Let's go get something to eat.

examples.text: 笑いすぎておなかが痛い。
examples.trans: My stomach hurts from laughing so hard.

meanings.note: Friendly morning greeting among coworkers, friends, and family.

examples.text: おはよう。いや、まず取っ手を上げて、それから押すんだ。
examples.trans: Morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: おはよう、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Good morning — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Standard polite morning greeting.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 皆さん、おはようございます！ようこそ、美央さん。準備はいいですか？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Mio. Is everything ready?

examples.text: おはようございます！はい、受付はきれいですし、鍵も揃っています。
examples.trans: Good morning! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.

meanings.note: Plain word for one's own aunt when speaking humbly to others.

examples.text: 私のおばはピアノを教えるのが上手でした。
examples.trans: My aunt was wonderful at teaching piano.

examples.text: 週末に大阪のおばの家へ遊びに行きます。
examples.trans: This weekend I am going to visit my aunt's house in Osaka.

meanings.note: Polite term for someone else's aunt, or when addressing one's own aunt.

examples.text: 美央さんのおばさんはパン屋さんですか？
examples.trans: Is your aunt a baker, Mio?

examples.text: 子どものころ、おばさんがよくケーキを焼いてくれました。
examples.trans: When I was a child, my aunt often baked cakes for me.

meanings.note: Affectionate, colloquial term for one's mother, often with さん.

examples.text: おふくろの料理が一番だ。
examples.trans: My mom's cooking is the best.

examples.text: たまにはおふくろに電話しよう。
examples.trans: I should call my mom once in a while.

examples.text: おめえの金がねえと生きてけねえかんな。
examples.trans: Without your money, we can't survive.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

おめでとうございます.lemma: おめでとうございます

meanings.note: Polite set expression of felicitation used for achievements, approvals, birthdays, and New Year greetings.

examples.text: おめでとうございます、隆さん！担当者の方は九号室について何とおっしゃいましたか？
examples.trans: Congratulations, Takashi! What did the clerk say about Room Nine?

examples.text: パン屋さんの三周年、本当におめでとうございます！
examples.trans: Congratulations on the third anniversary of your bakery!

surface: おめでとうございます

meanings.note: Thoughtful Japanese hospitality toward guests.

examples.text: 美央さん、あなたにはおもてなしの才能があります！血圧が救われました！
examples.trans: Mio, you have a true gift for hospitality! My blood pressure is saved!

examples.text: 受付におもてなしがあります。
examples.trans: There is wholehearted hospitality at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Mildly curious exclamation upon noticing something.

examples.text: お持ちしますよ。おや、中に石でも入っていますか？
examples.trans: Allow me to carry it. Goodness, are there stones inside here?

examples.text: おや、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Oh? — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Casual or warm farewell said before going to sleep (polite: おやすみなさい).

examples.text: おやすみ、また明日。
examples.trans: Good night, see you tomorrow.

examples.text: もう遅いからおやすみ。
examples.trans: It's late already, so good night.

examples.text: おやすみ、また明日。
examples.trans: Closing phrase.

examples.text: おやすみ、また明日。
examples.trans: Closing phrase.

meanings.note: Polite bedtime or evening parting phrase.

examples.text: おやすみなさい、美央さん。また明日の朝ごはんの時に。
examples.trans: Good night, Mio. See you at breakfast tomorrow morning.

examples.text: おやすみなさい、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Good night — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.

examples.text: 今、準備しております。
examples.trans: We are preparing right now.

examples.text: お待ちしております。
examples.trans: We are waiting for you.

meanings.note: Read おせわ; core of the standard business and social greeting お世話になっております ('thank you for your ongoing support')
Polite form of 世話(せわ) (care, trouble, everyday assistance)

examples.text: お世話になっております。今ちょうど向かっていますよ。
examples.trans: Thank you for everything. We are on our way right now.

examples.text: いつもお世話になってます。こちら、心ばかりの品です。
examples.trans: Thank you for your continued support. Here is a small token of our appreciation.

related.gloss: to be indebted to, to receive help from

meanings.note: Respectful form of 二人 ('two people / both of you').

examples.text: お二人とも、どうもありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both very much.

examples.text: はい、美央さん。あの青いスーツケースは私のです。お二人に全部本当のことを話します。
examples.trans: Yes, Mio. That blue suitcase is mine. I will tell you both the whole truth.

examples.text: どうぞごゆっくりお過ごしください。中庭はお二人だけの貸し切りです。
examples.trans: Please take all the time you need. The courtyard is all yours.

お二人用.gloss: for the two of you; for two people (polite)

meanings.en: for the two of you; for two people (polite)
meanings.note: Polite compound of お二人 ('two people') + suffix -用 ('for the use of').

examples.text: じゃあ、毎週金曜日の六時に、この中庭のテーブルをお二人用に予約しておくね！
examples.trans: Then I am reserving this courtyard table just for you two every Friday at six!

examples.text: 窓際の静かな席をお二人用に用意しました。
examples.trans: We prepared a quiet table by the window for the two of you.

meanings.note: Mutual pronoun/noun meaning 'both of us / one another'.

examples.text: 四月の喧嘩でお互い間違っていた十九の理由を説明する、五分間のスピーチです。
examples.trans: A five-minute speech explaining nineteen reasons why we were both wrong in April.

examples.text: 受付にお互いがあります。
examples.trans: There is each other at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite form of 仕事 when referring to someone else's work.

examples.text: うちの中庭が、陽翔さんの……お仕事に静かでよかったです。
examples.trans: We are glad our courtyard is peaceful for your... work.

examples.text: 受付にお仕事があります。
examples.trans: There is work at the reception desk.

meanings.note: A second helping, another cup, or a refill of food or drink.

examples.text: ご飯のお代わりをください。
examples.trans: Please give me another bowl of rice.

examples.text: コーヒーのお代わりはいかがですか。
examples.trans: Would you like a refill of coffee?

meanings.note: Polite form of 会計 used at cafés, shops, and market stalls.

examples.text: すみません、お会計をお願いします。
examples.trans: Excuse me, could we have the bill, please?

examples.text: お会計は現金で払ってもいいですか？
examples.trans: May I pay the bill in cash?

meanings.note: Polite noun stem from 似合う ('to suit someone well').

examples.text: よくお似合いですよ、和子さん。
examples.trans: It suits you very well, Kazuko.

examples.text: 受付にお似合いがあります。
examples.trans: There is suiting well at the reception desk.

related.gloss: match up; compare side by side

meanings.note: Polite noun formed from お- + 使う stem; in お使いください it politely invites a guest to use something.

examples.text: 四号室は、和子さんが望むだけいつまでもお使いください。
examples.trans: Please use Room Four for as long as you wish, Kazuko.

examples.text: 雨の日は玄関の大きな傘をどうぞお使いください。
examples.trans: On rainy days, please feel free to use the large umbrellas at the entrance.

examples.text: お供します！はい！
examples.trans: I'll gladly join you! Yes!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite term for someone else's older brother or addressing one's own brother.

examples.text: お兄さんは、ここ大阪に住んでいるんですか？
examples.trans: Does your older brother live here in Osaka?

examples.text: お兄さんというものをよく分かっていらっしゃいますね、健二さん。
examples.trans: You understand older brothers very well, Kenji.

examples.text: 十九の理由ですか！？お兄さんを迎えるんですか、それとも電車の時刻表を読むんですか？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Warm, affectionate family word for an older brother.

examples.text: 大工のおじいさんと孫の兄弟が二人で暮らしていて、お兄ちゃんはピアノ、弟は汽車が大好きだったの！
examples.trans: A master carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the younger brother loved trains!

examples.text: お兄ちゃんは元気で声が大きくて、いつも音階を急いで弾いていたわ。
examples.trans: The older brother was energetic and loud, always rushing through his musical scales.

meanings.note: Rough/intimate second-person pronoun used here by an older brother to his younger brother.

examples.text: やっぱり「祖父の物を預けた誰か」はお前だったんだな、陽翔。
examples.trans: So 'somebody with something of Grandfather's' really was you all along, Haruto.

examples.text: あのハガキの几帳面な四角い字、二秒でお前の字だとわかったよ。
examples.trans: That neat square handwriting on the postcard—I knew it was yours in two seconds.

examples.text: 意地を張った三年間だな……正直に言うと、俺もお前に会いたかったよ。
examples.trans: Three stubborn years... to tell the truth, I missed you too.

meanings.note: Read おちから; honorific form of 力(ちから), frequently used in polite requests such as お力を貸(か)してください (please lend us your support) and お力になる (to be of assistance)

examples.text: 実は困ったことがありまして、お力をお借りできないかと。
examples.trans: We have run into trouble and hoped we might borrow your assistance.

examples.text: 私でよろしければ、いつでもお力になりますよ。
examples.trans: If I can be of service, I will gladly help you anytime.

examples.text: この間お勧めした土地ご購入の件、そろそろいかがです？
examples.trans: How are you feeling about buying that parcel of land I recommended recently?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite form of 名前 used when asking a guest's name.

examples.text: はい、鞄は荷物室で大切に預かっています。お名前を伺えますか？
examples.trans: Yes, we are keeping your bag safely in our luggage room. May I ask your name?

examples.text: 受付にお名前があります。
examples.trans: There is name at the reception desk.

examples.text: お国がわいせつに指定したものは、すべてわいせつになるってことさ。
examples.trans: Everything the state designates as indecent becomes indecent—that's what it means.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: おい、何だこのお姉さん。
examples.trans: Hey, who on earth is this young lady?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お姉ちゃんはかわいいなあ。
examples.trans: Still, the girl herself is awfully cute.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お嬢さん、お荷物が重そうですから二階までお持ちしますよ。
examples.trans: Young lady, your luggage looks heavy, so let me carry it up to the second floor for you.

examples.text: 隣の花屋のお嬢さんが、今朝摘んだばかりの椿を届けてくれた。
examples.trans: The young lady from the flower shop next door delivered camellias picked fresh this morning.

examples.text: ちょっと誰だ、あのお嬢さん？
examples.trans: Hold on — who is that proper young lady over there?

examples.text: もうやめときなって。君みたいな真面目なお嬢さんがいられるとこじゃないのよ。
examples.trans: Forget it while you can — this is no place for an earnest young lady like you.

examples.text: おもしれえじゃねえか、お宅の監督。
examples.trans: Your director is hilarious, isn't he!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Read おきゃく; polite form of 客(きゃく), usually followed by さん or 様(さま) in conversation
Someone visiting a home, office, or venue

examples.text: 会社のほうは何とかやってますが、お客さん減っちゃって。
examples.trans: We're managing to keep the company running somehow, though we've lost customers.

examples.text: ご来訪のお客様がお待ちですが。
examples.trans: Your visiting guest is waiting for you, sir.

meanings.note: Standard respectful term for inn guests and customers.

examples.text: 今日来る四号室のお客さまは一週間泊まります。完璧にしましょう！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week. Let's make everything perfect!

examples.text: お腹を空かせた八人のお客さまが、七時半に階段を下りて来ますよ！
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests will come down the stairs at seven thirty!

examples.text: 八時ちょうどです！お客さまが着きました！
examples.trans: Eight o'clock on the dot! Our guest has arrived!

meanings.note: Warm everyday polite word for a guest or customer.

examples.text: ああ、部屋は八室、真鍮の鍵も八つだ。今日は四号室にお客さんが来る。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 時計は七時二十九分だ。お客さんたちが階段を下りて来るぞ。
examples.trans: My watch says seven twenty-nine. The guests are coming down the stairs.

meanings.note: High-respect term for a guest at an inn, café patron, or house visitor; more formal than お客さん.

examples.text: 深呼吸して……笑顔で……お客様をお迎えに行きましょう！
examples.trans: Deep breath... smile... let us go welcome our guest!

examples.text: 四号室のお客様に、温かい緑茶とタオルをお持ちしました。
examples.trans: I brought hot green tea and towels to the guest in Room Four.

meanings.note: Read おまわりさん; friendly, everyday term for a uniformed police officer (from 巡(まわ)る, 'to patrol'), commonly used when addressing an officer directly

examples.text: もっとちゃんと見てください、お巡りさん。
examples.trans: Please take a closer look, Officer.

examples.text: 道に迷ったら、あそこのお巡りさんに聞いてみよう。
examples.trans: If we get lost, let's ask the police officer over there.

お布施.gloss: temple offering, donation to Buddhist clergy

examples.text: それとね、これは別で一億円。これはお布施です。
examples.trans: And separately, here is another 100 million yen. Consider this a temple donation.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Warm standard greeting welcoming family, guests, or regulars back to a home or inn.

examples.text: こんばんは、皆さん。九号室の金曜日のお茶会へ、お帰りなさい。
examples.trans: Good evening, everyone, and welcome back to Friday tea in Room Nine.

examples.text: お帰りなさい！温かいお風呂とお茶が用意できていますよ。
examples.trans: Welcome back! A warm bath and hot tea are ready for you.

meanings.note: Polite everyday form of 店 ('shop').

examples.text: 見事な速さです！お店の人から領収書をもらいましたか？
examples.trans: Impressive speed! Did you get a receipt from the shopkeeper?

examples.text: お店の外に大きな看板はありますか？
examples.trans: Is there a big sign outside the shop?

meanings.note: Humble noun form of 待たせる, used in apologies like お待たせしました.

examples.text: 大変お待たせいたしました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for waiting.

examples.text: お待たせしてすみません。
examples.trans: Sorry to keep you waiting.

meanings.note: Read おまち; polite stem of 待(ま)つ used in humble expressions (お待ちしております, 'we have been awaiting you') and honorific expressions (お待ちです / お待ちください)

examples.text: 会長、お待ちしておりました。
examples.trans: Chairman, we have been waiting for you.

examples.text: ご来訪のお客様がお待ちですが。
examples.trans: Your visiting guest is waiting for you, sir.

meanings.note: Polite/honorific form of 忙しい with prefix お.

examples.text: お忙しいところすみません。
examples.trans: Sorry to bother you while you're busy.

examples.text: 毎日お忙しいですか。
examples.trans: Are you busy every day?

お持ちする.gloss: to humbly bring; to carry (for someone)

meanings.en: to humbly bring; to carry (for someone)
meanings.note: Humble (kenjōgo) pattern お + 持ち + する used when bringing tea, menus, or luggage to guests.

examples.text: ようこそ、皆さん、いらっしゃいませ！熱いミントティーをすぐお持ちします！
examples.trans: Welcome, everyone, come right in! I will bring hot mint tea right out!

examples.text: お荷物は私が二階の部屋までお持ちしますね。
examples.trans: I will carry your luggage up to the second-floor room for you.

meanings.note: Matching clothes, accessories, or items worn or possessed by two or more people.

examples.text: 友達とお揃いのTシャツを買った。
examples.trans: I bought matching T-shirts with my friend.

examples.text: カップルでお揃いの時計をつけている。
examples.trans: The couple is wearing matching watches.

meanings.note: Polite everyday word for midday or lunch.

examples.text: あと数分待ちましょう、陽翔さん。お昼の町の道路はいつも混んでいますから。
examples.trans: Let's wait a few more minutes, Haruto. City roads at lunchtime are always crowded.

examples.text: 受付にお昼があります。
examples.trans: There is noon at the reception desk.

お楽しみ.gloss: fun, enjoyment, something to look forward to

meanings.en: fun, enjoyment, something to look forward to
meanings.note: Something fun or enjoyable to look forward to.

examples.text: 週末のお楽しみとして取っておく。
examples.trans: I'm saving it as a treat for the weekend.

examples.text: 次回の放送をお楽しみに！
examples.trans: Look forward to the next broadcast!

meanings.note: Read おかあさん; standard polite word used both to address one's own mother directly and to refer respectfully to someone else's mother

examples.text: お母さん、私ね、いつかイタリアに留学したいの。
examples.trans: Mother, listen—someday I want to study abroad in Italy.

examples.text: もうお母さんに全部言ってきちゃった。
examples.trans: I already went and told Mom everything.

meanings.note: Used in お気になさらないでください ('please do not worry about it').

examples.text: いいえ、お気になさらないでください！陽翔さまですね。
examples.trans: Not at all, please do not worry! You must be Haruto.

examples.text: 受付にお気があります。
examples.trans: There is mind at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Something one is especially fond of.

examples.text: ワンピースと楽譜と、お気に入りのティーカップだけですわ！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 受付にお気に入りがあります。
examples.trans: There is favorite at the reception desk.

examples.text: ありがとうございます、お気遣いいただいて。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your kind consideration.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite everyday word for drinking water.

examples.text: はい、冷たいお水を一口飲んでください、陽翔さん。その紙は何ですか？
examples.trans: Here, drink a sip of cool water, Haruto. What is on that paper?

examples.text: 受付にお水があります。
examples.trans: There is water at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Standard everyday word for hot water in taps, baths, or kettles.

examples.text: 美央ちゃん、急須にお湯を注いで！みんな来たよ！
examples.trans: Mio, pour the hot water into the teapot! Here comes everyone!

examples.text: 先週、新しい電球に替えたし、石鹸もお湯もばっちりだ。
examples.trans: I put in a new lightbulb last week, and soap and hot water are all set.

examples.text: はい！隅のお湯のパイプから聞こえたみたいです。
examples.trans: Yes! It sounded like it came from the hot-water pipe in the corner.

examples.text: お玉でスープをよそってください。
examples.trans: Please serve the soup with a ladle.

examples.text: 新しいお玉を買わないと。
examples.trans: I need to buy a new ladle.

お疲れさま.gloss: thank you for your hard work, good job

meanings.en: thank you for your hard work, good job, see you later
meanings.note: Read おつかれさま (kanji: お疲れ様); ubiquitous workplace and on-set greeting acknowledging coworkers' effort during or at the end of a workday

examples.text: 皆さん、今日はお疲れさまでした。乾杯！
examples.trans: Everyone, thank you for your hard work today. Cheers!

examples.text: 遅くまで撮影お疲れさま。気をつけて帰ってね。
examples.trans: Good job filming so late. Get home safe.

related.gloss: thank you for your trouble (to subordinates/couriers)

examples.text: お前らはもうこれ以上でかくなんねえから、終わりってことで。お疲れさん。
examples.trans: You guys aren't getting any bigger than this, so it's curtains for you. Good work.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Everyday polite form of 皿 ('plate, dish') with beautifying prefix お-.

examples.text: 二人とも、きれいなお皿は五分置いておいて、ドアのそばで聴きましょう！
examples.trans: Both of you, leave the clean plates for five minutes and let us listen by the door!

examples.text: 焼きたてのレモンタルトを白いお皿に並べました。
examples.trans: We arranged the freshly baked lemon tarts on white plates.

meanings.note: Written or spoken notification.

examples.text: どうせ通りの雨戸を塗り替えるとか、退屈なお知らせだよ。
examples.trans: It is probably some boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

examples.text: 「物件売却のお知らせ。中庭八番館を、商業オフィス用として売却いたします。」
examples.trans: 'Notice of Property Sale: Number Eight Courtyard Building is offered for commercial office sale.'

examples.text: 待ってください……このお知らせの裏に、折りたたまれた二枚目の紙が留めてあります……
examples.trans: Hold on... clipped to the back of this notice is a folded second page...

meanings.note: Polite term for someone a guest knows.

examples.text: 本当ですか？大阪にお知り合いがいるんですか？
examples.trans: Really? Do you know someone here in Osaka?

examples.text: 受付にお知り合いがあります。
examples.trans: There is acquaintance at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Expression of thanks or appreciation.

examples.text: いいえ、どちらもありません！静かな天井の梁を気に入って、お礼を言ってくれました。
examples.trans: Neither! He loved the quiet ceiling beams and thanked us.

examples.text: 受付にお礼があります。
examples.trans: There is thanks at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Read おいのり; polite form of 祈(いの)り, used with する to mean 'to pray' or 'to offer a prayer'

examples.text: 恵美さん、ちゃんとお祈りはしてきた？
examples.trans: Emi, did you make sure to say your prayers?

examples.text: 撮影が無事に終わるようにお祈りしています。
examples.trans: I am praying that the shoot wraps up safely.

examples.text: 今日の一番の目的はお祝いだ。
examples.trans: Tonight's main purpose is a celebration.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: A traditional festival, often associated with a Shinto shrine, featuring parades, stalls, and celebrations.

examples.text: 夏はお祭りに出かけて屋台を楽しむ。
examples.trans: In the summer, we go out to festivals and enjoy the food stalls.

examples.text: 町全体がお祭り騒ぎだ。
examples.trans: The whole town is in a festive mood.

examples.text: お紅茶飲みますか？
examples.trans: Would you care for some black tea?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in お腹が空く ('to get hungry').

examples.text: お腹を空かせた八人のお客さまが、七時半に階段を下りて来ますよ！
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests will come down the stairs at seven thirty!

examples.text: 受付にお腹があります。
examples.trans: There is stomach at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite everyday word for Japanese tea.

examples.text: ルールその一。まず温かいお茶を飲んで、それからベルに出ること。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: 「座って。温かいお茶と、金曜日のレモンケーキがあるよ。」
examples.trans: 'Sit down. There is hot tea and Friday lemon cake.'

examples.text: お茶とレモンケーキ！美央さんは、緊張する弟のための学校を開くべきですよ。
examples.trans: Tea and lemon cake! Mio, you ought to open a school for nervous younger brothers.

meanings.note: Polite prefix お- + 茶会 (ちゃかい, 'tea gathering').

examples.text: 金曜日の六時からピアノのお茶会を開きます。
examples.trans: We hold a piano tea gathering starting at six on Fridays.

examples.text: ご近所の方を小さなお茶会に招待しました。
examples.trans: We invited the neighbours to a small tea gathering.

examples.text: 最近はお茶農家も競争が厳しいみたいでね。
examples.trans: Lately it seems competition is fierce even for tea farmers.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite noun form of 薦める; お薦めする means 'to recommend'.

examples.text: 今日のお薦めは何ですか。
examples.trans: What is today's recommendation?

examples.text: この本をお薦めします。
examples.trans: I recommend this book.

meanings.note: Respectful way to refer to a guest's understanding words.

examples.text: 優しいお言葉をありがとうございます！すぐ健二さんが地下室を見ますね。
examples.trans: Thank you for being so understanding! Kenji will check the basement right away.

examples.text: 受付にお言葉があります。
examples.trans: There is kind words at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite noun for an apology or amends.

examples.text: そうだ、部屋が変わるお詫びに、どんな割引をしましょうか？
examples.trans: Wait—to apologise for changing rooms, what discount should we offer?

examples.text: あの、上へご案内する前に、正直にお詫びしたいことがあります。
examples.trans: Um, before showing you upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

examples.text: 手違いのお詫びに、今夜は半額で、朝ごはんも付いています。
examples.trans: As an apology for our mix-up, tonight is half price with breakfast included.

meanings.note: Polite nominalized form of 誘う ('to invite'); with する (お誘いする) it forms humble 'to invite an honored person'.

examples.text: 今週の金曜日、六時のグランドオープンにお誘いしましたか！？
examples.trans: Did you invite him to our grand opening this Friday at six o'clock?!

examples.text: 素敵なお茶会のお誘いをいただき、ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the lovely tea-party invitation.

examples.text: 昨日ね、お買い物してたら昔の同僚とたまたま会ったんです。
examples.trans: Yesterday while I was out shopping, I bumped into an old coworker by chance.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 皆さま、札幌ツアーへようこそお越しくださいました。
examples.trans: Everyone, welcome aboard the Sapporo tour.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite noun for bowing in greeting, gratitude, or after a performance (お辞儀をする = 'to bow').

examples.text: 胸を張ってお辞儀をして、笑顔でメニュー表を配ってください、隆さん！
examples.trans: Stand proud, take a bow, and hand out the menu cards with a smile, Takashi!

examples.text: 隆さんもどうぞお辞儀をしてください。叔母様の金曜日の部屋がまた生き返りましたよ。
examples.trans: Take a bow yourself, Takashi—your aunt's Friday room has come back to life.

meanings.note: Going out to meet and welcome someone.

examples.text: 任せてください。下へ行って、温かくお迎えしましょう。
examples.trans: Leave it to me. Let's go downstairs and welcome him warmly.

examples.text: 受付にお迎えがあります。
examples.trans: There is welcoming at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Used in ごゆっくりお過ごしください ('please enjoy a relaxing stay').

examples.text: はい、伝えます！どうぞごゆっくりお過ごしください。
examples.trans: I certainly will! Please enjoy a relaxing morning.

examples.text: どうぞごゆっくりお過ごしください。中庭はお二人だけの貸し切りです。
examples.trans: Please take all the time you need. The courtyard is all yours.

meanings.note: Polite expression when interrupting or visiting someone's room.

examples.text: すみません、陽翔さん。夜分にお邪魔して申し訳ありません。
examples.trans: Excuse me, Haruto. Sorry to disturb you so late in the evening.

examples.text: 受付にお邪魔があります。
examples.trans: There is disturbing at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite form of 部屋 used with inn guests.

examples.text: 大阪の最初の夜に、お部屋で寂しく過ごすなんて駄目ですよ！
examples.trans: You cannot spend your first evening in Osaka feeling lonely upstairs!

examples.text: 受付にお部屋があります。
examples.trans: There is room at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite everyday form of 酢 ('vinegar') with prefix お-.

examples.text: ぬるま湯にお酢を一滴入れるとガラスがきれいになります。
examples.trans: Adding a drop of vinegar to warm water makes glass sparkle.

examples.text: サラダに少しだけお酢をかけました。
examples.trans: I drizzled just a touch of vinegar over the salad.

meanings.note: Polite お + 金 ('gold, money'); the everyday word for money.

examples.text: 昔、雨の春に、ガラスの屋根から水がもれました。直すお金がなかったんです。
examples.trans: One rainy spring the glass roof leaked. There was no money to fix it.

examples.text: 財布にお金があまりありません。
examples.trans: I don't have much money in my wallet.

examples.text: 正直、撮影も、ただのお金目当てだったのに、うれしいんだ。
examples.trans: Honestly, I only came to the shoot for the money, yet I feel so happy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Warm, polite word for next-door neighbors.

examples.text: 素敵なお隣さんと、温かいパンと、開かれた門に乾杯！
examples.trans: To wonderful neighbours, warm bread, and an open gate—cheers!

examples.text: 受付にお隣さんがあります。
examples.trans: There is neighbor at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Polite form of 電話.

examples.text: あ、もしもし！濃い青いスーツケースの件でお電話ですか？
examples.trans: Oh, hello! Are you calling about the dark-blue suitcase?

examples.text: 受付にお電話があります。
examples.trans: There is phone call at the reception desk.

examples.text: 税金対策とか言って、お預けのギャラ三千万。
examples.trans: Calling it tax planning, he kept thirty million yen of my pay on deposit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used with します or です to make polite requests.

examples.text: まだですか？では宿の電話番号と住所をお願いします。ありがとうございます！
examples.trans: Not yet? Then please take our inn's phone number and address. Thank you!

examples.text: 留守をお願いします！もう行って来ます！
examples.trans: Hold the fort! I am heading out right now!

examples.text: 砂糖なしの紅茶をお願いします。それと温かいパンを一切れ。
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: カット！もう一度お願いしまーす。
examples.trans: Cut! Let's take it one more time, please.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standard everyday word for a bath or bathroom.

examples.text: 暖かい毛布がありますし、今夜のお風呂はもう済ませたので大丈夫ですよ。
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, and I already washed up tonight, so I am fine.

examples.text: 受付にお風呂があります。
examples.trans: There is bath at the reception desk.

meanings.note: At the end of a sentence, turns it into a question; between nouns, means 'or'.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 初日はいつも早く歩きます。パソコンはどこですか？
examples.trans: I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 紙の帳面ですか？本当に？
examples.trans: A paper ledger? Really?

meanings.note: A sentence-ending particle used to ask a question softly or casually.

examples.text: これでいいのかい？
examples.trans: Is this alright?

examples.text: 疲れているのかい？
examples.trans: Are you tired?

meanings.note: Native Japanese anatomical noun (踵).

examples.text: かかとの下に柔らかい枕を二つ置きました。
examples.trans: He placed two soft pillows under her heel.

examples.text: 新しい靴のかかとが少し固いです。
examples.trans: The heel of my new shoes is a bit stiff.

meanings.note: With 鍵が means 'be locked'; with 時間が means 'take time'.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 古いレンガの建物は、普通なら上の階までお湯が来るのに時間がかかりますよね。
examples.trans: Old brick buildings usually take a long time for hot water to reach the top floor.

examples.text: おじいさんが、粉砂糖のかかった温かいレモンケーキを切ってくれたの！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar!

examples.text: 長えかくれんぼしやがって。協力ありがとさん。
examples.trans: Quite a long game of hide-and-seek you played. Thanks for the cooperation.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan verb (かぐ -> かぎます -> かがない -> かいだ -> かいで).

examples.text: 焼きたてのパンのにおいをかいでみてください。
examples.trans: Try smelling the aroma of freshly baked bread.

examples.text: 庭のバラの花をかぐと、春の気分になります。
examples.trans: Smelling the roses in the garden puts me in a spring mood.

かける.gloss: put on (glasses); lock; phone; call out

meanings.en: put on (glasses); lock; phone; call out
meanings.note: Versatile transitive verb used with 眼鏡を, 鍵を, 電話を, and 声を.

examples.text: なんと大変な間違いでしょう！眼鏡をかけて名札を見ますね。
examples.trans: What a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and read the tag.

examples.text: 今かけます……もしもし？青いスーツケースの取り違えは届いていますか？
examples.trans: Dialling now... Hello? Has anyone reported a swapped blue suitcase?

examples.text: もう一つの青いスーツケースは、荷物室にしっかり鍵をかけておきました。
examples.trans: I locked the other blue suitcase safely inside our luggage room.

examples.text: そうか。またすぐかけ直す。
examples.trans: I see. I'll call you right back.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Woven basket for bread or fruit.

examples.text: かごの中に黄色いレモンが六個あるの！このキッチンは今日のためにあったんだよ！
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now! This kitchen was waiting for today!

examples.text: 受付にかごがあります。
examples.trans: There is basket at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Gentle sentence-ending question particle.

examples.text: 明るい日差しの中で、もう一度あの紙の名札を見てもいいかしら？
examples.trans: May I look at that paper tag once more here in the bright sunlight?

examples.text: 受付で「かしら」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'かしら' (I wonder).

meanings.note: Slight

examples.text: かすかな音が聞こえる。
examples.trans: I hear a faint sound.

examples.text: 記憶がかすかだ。
examples.trans: The memory is dim.

examples.text: モヤモヤした時は安酒かっ食らうのが一番だな。
examples.trans: When your head feels murky, gulping cheap booze is the best cure.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Casual sentence-final particle expressing a soft guess.

examples.text: 小さい箱が三つだけですよ！たぶん四つかな！
examples.trans: Only three small boxes! Maybe four!

examples.text: 受付で「かな」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'かな' (I wonder).

かぶる.gloss: to put on; to wear (on the head)

meanings.en: to put on; to wear (on the head)
meanings.note: Godan verb (被る) specifically used for hats, helmets, hoods, or pulling blankets over the head.

examples.text: 灰色の帽子をかぶった年配の男性が、すぐ外の歩道で立ち止まりました。
examples.trans: An older gentleman with a grey hat stopped right outside on the pavement.

examples.text: 日差しが強い日は、麦わら帽子をかぶって中庭を掃除します。
examples.trans: On days with strong sunlight, I wear a straw hat to sweep the courtyard.

meanings.note: Combines with しれません to express possibility ('might have').

examples.text: 見てください、もう十二時四分です。私のハガキをごみ箱に捨てたのかもしれません。
examples.trans: Look, it is already four minutes past twelve. Maybe he tossed my postcard in the bin.

examples.text: 受付で「かも」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'かも' (maybe).

meanings.note: After a noun, marks starting time/place ('from'); after a clause, gives a reason ('because').

examples.text: おはよう。いや、まず取っ手を上げて、それから押すんだ。
examples.trans: Morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: 紙なら、停電になっても使えるからね。
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: 由香はこの通りのみんなと昔からの友達みたいに話すんだ。
examples.trans: Yuka talks with everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Mimetic adverb for something thoroughly dry and light.

examples.text: 雨戸の木は廊下に入れたのでからからに乾いています。
examples.trans: Because we brought the shutter wood into the hall, it is bone-dry.

examples.text: 晴れた風で洗濯物がからからに乾きました。
examples.trans: The laundry dried crisp and bone-dry in the sunny breeze.

meanings.note: Everyday i-adjective for charming objects, designs, or small things.

examples.text: この青いマグカップはとてもかわいいですね。
examples.trans: This blue mug is so cute, isn't it?

examples.text: 市場でかわいい花の鉢を見つけました。
examples.trans: I found a cute flower pot at the market.

examples.text: おめえの金がねえと生きてけねえかんな。
examples.trans: Without your money, we can't survive.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the grammatical subject (especially new info or with ある/いる/わかる); after a clause, means 'but'.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: なるほど！それで、これが鍵ですか？
examples.trans: Fair enough! And are these the keys?

meanings.note: Nominalized stem of がたつく ('to rattle, wobble').

examples.text: ピンを直したら木のがたつきがゼロになりました。
examples.trans: Once the pin was fixed, there was zero rattle in the wood.

examples.text: 古いテーブルの脚のがたつきを直しました。
examples.trans: We fixed the wobble in the legs of the old table.

examples.text: がっかりさせないでよって。
examples.trans: And she says don't disappoint her.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

がる.gloss: to show signs of; (in やがる) contemptuous verb suffix

meanings.en: (in ～やがる) to have the nerve to, to do (with contempt)
meanings.note: Part of the rough auxiliary verb suffix ～やがる (te-form ～やがって), attached to a verb stem to express anger, disdain, or tough camaraderie toward someone's action

meanings.en: to show signs of feeling, to act as if
meanings.note: Godan auxiliary suffix attached to adjective stems (e.g., 怖(こわ)がる, 強(つよ)がる) to describe outward displays of emotion or desire

examples.text: 長えかくれんぼしやがって。協力ありがとさん。
examples.trans: Quite a long game of hide-and-seek you played. Thanks for the cooperation.

examples.text: てめえら裏切りやがってよ！
examples.trans: You bastards betrayed us!

examples.text: 部屋をきちんと片付けてください。
examples.trans: Please tidy up the room properly.

examples.text: 約束はきちんと守ります。
examples.trans: I will accurately keep my promises.
