meanings.note: This is used as a adj meaning neat.

cells: きちんとしたじゃない

examples.text: それはとてもきちんとしたです。
examples.trans: It is very neat.

examples.text: もっときちんとしたしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more neat.

meanings.note: Precisely; exactly; without any deviation in time or amount.

examples.text: 会議は3時きっかりに始まった。
examples.trans: The meeting started exactly at 3 o'clock.

examples.text: きっかり1万円を支払った。
examples.trans: I paid exactly 10,000 yen.

examples.text: お前らみたいな凶悪な前科もんは、きっちり監視しとかないと。
examples.trans: We have to keep a tight watch on vicious ex-convicts like you guys.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses confident expectation.

examples.text: 持ち主の人も、きっとすぐ探しに来ますよ。
examples.trans: Whoever owns it will surely come looking for it soon.

examples.text: 一週間も青いスーツケースを守ったんですよ？きっと力になってくれます！
examples.trans: After we guarded his blue suitcase all week? He will gladly lend a hand!

meanings.note: This is used as a adj meaning tight.

examples.text: それはとてもきついです。
examples.trans: It is very tight.

examples.text: もっときついしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more tight.

meanings.note: A golden-brown color, typically describing perfectly baked or fried food.

examples.text: パンがきつね色に焼けた。
examples.trans: The bread baked to a golden brown.

examples.text: 玉ねぎをきつね色になるまで炒める。
examples.trans: Sauté the onions until they are golden brown.

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken contraction of the conditional ending ～ければ or ～けば (e.g., やっておけば → やっときゃ, 任(まか)しておけば → 任しときゃ)
In ～なきゃ (short for ～なければ), expresses obligation when the final ならない or いけない is dropped

examples.text: 大ヒットとまではいかなくても、これやっときゃ間違いねえってヤツ。
examples.trans: Even if it won't be a mega-hit, it's a surefire bet if you stick to it.

examples.text: なくなるんじゃねえの、十年後ぐらいには。俺に任しときゃな、もっと早かったのによ。
examples.trans: Sure, they'll probably vanish—in ten years or so. If they'd left it to me, I'd have finished them faster.

きる.gloss: to do completely, to finish; to cut

meanings.en: to do completely, to finish doing to the end
meanings.note: Godan auxiliary verb (kanji: 切る) attached to a verb stem (e.g., 撮(と)りきる 'to finish filming completely', やりきる 'to carry through to the end')

meanings.en: to cut, to sever, to turn off
meanings.note: Standalone verb 切(き)る

examples.text: その代わり、今日中に必ず撮りきってください。
examples.trans: In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.

examples.text: この二十分の間にすべてを撮りきって逃げる！
examples.trans: Within those twenty minutes, we shoot everything and bolt!

related.gloss: to see through to the end, to accomplish completely
to use up completely, to exhaust

meanings.note: Common na-adjective (きれいな before a noun) for both cleanliness and beauty.

examples.text: おはようございます！はい、受付はきれいですし、鍵も揃っています。
examples.trans: Good morning! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.

examples.text: 落ち着いてよ、隆さん。部屋はきれいだし、タオルも新しい。
examples.trans: Relax, Takashi. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 隆さん、きれいな布と冷たい水をお持ちしました。
examples.trans: Takashi, I brought a clean cloth and cold water.

meanings.note: This is used as a adj meaning cleanly.

examples.text: それはとてもきれいだです。
examples.trans: It is very cleanly.

examples.text: もっときれいだしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more cleanly.

ぎ.gloss: voiced verb-stem syllable (-gi); bound morpheme gi

examples.text: 監督、時間です。急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.

examples.text: いらねえよ！嫌いなんだようなぎはよ。
examples.trans: I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

く.gloss: adverbial adjective suffix; colloquial phonetic contraction

meanings.note: Inflectional ending replacing ～い on i-adjectives to form adverbs or link clauses (e.g., 大(おお)きく 'greatly/big', 早(はや)く 'quickly')

meanings.en: colloquial phonetic element in contracted speech
meanings.note: Appears in rough or emphatic spoken contractions where adjacent syllables geminate (such as おっきい for 大きい or verb stems before から)

examples.text: まあまあ、細かいことは気にすんなよ。ここのおっきいのが後藤だ。
examples.trans: Now, now, don't sweat the small details! The big guy here is Goto.

examples.text: 真由美も大輔も私が育てっから。このバカが！
examples.trans: I'll raise Mayumi and Daisuke myself, you fool!

meanings.en: smelling of, reeking of, looking suspiciously like
meanings.note: i-adjective suffix (kanji: 臭い) attached to nouns to mean 'suspiciously like' or 'having the air of' (e.g., ウソくさい 'phony/fake', 水(みず)くさい 'distant/reserved between close friends')
Standalone adjective 臭(くさ)い describing an unpleasant odor

examples.text: 何だ、このウソくさいのは。
examples.trans: What is this phony-looking video?

examples.text: 水くさいこと言うなよ。昔から浮いたり沈んだりをさらし合える仲だろ。
examples.trans: Don't talk like a stranger. You and I have seen each other's highs and lows since way back.

examples.text: 何、もうくじけちゃったの？そんなんじゃお金集まんないよ。
examples.trans: What, discouraged already? We won't raise money like that.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前、組の上がりくすねてんだろ。謝れよ。
examples.trans: You have been skimming money from the gang's take, haven't you. Apologize.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In 〜くせに, playfully teases someone ('even though you actually...').

examples.text: ちょっと聞いてよ！本当は健二さんが私たちの二倍気になっているくせに！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Kenji is actually twice as curious as we are!

examples.text: あら、聞いた？昨日はボイラーを直して、今日は兄弟の仲を直すくせに！
examples.trans: Oh, hear that? Yesterday you fixed the boiler, and today you are fixing two brothers!

meanings.note: Conjunction expressing annoyance or reproach toward someone's behavior.

examples.text: 知らないくせに偉そうに言うな。
examples.trans: Don't talk big even though you don't know.

examples.text: 暇なくせに手伝ってくれない。
examples.trans: Even though he's free, he won't help.

meanings.note: Being completely exhausted or physically worn out.

examples.text: 一日中働いてもうくたくただ。
examples.trans: I'm completely worn out after working all day.

examples.text: くたくたになるまで走った。
examples.trans: I ran until I was dead tired.

examples.text: 恐れ入りますが、こちらの宿帳にお名前をご記入ください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, could you please write your name here in this guest register?

examples.text: 足元が滑りやすくなっておりますので、どうぞお気をつけください。
examples.trans: The footing is slippery, so please watch your step.

meanings.note: Its imperative ください after a te-form verb is the standard 'please do'.

examples.text: わかりました。大事なことを全部教えてください。
examples.trans: Got it. Please tell me everything I need to know.

examples.text: 誰にも言わないでくださいね！さあ、ベルが鳴ったら明るい笑顔ですよ。
examples.trans: Please do not tell anyone! Now, smile brightly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 美央さん、このスーツケースの中を見てください！私の鞄じゃありません！
examples.trans: Mio, please look inside this suitcase! It is not my bag!

くだる.gloss: to descend; (in くだらない) trivial, nonsense

meanings.en: (in negative くだらない / くだらん) trivial, foolish, nonsense, worthless
meanings.note: Overwhelmingly used in the negative form くだらない (or rough くだらん) to dismiss something as pointless, stupid, or beneath consideration

meanings.en: to descend, to go down, to be handed down
meanings.note: Godan verb 下(くだ)る; to go down from a height or from the capital, or for a judgment/order to be issued

examples.text: くだらんことをするな。金は？
examples.trans: Cut out the nonsense. Where's the money?

examples.text: そんなくだらない理由で俺を閉め出すのか？
examples.trans: You are shutting me out over a ridiculous reason like that?

meanings.note: Follows a number or quantity to mean 'approximately'.

examples.text: 静かで丁寧な声で、三十五歳くらいです。怒ってはいなくて、緊張していました。
examples.trans: A quiet, polite voice, around thirty-five. He was not angry, just nervous.

examples.text: 受付で「くらい」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'くらい' (about).

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: すぐ戻ってきます。
examples.trans: I will come right back.

meanings.note: The nut and the tree; くるみの木 is walnut wood.

examples.text: アップライトピアノ！本物のくるみの木のピアノです！
examples.trans: An upright piano! A real walnut piano!

examples.text: このパンにはくるみが入っています。
examples.trans: There are walnuts in this bread.

examples.text: 村西さん、くれぐれもよろしくお願いします。
examples.trans: Mr. Muranishi, please take every care with this.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: After a te-form verb, shows someone kindly doing an action for the speaker's side.

examples.text: 雨の中へ追い返さず、正直に話してくれてありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both for speaking honestly instead of sending me back into the rain.

examples.text: いいえ、どちらもありません！静かな天井の梁を気に入って、お礼を言ってくれました。
examples.trans: Neither! He loved the quiet ceiling beams and thanked us.

examples.text: 上へ行く前に、野菜スープも最後の一滴まで飲んでくれたよ。
examples.trans: Before going upstairs, he even finished the vegetable soup to the very last drop.

meanings.note: Friendly title suffix often used for younger men, boys, or former students.

examples.text: まあ、なんてこと……その目！階段の三段目の、小さな陽翔くん！？
examples.trans: Goodness gracious... those eyes! Little Haruto from the third step?!

examples.text: よく顔を見せてちょうだい、陽翔くん！ピアノよりずっと背が高くなったわね！
examples.trans: Let me get a proper look at you, Haruto! You grew much taller than the piano!

examples.text: 大輝くんは帰ったりしませんよ。いつも五秒だけ強がって、すぐ優しくなったもの。
examples.trans: Daiki will not walk away. He always acted tough for five seconds and softened right away.

examples.text: しかたないだろ！こんな状況ですぐに対応できるはずがない。
examples.trans: Give them a break! Nobody can adjust right away in a situation like this.

examples.text: 雨が降る前に、機材を片づけて急ぐぞ。
examples.trans: Let's pack up the gear and hurry before it starts raining.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic adverb paired with 眠る ('sleep soundly').

examples.text: おかげさまで、今夜はぐっすり眠れそうです。
examples.trans: Thanks to your kindness, I think I will sleep soundly tonight.

examples.text: ぐっすりお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (soundly).

meanings.note: Attaches to quantities or interrogatives (どのぐらい, 何本ぐらい) to indicate approximation.

examples.text: 一日何本ぐらい売れる？
examples.trans: About how many sell in a day?

examples.text: 十分ぐらい待ちました。
examples.trans: I waited about ten minutes.

examples.text: 椅子のぐらつきを直した。
examples.trans: I fixed the wobble of the chair.

examples.text: 歯のぐらつきが気になる。
examples.trans: I'm worried about the looseness of my tooth.

meanings.note: Noun suffix written 気(け) (e.g., 人気(ひとけ) 'sign of life', 火気(かけ)/火の気 'trace of fire'); also appears as a syllable inside common words like 訳(わけ) and 空(あ)ける
Colloquial sentence-final particle (often っけ) used when trying to recall a fact or asking for confirmation

examples.text: 何日か空けるかもしれない。
examples.trans: I might be away for a few days.

examples.text: 君はロンリーな未亡人です。さみしい二人が出会うわけですよ。
examples.trans: In this story you are a lonely widow, and two lonely souls cross paths.

related.gloss: to vacate, to leave empty, to open

meanings.note: Conversational clause connector softening a contrast or trailing off politely.

examples.text: 二十五年前、この近くでピアノを教えていたの。もう遠い昔だけど。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano near here, though that was long ago.

examples.text: 一番上の棚にあった金色の包みですけど。どうして？
examples.trans: The gold wrapper on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Zelkova-tree lane in Osaka where the story's old family house stood.

examples.text: 和子さん、すごく驚いていますね！「けやき通り十二番地」をご存じなんですか？
examples.trans: Kazuko, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve, Keyaki Lane?

examples.text: 和子さん、けやき通りの兄弟のことをもっと教えてください！
examples.trans: Kazuko, please tell me more about the brothers on Keyaki Lane!

meanings.note: Softer, slightly more conversational variant of けれども.

examples.text: 外は寒いけれど、サンルームの中は暖かいです。
examples.trans: It is cold outside, though inside the sunroom it is warm.

examples.text: 少し大変ですけれど、みんなでやれば終わりますよ。
examples.trans: It's a bit of work, though if we do it together we'll finish.

examples.text: 日本のポルノ業界をけん引する作品を中心に放送してまいります。
examples.trans: We will broadcast programming centered on works that lead Japan's adult video industry.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: seeming, having an air of, looking as if
meanings.note: Suffix written 気(げ) attached to adjective or verb stems to form na-adjectives/nouns describing outward appearance (e.g., 寂(さび)しげ 'looking lonely', 意味(いみ)ありげ 'meaningful/suggestive')

meanings.en: mood, humor; (in すっげえ) colloquial phonetic shift
meanings.note: Appears in 機嫌(きげん) ('mood', as in ごきげんよう) and in rough spoken contractions like すっげえ (from すごい 'amazing/wild')

examples.text: すっげえ食い合わせだな。腹に入れば同じだよ。
examples.trans: What a wild food combination — well, it all goes to the same stomach.

examples.text: 皆様こんにちは、ごきげんよう。黒木香でございます。
examples.trans: Good afternoon, everyone. I am Kaoru Kuroki.

examples.text: 指切りげんまん、ウソついたら針千本のーます。指切った。
examples.trans: Pinky promise sealed—if I tell a lie, I'll swallow a thousand needles!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

こう.gloss: like this, in this way, so

meanings.en: like this, in this way, thus
meanings.note: Proximal manner adverb (part of the こう・そう・ああ・どう demonstratives) pointing to a state or action close to the speaker; frequently combined with する as こうする ('to do like this')

examples.text: このほうが落ち着くの。こうしてほしかった。
examples.trans: Holding me tight like this calms me down — this is what I wanted all along.

examples.text: いつもこうなの？たまにはゆっくり休みなよ。
examples.trans: Is it always like this? You should take a proper rest once in a while.

こういう.gloss: this kind of, like this, such

meanings.en: this kind of, such, like this
meanings.note: Pre-noun adjectival (連体詞, from こう + 言う) placed directly before a noun to mean 'this sort of' or 'things like this'

examples.text: 舌が野蛮なんだよ。私、こういう境界線ははっきりしたいタイプなの。
examples.trans: Your palate is barbaric! I'm the type who likes clear boundaries on things like this.

examples.text: 申し訳ありませんが、うちではこういう本は置けません。
examples.trans: I am very sorry, but we cannot stock books like this in our store.

meanings.note: Connects how things turned out in the present moment.

examples.text: もし正しい鞄を持っていたら、今夜こうして誰もここに立っていませんでしたよ！
examples.trans: If he had picked up the right bag, none of us would be standing here like this tonight!

examples.text: 受付で「こうして」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'こうして' (like this).

meanings.note: Demonstrative place pronoun near the speaker.

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: ありがとうございます！ここでは下の名前で呼びますか？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we call each other by first names here?

examples.text: その通り！もうすっかりここの仲間だね。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in.

examples.text: ここからは歩いて行きます。
examples.trans: I will walk from here.

examples.text: ここからが本番だ。
examples.trans: The real thing starts now.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning scrape.

examples.text: 私は毎日こすれる。
examples.trans: I scrape every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒にこすれる。
examples.trans: I scrape together with them.

examples.text: これはこそです。
examples.trans: This is for sure.

examples.text: あのこそを見ます。
examples.trans: I see that for sure.

meanings.note: Polite directional/demonstrative pronoun.

examples.text: こちらが四番の鍵です。朝ごはんは七時半から十時までです。
examples.trans: Here is key number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: こちらです、陽翔さん。低い木の梁に頭をぶつけないでくださいね。
examples.trans: Right here, Haruto. Please mind your head on the low wooden beam.

examples.text: ほっとしました！こちらが銀の鍵です、陽翔さん。
examples.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Haruto.

meanings.note: Expressive mimetic adverb for doing something stealthily or without others noticing.

examples.text: あっ！私が印刷したカフェのメニュー表を、こっそり持っていたんですか、健二さん！？
examples.trans: Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of the cafe menu I printed, Kenji?!

examples.text: 夜遅くにキッチンへ行って、こっそり甘いタルトを一切れ食べました。
examples.trans: Late at night I went to the kitchen and secretly ate a slice of sweet tart.

meanings.note: Casual form of こちら; points to the speaker's side.

examples.text: 一、二、三！左側をこっちに動かして！
examples.trans: One, two, three! Slide the left side toward me!

examples.text: こっちに来て、この写真を見て！
examples.trans: Come over here and look at this photo!

meanings.note: Abstract noun for intangible matters, facts, or instructions.

examples.text: わかりました。大事なことを全部教えてください。
examples.trans: Got it. Please tell me everything I need to know.

examples.text: ルールその一。まず温かいお茶を飲んで、それからベルに出ること。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: 木の汽車のことで緊張だと？一時間ごとに話が妙になるな。
examples.trans: Nervous over a wooden toy train? This story grows stranger every hour.

meanings.note: Mimetic/onomatopoeic adverb (擬音語) describing a pot simmering softly over low heat, or a light knocking sound.

examples.text: 石のキッチンでスープがことこと煮える音は、都会の車の音よりずっといいね。
examples.trans: Listening to soup simmer in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day.

examples.text: 朝からことこと煮込んだ野菜スープが、ちょうど食べ頃になりました。
examples.trans: The vegetable soup that has been simmering gently since morning is just ready to eat.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb for kneading bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: 毎朝六時にパンの生地をしっかりこねます。
examples.trans: Every morning at six we knead the bread dough thoroughly.

examples.text: 祖母と一緒に日曜日のパンをこねていました。
examples.trans: I used to knead Sunday bread together with my grandmother.

meanings.note: Prenominal determiner; must be followed directly by a noun.

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 由香はこの通りのみんなと昔からの友達みたいに話すんだ。
examples.trans: Yuka talks with everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: じゃあ、この宿が自分で挨拶しているんですね？
examples.trans: So the inn is saying hello on its own?

この世.gloss: this world, the world of the living

meanings.en: this world, the world of the living
meanings.note: Read このよ. Frequently used for emphatic hyperbole ('in the entire world') or in contrast to あの世 (the afterlife).
Often expanded as この世の中 ('this world / society around us').

examples.text: この世で一番多く見られてる作品のジャンルはポルノなんですよ。
examples.trans: The single most-watched genre in the entire world is adult video.

examples.text: この世の中はね、喜ばせごっこなんですよ。
examples.trans: This whole world is a game of making people happy.

examples.text: この世界でやっていくんだったら、人々を喜ばせるために想像力を働かせろ。
examples.trans: If you want to make it in this world, use your imagination to make people happy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Transitive godan verb (intransitive partner こぼれる).

examples.text: 熱いコーヒーをこぼす前に座って飲んでください。
examples.trans: Sit down and drink your hot coffee before you spill it.

examples.text: バケツの水を廊下にこぼさないように気をつけましょう。
examples.trans: Let's be careful not to spill bucket water in the hallway.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb meaning liquid spills.

examples.text: 大変だ！テーブルには一滴もこぼれていませんが……全部私のネクタイに！
examples.trans: Oh dear! Not a single drop spilled on the table, yet all of it is on my tie!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにこぼれます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully spill.

こむ.gloss: to be crowded; to go deeply into (or こんだけ 'this much')

meanings.en: to be crowded, to be congested
meanings.note: Written 混む or 込む. Intransitive godan verb used for streets, trains, and venues filling up with people.

meanings.en: (in こんだけ) this much, to this extent
meanings.note: In the dialogue, こんだけ is a casual spoken contraction of これだけ ('this much / to such an extent'), misparsed by tokenizers as a form of こむ.

examples.text: こんだけ騒ぎになっちゃったら出演させるわけにはいかないんで。
examples.trans: With an uproar this big, there is no way we can put you on air.

examples.text: 週末の繁華街は夜遅くまで人で混んでいる。
examples.trans: The downtown entertainment district is crowded with people until late on weekends.

related.gloss: to become empty, to thin out

こら.gloss: hey!, listen here! (rough interjection); to be brought (こられる)

meanings.note: Rough, intimidating interjection used when scolding, threatening, or barking at someone.

meanings.en: (in こられる) passive or potential stem of 来る (くる)
meanings.note: In 持ってこられたら, こられ is the passive/potential stem of 来る ('if someone brings / is able to bring').

examples.text: てめえ、賠償金払えんのか、こら。
examples.trans: Hey, do you think you can pay the penalty damages?

examples.text: ここまでそっくりな免許を持ってこられたら見分けがつきません。
examples.trans: When someone brings a license this identical, even we cannot tell them apart.

meanings.note: Standalone demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker.

examples.text: なるほど！それで、これが鍵ですか？
examples.trans: Fair enough! And are these the keys?

examples.text: もう一つの濃い青いスーツケース！これ、和子さんの鞄ですか？
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Kazuko's bag?

examples.text: これ、塩が強い有塩バターだよ！甘いジャムパンには無塩バターがいるの！
examples.trans: This is salty salted butter! My sweet jam rolls need unsalted butter!

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。
examples.trans: I'm going home now.

examples.text: これからが本番だ。
examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: A conjunction or phrase meaning 'with this', 'now', or 'by doing this'.

examples.text: これで準備は完了です。
examples.trans: With this, the preparations are complete.

examples.text: これで安心ですね。
examples.trans: Now we can be relieved.

こんな.gloss: such, like this; (with に) this much

meanings.en: such, like this; (with に) this much
meanings.note: Prenominal demonstrative; こんなに means 'this much / so'.

examples.text: 窓を拭いたら中庭がこんなに広く見えますね！
examples.trans: Now that we wiped the windows, the courtyard looks this big!

examples.text: こんな静かな午後にピアノが聴けるなんて幸せです。
examples.trans: How lucky to hear piano on such a quiet afternoon.

こんなに.gloss: so; this much; to this degree

meanings.en: so; this much; to this degree
meanings.note: Built from こんな ('this kind of'); shows surprise at an amount.

examples.text: どうしてこんなに明るい部屋を、本棚の後ろに隠したんですか？
examples.trans: Why would someone hide such a bright room behind a bookcase?

examples.text: こんなにたくさんのお客さまは初めてです。
examples.trans: This is the first time we've had so many guests.

meanings.note: Standard daytime greeting; final は is pronounced ワ.

examples.text: こんにちは！あなたが美央ちゃんね。キッチンの由香だよ。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Mio. I am Yuka from the kitchen.

examples.text: 短い文を三つだけ言いましょう。一つ目、「こんにちは、大輝兄さん、来てくれてありがとう。」
examples.trans: Just say three short sentences. First: 'Hello, big brother Daiki, thank you for coming.'

examples.text: 「こんにちは、大輝兄さん、来てくれてありがとう。」……はい、それなら覚えられます。
examples.trans: 'Hello, big brother Daiki, thank you for coming.' ...Yes, I can remember that.

meanings.note: Standard evening greeting; final は is pronounced ワ.

examples.text: もしもし？こんばんは！門のところには誰も立っていませんよ！
examples.trans: Hello? Good evening! Nobody is standing at the gate!

examples.text: いらっしゃいませ！こんばんは。雨の中、どうぞ中へお入りください。
examples.trans: Welcome! Good evening. Please come inside out of the rain.

examples.text: こんばんは。きれいな床を濡らしてしまって、すみません。
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for getting your clean floor wet.

meanings.note: Honorific prefix attached mainly to Sino-Japanese (kango) words and certain adverbs like ごゆっくり.

examples.text: はい、伝えます！どうぞごゆっくりお過ごしください。
examples.trans: I certainly will! Please enjoy a relaxing morning.

examples.text: ごゆっくりお休みください。朝ごはんは七時半から一階です。
examples.trans: Please sleep well. Breakfast starts at seven thirty on the first floor.

examples.text: 助かりました！和子さん、少々失礼します、ごゆっくり紅茶をどうぞ！
examples.trans: Saved! Excuse me for a moment, Kazuko, please enjoy your tea!

meanings.note: Polite hospitality verb; でございます is a courteous counterpart of です.

examples.text: はい、ひだまり旅館でございます！受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Hello, Hidamari Inn! This is Mio at reception.

examples.text: 失礼いたします。温かいお茶でございます。焼きたてのレモンケーキもすぐ参りますね。
examples.trans: Excuse me, gentlemen. Here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on its way right now.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much.

examples.text: ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Hospitality treat or meal offered generously.

examples.text: そして明日の朝八時、最初の中庭コーヒーは宿からのごちそうですよ！
examples.trans: And tomorrow morning at eight, your first courtyard coffees are on the house!

examples.text: 受付にごちそうがあります。
examples.trans: There is treat at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Suffix attached to time or count units (三十秒ごとに 'every thirty seconds').

examples.text: 三十秒ごとにレースのカーテンから覗いている人が言うセリフかな？
examples.trans: Says the man peeking through the lace curtain every thirty seconds!

examples.text: 受付にごとがあります。
examples.trans: There is every at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Written ご飯 or ごはん. Polite prefix ご + 飯 (めし); refers generally to any prepared meal.
Specifically denotes steamed or boiled rice at the table, contrasting with 米 (こめ, uncooked rice grains).

examples.text: 早く上がりなさい。ごはんできてますから。
examples.trans: Come on inside quickly. Dinner is ready.

examples.text: 忙しい撮影の合間に、スタッフみんなで温かいごはんを食べた。
examples.trans: Between busy takes, the whole crew ate a warm meal together.

meanings.note: Compound of ごみ ('trash') and 箱 ('box').

examples.text: 見てください、もう十二時四分です。私のハガキをごみ箱に捨てたのかもしれません。
examples.trans: Look, it is already four minutes past twelve. Maybe he tossed my postcard in the bin.

examples.text: 受付にごみ箱があります。
examples.trans: There is trash bin at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Casual/intimate apology, often softened with な or ね.

examples.text: 遅れてごめん。
examples.trans: Sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 大輔、ごめんな。
examples.trans: Daisuke, I'm sorry.

meanings.note: Standard heartfelt apology.

examples.text: 本当にごめんなさい。
examples.trans: I'm really sorry.

examples.text: ごめんなさい、もうしません。
examples.trans: I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

meanings.note: Used after a te-form verb (見てごらん 'take a look').

examples.text: 受付の後ろの鏡を見てごらんよ、隆さん。
examples.trans: Take a look in the mirror behind the desk, Takashi.

examples.text: 待てよ。足元の石段を見てごらん。
examples.trans: Hold on. Look down at the stone step.

examples.text: 夕空に映える金色のちょうちんを見上げてごらんなさい……なんて穏やかなんでしょう！
examples.trans: Look up at the golden lanterns glowing against the evening sky... how peaceful!

meanings.note: Respectful form of 一緒 used when inviting someone along.

examples.text: 和子先生、明日この近くで陽翔と静かな夕食を予約しました。ご一緒していただけませんか？
examples.trans: Miss Kazuko, Haruto and I booked a quiet dinner nearby tomorrow. Would you join us?

examples.text: 受付にご一緒があります。
examples.trans: There is together at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Honorific term for someone else's husband or the master of a house/shop.

examples.text: ご主人はいらっしゃいますか。
examples.trans: Is your husband in?

examples.text: ご主人、お帰りなさいませ。
examples.trans: Welcome home, sir.

ご令嬢.gloss: heiress, daughter of a noble house

meanings.en: heiress, daughter of a noble house

examples.text: やっぱりワインは赤ですね。ご令嬢もいかがですか？
examples.trans: When it comes to wine, red really is best. Would you care for some, madam?

examples.text: ご令嬢が村西君をいたく気に入ってな。
examples.trans: The heiress took an immense liking to Muranishi here.

meanings.note: Respectful form of 兄弟 when speaking of guests' family.

examples.text: レモンケーキを食べているご兄弟ですか？
examples.trans: Two brothers eating lemon cake?

examples.text: 受付にご兄弟があります。
examples.trans: There is brothers at the reception desk.

examples.text: 監督は今は衛星にご執心ですけど、また撮れる日を楽しみにしてるんです。
examples.trans: He is absorbed in satellites right now, yet I look forward to the day we film again.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: どうか押し合わずにご堪能いただければと思います。さあ、早速参りましょう！
examples.trans: Please enjoy the show to your heart's content without pushing. Now let's begin!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Respectful term for a husband-and-wife guest pair.

examples.text: いいえ、隆さん。六号室には一時間前に南から来たご夫婦が入りました。
examples.trans: No, Takashi. The couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

examples.text: 受付にご夫婦があります。
examples.trans: There is married couple at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Respectful counterpart of 知っている ('do you know...?').

examples.text: 和子さん、すごく驚いていますね！「けやき通り十二番地」をご存じなんですか？
examples.trans: Kazuko, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve, Keyaki Lane?

examples.text: 受付にご存じがあります。
examples.trans: There is knowing at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Used in ご安心ください ('please rest assured').

examples.text: ご安心ください！三階の静かな屋根裏の書斎を、特別にご用意しました。
examples.trans: Please rest assured! We prepared our quiet third-floor attic study specially for you.

examples.text: 受付にご安心があります。
examples.trans: There is peace of mind at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Respectful form of 家族 for someone else's family.

examples.text: えっ？昔、ご家族がこの近くに住んでいたんですか？
examples.trans: Oh? Did your family live near here once?

examples.text: 受付にご家族があります。
examples.trans: There is family at the reception desk.

examples.text: 奈緒子のためにご尽力くださり、ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you deeply for everything you did on her behalf.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: このご恩は必ず報います。
examples.trans: I swear I will repay this kindness without fail.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ご来訪のお客様がお待ちですが。
examples.trans: Your visiting guest is waiting for you, sir.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite noun for escorting a guest to their room.

examples.text: あの、上へご案内する前に、正直にお詫びしたいことがあります。
examples.trans: Um, before showing you upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

examples.text: 受付にご案内があります。
examples.trans: There is guiding at the reception desk.

examples.text: ご清聴ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you all very much for listening.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

ご無沙汰.gloss: not contacting for a long time

meanings.en: not contacting for a long time

examples.text: どうしてここに？ご無沙汰してます。出てきたんですね。
examples.trans: What brings you here? Long time no see—so you got out!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used with する/いたす when preparing something for a guest.

examples.text: ご安心ください！三階の静かな屋根裏の書斎を、特別にご用意しました。
examples.trans: Please rest assured! We prepared our quiet third-floor attic study specially for you.

examples.text: 受付にご用意があります。
examples.trans: There is preparation at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Respectful form of 自分.

examples.text: 木の汽車が入ったご自分の鞄は、受け取らなかったんですか？
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

examples.text: 受付で「ご自分」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'ご自分' (oneself).

ご苦労さま.gloss: thank you for your hard work, good job

meanings.en: thank you for your hard work, appreciate your trouble
meanings.note: Written ご苦労様. Traditionally used by a boss or senior addressing subordinates or delivery/service workers; toward superiors or peers, お疲れ様です is standard.

examples.text: ご苦労さまです。今日も遠くまで配達ありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for your hard work. Thanks for making the deliveries so far out today.

examples.text: 遅くまで編集作業、ご苦労さまでした。
examples.trans: Thank you for all your hard work editing until so late.

related.gloss: thank you for your hard work (general)

examples.text: この仕事してきて、一番のご褒美だったかもしれないな。
examples.trans: In all my time doing this work, that may have been my greatest reward.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ああ美しい、ご覧ください。
examples.trans: Oh, how beautiful—please take a look.

examples.text: 皆様、どうぞとくとご覧くださいませ。
examples.trans: Everyone, please take a good, close look.

meanings.note: Polite na-adjective thanking someone for their kindness.

examples.text: まあ、ご親切にありがとう。コップ半分だけお願いします。
examples.trans: Oh, how kind of you. Just half a glass, please.

examples.text: この旅館はとてもご親切ですね。
examples.trans: This inn is very kind, isn't it?

examples.text: どうか我が社のプロジェクトにご賛同いただけないでしょうか。
examples.trans: Won't you please lend your approval to our project as well?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Honorific form of 購入, commonly used by salespeople thanking customers.

examples.text: ご購入ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your purchase.

examples.text: ご購入を検討しています。
examples.trans: I am considering purchasing it.

meanings.note: Polite prefix ご- + 近所 ('neighbourhood').

examples.text: ご近所の方が気軽に立ち寄れるカフェにします。
examples.trans: We will make it a café where neighbours can drop in easily.

examples.text: ご近所の本の交換用にかごを置きました。
examples.trans: We set out a basket for neighbourhood book sharing.

meanings.note: Affectionate everyday term for people living nearby, combining ご近所 ('neighbourhood') + -さん.

examples.text: 月曜日の入れ替わった青いスーツケースから、ずっと続くご近所さんになりましたね！
examples.trans: From a swapped blue suitcase on Monday to neighbours for good!

examples.text: 欠けたカップはゼロ、切れたヒューズもゼロ、そして笑顔のご近所さんが二十四人だ。
examples.trans: Zero chipped cups, zero blown fuses, and twenty-four smiling neighbours.

meanings.note: Used in apologies for causing inconvenience.

examples.text: ご迷惑をおかけしました、健二さん。一週間も鞄を守ってくれてありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Sorry for the trouble, Kenji. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.

examples.text: 受付にご迷惑があります。
examples.trans: There is trouble at the reception desk.

related.gloss: wander into; lose one's way into

meanings.note: Courteous compliment on a guest's menu choice.

examples.text: 素晴らしいご選択です！横に蜂蜜かりんごジャムはいかがですか？
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

examples.text: 受付にご選択があります。
examples.trans: There is choice at the reception desk.

examples.text: 今週か来週辺りでご都合のいい時間があれば…
examples.trans: If you have a convenient time sometime this week or next week...

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Casual reassuring sentence-final particle.

examples.text: おかげさまで、今夜はぐっすり眠れそうです。
examples.trans: Thanks to your kindness, I think I will sleep soundly tonight.

examples.text: 見事な速さです！お店の人から領収書をもらいましたか？
examples.trans: Impressive speed! Did you get a receipt from the shopkeeper?

examples.text: 階段が狭いし、隆さんが古いランプの箱を置いているからさ。
examples.trans: Because the stairs are narrow and Takashi keeps old lamp boxes up there.

meanings.note: Encouraging interjection when starting an action.

examples.text: 誰にも言わないでくださいね！さあ、ベルが鳴ったら明るい笑顔ですよ。
examples.trans: Please do not tell anyone! Now, smile brightly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 嬉しいです！さあ、朝ごはんをしっかりいただきますわ。
examples.trans: How wonderful! Now I am ready to enjoy a hearty breakfast.

examples.text: 古い建物は毎週火曜日にネジが一本緩むんだ。さあ座りな。
examples.trans: Old buildings loosen one screw every Tuesday. Go on, sit.

meanings.note: An exclamation used to urge someone to do something quickly, to invite someone enthusiastically, or to draw attention.

examples.text: さあさあ、遠慮しないで食べてください。
examples.trans: Come on, don't hold back, please eat.

examples.text: さあさあ、ショーの始まりですよ！
examples.trans: Step right up, the show is about to begin!

meanings.note: Focus particle meaning 'so long as' with a conditional.

examples.text: 喜んで、大輝くん。古いピアノを売る話さえ出なければね！
examples.trans: With pleasure, Daiki, so long as nobody brings up selling old pianos!

examples.text: 受付で「さえ」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'さえ' (even).

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; often used for dedicating one's life, time, or effort.

examples.text: 人生を仕事にささげる。
examples.trans: Devote one's life to work.

examples.text: 家族にすべてをささげた。
examples.trans: I dedicated everything to my family.

meanings.en: as one would expect; true to reputation
meanings.note: Expresses admiration when someone lives up to their reputation.

examples.text: さすがオーナー様、お目が高い！
examples.trans: As expected of the owner, you have a keen eye!

examples.text: さすがプロだね。
examples.trans: You're a pro, just as expected.

させる.gloss: to make (someone) do, to let (someone) do

meanings.en: to make (someone) do, to let or allow (someone) to do
meanings.note: Causative form of する, and the causative auxiliary attached to ichidan verb stems (e.g., もうけさせる, 'to let someone profit').

meanings.en: (in ～させていただく) to take the liberty of doing
meanings.note: Humble business construction literally meaning 'to humbly receive permission to do.'

examples.text: あんたは商才がある。頑張ってまたもうけさせてくれよ。
examples.trans: You've got real business flair; work hard and make me rich again.

examples.text: では、お宅の作品の流通をすべてストップさせていただきます。
examples.trans: Very well, then we will halt retail distribution of all your releases.

meanings.note: Refers to a short time earlier the same day.

examples.text: そうですよ！さっき、表紙の裏に二枚目の紙が留めてあるのに気づきました。
examples.trans: That's right! Earlier I noticed a second page clipped behind the cover sheet.

examples.text: 受付にさっきがあります。
examples.trans: There is a moment ago at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Frequently used in impatient or blunt commands urging someone to stop dawdling and get moving immediately.

examples.text: よし、じゃあさっさと乗れ。行くぞ！
examples.trans: Alright, hurry up and hop in! Let's roll!

examples.text: おい、スタッフさんがスタンバイしてんだよ。さっさとしろや。
examples.trans: Hey, the crew is standing by waiting for you. Hurry it up!

さっと.gloss: quickly, briskly, in one smooth motion

meanings.en: quickly, briskly, in one smooth motion
meanings.note: Mimetic adverb for swift, neat action without fuss.

examples.text: お昼のスープは注文からさっと出せるのが一番です。
examples.trans: For lunch soup, being able to serve it briskly is best.

examples.text: 乾いた布でテーブルの上をさっと拭きました。
examples.trans: I gave the tabletop a quick wipe with a dry cloth.

meanings.note: Polite title suffix more formal than さん, used for guests.

examples.text: いいえ、お気になさらないでください！陽翔さまですね。
examples.trans: Not at all, please do not worry! You must be Haruto.

examples.text: 受付にさまがあります。
examples.trans: There is honorable title suffix at the reception desk.

examples.text: それじゃ、さみしんぼうさん二人に乾杯。
examples.trans: Well then, cheers to two lonely souls.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standard farewell when parting.

examples.text: さようなら、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Goodbye — nice weather again today!

examples.text: 玄関で明るく「さようなら」と言いました。
examples.trans: At the entrance, they cheerfully said, 'goodbye!'

examples.text: 俺は死ぬ気でお前と向かい合ってる。受け止めてやるからすべてさらけ出せ。
examples.trans: I'm facing you with everything on the line; I'll catch whatever you give, so bare it all.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 水くさいこと言うなよ。昔から浮いたり沈んだりをさらし合える仲だろ。
examples.trans: Don't talk like a stranger. You and I have seen each other's highs and lows since way back.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written 更に. Modifies verbs or adjectives to indicate an increase in degree, scale, or intensity.
Used as a sentence-initial connector to add an additional, often stronger point.

examples.text: 当然、お前さんは販売網を北海道からさらに広げるわな？
examples.trans: Naturally, you're going to expand your sales network even further out from Hokkaido, right?

examples.text: 新作のビデオは前作よりさらに過激な内容になっている。
examples.trans: The new video release features content even more extreme than the previous one.

related.gloss: in addition, on top of that

meanings.note: Passive form of する (to do).

examples.text: この法律は来年から施行される。
examples.trans: This law will be enforced starting next year.

examples.text: 彼はみんなから尊敬されている。
examples.trans: He is respected by everyone.

meanings.note: Takes に for the thing touched: スイッチにさわる.

examples.text: 隆さん、その真鍮のスイッチにさわる前に、一分待ってよ。
examples.trans: Takashi, wait one minute before you touch that brass switch.

examples.text: 三十年前の布の電線だよ、隆さん。俺が中を見る前に、スイッチにさわるな。
examples.trans: It's thirty-year-old cloth wire, Takashi. Never touch a switch before I look inside.

examples.text: 熱いですから、ポットにさわらないでください。
examples.trans: It's hot, so please don't touch the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday respectful title suffix for adults regardless of gender or marital status.

examples.text: はじめまして、由香さん。すごくいい匂いですね！
examples.trans: Nice to meet you, Yuka. Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 皆さん、おはようございます！ようこそ、美央さん。準備はいいですか？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Mio. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 落ち着いてよ、隆さん。部屋はきれいだし、タオルも新しい。
examples.trans: Relax, Takashi. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 奇遇ねえ。ニシンのさんしょう漬け、懐かしいでしょ。
examples.trans: What a coincidence! Herring pickled with pepper leaves—brings back memories, doesn't it?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

ざ.gloss: bound syllable za (as in いざ); colloquial fused particle

examples.text: いざとなると、どうしていいか分からなくなって…
examples.trans: Now that the moment is here, I don't know what to do anymore...

examples.text: いざ本番が始まると、不思議と手が震えなかった。
examples.trans: Once the actual shoot began, strangely enough my hands didn't shake.

meanings.note: Skimming or glancing over something briefly (ざっと目を通す).

examples.text: 素晴らしいですね……待っている間に、大家さんからの手紙にざっと目を通しましょう。
examples.trans: How wonderful... while we wait, let me glance through this letter from the landlord.

examples.text: ざっとお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (quickly).

meanings.note: A type of large-crystal sugar, often used in Japanese confectionery and cooking for its distinctive texture and slow melting rate.

examples.text: カステラの底にはざらめ糖が敷かれている。
examples.trans: Coarse sugar is spread on the bottom of castella cake.

examples.text: ざらめ糖を使って煮物を作る。
examples.trans: Make a simmered dish using coarse sugar.

meanings.note: Clause-linking particle listing reasons or parallel qualities.

examples.text: おはようございます！はい、受付はきれいですし、鍵も揃っています。
examples.trans: Good morning! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.

examples.text: 落ち着いてよ、隆さん。部屋はきれいだし、タオルも新しい。
examples.trans: Relax, Takashi. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 一番から七番まで鍵は全部出ているし、八号室はペンキが乾いていない。
examples.trans: Every key from one to seven is out, and room eight still has wet paint.

meanings.note: Always pairs with a negative verb to mean 'nothing except / only'.

examples.text: 宿のせいじゃありませんよ。でも、今着ているコートしかありませんわ！
examples.trans: It is not the inn's fault. Still, I only have the coat I am wearing right now!

examples.text: 最後の一個を冬に使ったんだ。橋の向こうの古い金物屋にしか、このサイズはない。
examples.trans: I used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

meanings.note: Written 然し (almost always in kana). Standard conjunction introducing a contrasting clause or sentence.
In conversational Japanese, frequently used as an interjectional pivot to express fresh surprise, exasperation, or admiration.

examples.text: もうさっさと終わらせましょ、こんな仕事。しかしひでえな、作文かこれ？
examples.trans: Let's just get a job like this over with fast—honestly, what an awful script!

examples.text: いやあ、しかしみんなまだ慣れんな。
examples.trans: Man, I still cannot get used to how everyone looks now.

meanings.note: A frown, a grimace, a scowl, or a puckered face (often showing displeasure, pain, or deep thought).

examples.text: 彼は苦い薬を飲んでしかめっ面をした。
examples.trans: He grimaced after drinking the bitter medicine.

examples.text: しかめっ面をしないで笑って。
examples.trans: Don't scowl; smile.

meanings.note: Conjunction adding an emphatic extra detail.

examples.text: しかもその方は、今夜八時にここへ着きます。あと四十分です！
examples.trans: And he arrives here at eight o'clock this evening—in forty minutes!

examples.text: 受付で「しかも」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'しかも' (moreover).

meanings.note: Compound ichidan verb formed from する + すぎる.

examples.text: 最近働きすぎています。
examples.trans: I've been working too much lately.

examples.text: 心配しすぎないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'securely, heartily, or reliably'.

examples.text: もう一つの青いスーツケースは、荷物室にしっかり鍵をかけておきました。
examples.trans: I locked the other blue suitcase safely inside our luggage room.

examples.text: 嬉しいです！さあ、朝ごはんをしっかりいただきますわ。
examples.trans: How wonderful! Now I am ready to enjoy a hearty breakfast.

examples.text: 門のベルが鳴ったぞ。しっかり一回だ。
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

examples.text: 紐をしっかりと結ぶ。
examples.trans: Tie the string firmly.

examples.text: しっかりと考えてから決める。
examples.trans: Decide after thinking solidly.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning doing.

examples.text: 私は毎日している。
examples.trans: I doing every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒にしている。
examples.trans: I doing together with them.

してやる.gloss: to do for someone; to do to someone (emphatic)

meanings.en: to do (a favor) for someone (of equal or lower status)
meanings.note: Compound of する (in て-form) + auxiliary やる. Used casually toward peers, juniors, or third parties (e.g., 勘弁してやる, 'to forgive/let someone off').

meanings.en: to definitely do to someone, I'll show them
meanings.note: Also expresses bold determination or defiance when taking an action that affects someone else.

examples.text: 俺がもう騒ぎ起こさせないようにするから、今回は勘弁してやってよ。
examples.trans: I will make sure he causes no more uproar, so let him off this time.

examples.text: あいつが困っているなら、俺が力貸してやるよ。
examples.trans: If he's in a bind, I'll lend him a hand myself.

しばらく.gloss: for a while, for the time being

meanings.en: for a while, for some time, for the time being
meanings.note: Written 暫く (usually in kana). Often followed by the topic particle は (しばらくは, 'for the time being at least').

examples.text: よく売れるわ。しばらくは稼げそうだ。
examples.trans: They're selling great. Looks like we'll be making good money for a while.

examples.text: 警察の監視が厳しいから、しばらくおとなしくしていろ。
examples.trans: Police surveillance is tight right now, so lay low for a while.

related.gloss: for the time being, for now

しまう.gloss: finish; end up doing; put away

meanings.en: finish; end up doing; put away
meanings.note: Alone means 'put away'; after a te-form verb, expresses completion or an accidental slip.

examples.text: ああ、大失敗です！昨日、眼鏡なしでタブレットに電話予約を入れてしまいました！
examples.trans: Oh, disaster! Yesterday I entered a phone booking on the tablet without my glasses!

examples.text: あと三十五分です！ひどい一つ星の口コミを書かれてしまいます！
examples.trans: Thirty-five minutes left! He will write a terrible one-star review!

examples.text: こんばんは。きれいな床を濡らしてしまって、すみません。
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for getting your clean floor wet.

しゃ.gloss: if/when (colloquial ～ては); honorific segment in ～てらっしゃる

meanings.en: (colloquial particle) contraction of ～ては or ～では
meanings.note: In rapid speech, ～ては/～では contracts to ～ちゃ/～しゃ after certain sounds to express a negative condition ('if one does X, it won't do').

meanings.en: (in dialogue) substring of ～てらっしゃる or しゃべる
meanings.note: In the show's dialogue, appears inside the contracted honorific auxiliary ～てらっしゃる (from ～ていらっしゃる, 'to be doing') and the verb しゃべる (喋る, 'to talk, chatter').

examples.text: 今着てらっしゃるのがお似合いです。白はイノセンスの象徴ですから。
examples.trans: What you're wearing right now suits you best. White is the symbol of innocence.

examples.text: 安全圏からペチャクチャしゃべんないでよ。何にも知らないくせに。
examples.trans: Quit chattering at me from your safe zone when you don't know a thing.

しょ.gloss: right?, isn't it?, probably (colloquial でしょう)

meanings.note: Colloquial shortened form of the presumptive copula でしょう, spoken with rising intonation to seek confirmation or agreement.
Spoken with falling intonation (or with ね/よ as でしょうね) to express an educated guess or conjecture.

examples.text: ポルノ、見てるんでしょ？
examples.trans: You watch them yourself, don't you?

examples.text: きっと情熱的な撮影をしてるんでしょうね、村西監督は。
examples.trans: Director Muranishi must be in the middle of a passionate shoot right now.

examples.text: 彼とはどうも性が合わない。
examples.trans: I just don't get along with his nature.

examples.text: 風邪の症状が出ている。
examples.trans: Cold symptoms are appearing.

しょうが.gloss: way, means (in しょうがない 'no use / cannot be helped')

meanings.en: (in しょうがない / しょうがねえ) no use, pointless; cannot be helped
meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 仕様が (しようが, 'way or means of doing'). Almost exclusively bound with ない (or rough ねえ) in しょうがない ('there's no point / it can't be helped').
When written 生姜 (しょうが), a common homophone noun meaning the culinary root ginger.

examples.text: ほえててもしょうがねえだろ、現実は池沢が売れてんだからよ。
examples.trans: Barking does no good when the reality is that Ikezawa's tapes are the ones selling.

examples.text: 偽物のセックスなんか撮ってもしょうがないんだ、俺は。
examples.trans: There is zero point in my filming fake intimacy anymore.

related.gloss: it can't be helped, there is no point
there is no other way, unavoidable

examples.text: しょう油という最高のダシがあるのに。
examples.trans: Even though we already have the finest seasoning in soy sauce...

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial i-adjective for a strong salty taste.

examples.text: 甘い苺ジャムに、しょっぱいバターを出しても大丈夫でしょうか？
examples.trans: Can we really serve salty butter alongside sweet strawberry jam?

examples.text: 今日はとてもしょっぱいですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very salty, isn't it?

meanings.note: part of kamoshirenai

examples.text: 明日行くかもしれない。
examples.trans: I might go tomorrow.

examples.text: 嘘かもしれない。
examples.trans: It might be a lie.

しれる.gloss: be known (in かもしれません)

meanings.en: be known (in かもしれません)
meanings.note: Used after かも to form かもしれません ('might / perhaps').

examples.text: 見てください、もう十二時四分です。私のハガキをごみ箱に捨てたのかもしれません。
examples.trans: Look, it is already four minutes past twelve. Maybe he tossed my postcard in the bin.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにしれます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully be known.

じ.gloss: old man, mister (in じいさん / おじさん); character (字)

meanings.en: old man, pops; middle-aged man (in じいさん / おじさん)
meanings.note: In the dialogue, extracted from the familiar address terms おじさん (伯父さん/小父さん, 'mister, uncle') and じいさん (爺さん, 'old man, pops,' from 爺 じい/じ).

meanings.en: letter, character, handwriting (字); hour, o'clock (時)
meanings.note: As a standalone noun or counter, represents 字 ('character, handwriting') or 時 ('o'clock, time').

examples.text: おじさん、ここに笛あるかい？笛！
examples.trans: Hey mister, got any whistles in this shop? A whistle!

examples.text: じいさん、ここに笛ねえか？早くしてくれよ！
examples.trans: Hey pops, got a whistle in here? Hurry it up, please!

meanings.note: Listening or watching without moving.

examples.text: とても静かな子でね！階段の三段目に座って、一音残らずじっと聞いていたの。
examples.trans: Such a quiet child! He sat on the third step of the stairs listening closely to every single note.

examples.text: じっとお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (still).

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: じゃ、始めます。
examples.trans: Well then, I will start.

examples.text: じゃ、また明日。
examples.trans: Well then, see you tomorrow.

meanings.note: Conversational contraction of では introducing a conclusion or farewell.

examples.text: じゃあ、この宿が自分で挨拶しているんですね？
examples.trans: So the inn is saying hello on its own?

examples.text: じゃあ、どうして普段はお客さんに貸さないんですか？
examples.trans: Then why do we never rent it out to guests normally?

examples.text: えっ、じゃあ今夜は暖房も、洗面所のお湯も出ないんですか？
examples.trans: Wait, does that mean no heating tonight and no hot water at the taps either?

meanings.note: Friendly casual farewell among friends and colleagues.

examples.text: また明日の朝六時にね。じゃあね！
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning at six. Bye then!

examples.text: 気をつけて帰ってね。じゃあね！
examples.trans: Get home safely. See you later!

meanings.note: Suffix attached to place or time nouns (町じゅう 'all across town', 一晩じゅう 'all night long').

examples.text: 座って、美央ちゃん！今朝は町じゅう走ったんだから、コーヒーを飲んで。
examples.trans: Sit down, Mio! You ran all across town this morning, so drink some coffee.

examples.text: デシベルのことで一晩じゅう慌てていたなんて、隆さんが聞いたらびっくりするよ！
examples.trans: Takashi will be stunned when he hears he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: 大阪じゅうの歴史ある中庭建築を専門にしている建築家ですよ！
examples.trans: An architect who specialises in historic courtyard buildings all across Osaka!

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic adverb used with 見る ('stare at').

examples.text: お客さんをじろじろ見るんじゃない。鞄を渡して、余計なことは聞かないんだ。
examples.trans: Do not stare at guests. We hand over the bag and mind our own business.

examples.text: じろじろお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (staringly).

meanings.note: verb suffix

examples.text: ストーブをつけて、冷え切った客間を早く暖めましょう。
examples.trans: Let's turn on the heater and quickly warm up the chilled guest room.

examples.text: お客様がお帰りになる前に、お預かりした傘をお渡しするのを忘れないでね。
examples.trans: Before the guest leaves, don't forget to hand back the umbrella we kept for them.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

examples.text: 遅れてすいません！
examples.trans: Sorry I'm late!

すか.gloss: is it?, really? (casual contraction of ですか)

meanings.note: Appears at the end of polite questions as part of ですか / んですか, or in colloquial speech as the clipped contraction ～っすか / ～すか.
As a slang noun (スカ), refers to drawing a losing blank in a lottery or a disappointing dud.

examples.text: 人のありのままの姿撮って、わいせつなんですか？
examples.trans: Is filming people just as they naturally are really indecent?

examples.text: 社長、よろしいんですか？
examples.trans: President, are you sure about that?

meanings.note: Attaches to verb or adjective stems (速すぎる 'too fast', 長すぎました 'was too long').

examples.text: 青いハンドルを左へゆっくり回せ。速すぎるなよ。
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel slowly to the left. Not too fast.

examples.text: 三年は長すぎました、美央さん。二回目の冬に電話するべきだったんです。
examples.trans: Three years was too long, Mio. I should have phoned him two winters ago.

すく.gloss: to become empty; to get hungry (with おなかが)

meanings.en: to get hungry (in おなかがすく)
meanings.note: Written 空く. Literally 'to become empty'; most frequently heard in the set expression おなかがすく ('one's stomach gets empty' -> to become hungry).

meanings.en: to thin out, to become less crowded
meanings.note: Used of roads, trains, or shops when crowds clear out (the direct antonym of 混む).

examples.text: 朝から何も食べてないから、おなかすいたよ。
examples.trans: I haven't eaten a thing since morning, so I'm starving.

examples.text: 昼過ぎになれば、この喫茶店も少しはすくだろう。
examples.trans: Once it's past noon, this coffee shop should clear out a bit.

related.gloss: to be crowded, to be congested

meanings.note: Immediately in time or directly adjacent in space.

examples.text: 中庭側です。大きな木のすぐ上で、とても静かですよ。
examples.trans: The courtyard side. Right above the big tree, and it is very quiet.

examples.text: どうぞ座ってください、和子さん。今すぐ名札を確認しましょう。
examples.trans: Please sit down, Kazuko. Let's check the luggage tag right away.

examples.text: 美央さん、今すぐ駅の忘れ物センターに電話してください。
examples.trans: Mio, please call the station lost-and-found office right away.

examples.text: いや、すけべだな。
examples.trans: Well now, what a rascal!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

すける.gloss: it is that..., though (in ～んですけど); to be transparent (透ける)

meanings.en: (in ～んですけど / ～んですけれど) it is that..., though; excuse me, ...
meanings.note: In the dialogue, a tokenizer segmentation of んですけど / んですけれど, the polite explanatory clause ending used to soften statements or introduce a request.

meanings.en: to be transparent, to show through
meanings.note: As a standalone ichidan verb written 透ける (すける), means for light or an underlying object to show through thin material.

examples.text: あの、監督、ここ僕の家なんですけど…
examples.trans: Um, Director... this building is my own apartment!

examples.text: あの、こちらに行きたいんですけれど。
examples.trans: Excuse me, I'm trying to find this address right here.

すげる.gloss: amazing, incredible; super, crazy (colloquial すげえ)

meanings.en: (as すげえ) amazing, awesome, incredible; super, extremely
meanings.note: In the dialogue, すげえ is the rough/colloquial vowel-coalesced form of すごい (凄い), used both as an adjective ('amazing!') and as an intensifier adverb ('super good').

meanings.en: to fit, to attach (a handle or strap)
meanings.note: As a literal ichidan verb written 挿げる (すげる), means to fasten a cord or thong onto clogs (下駄の鼻緒をすげる).

examples.text: すげえ。俺たちが見てたのは偽もんだったんすね。
examples.trans: Amazing—so what we used to watch on screen was all fake!

examples.text: まあね、相性とかはすげえいいよね。
examples.trans: Well, our chemistry together is honestly amazing.

meanings.note: In adverbial form すごく, commonly means 'very / wonderfully'.

examples.text: はじめまして、由香さん。すごくいい匂いですね！
examples.trans: Nice to meet you, Yuka. Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 屋根に当たる雨の音を聞いて。すごく居心地がいいね！
examples.trans: Listen to the sound of rain on the roof—it feels so cosy!

すずらん.gloss: lily of the valley; Suzuran (Hokkaido brand/train name)

meanings.note: Written 鈴蘭 (literally 'bell orchid'). The emblematic spring flower of Hokkaido.

meanings.en: Suzuran (Hokkaido brand, coffee shop, or express train name)
meanings.note: In the show's Hokkaido scenes, used in quotation marks 「すずらん」 as a regional product or menu name named after the flower.

examples.text: すみません、「すずらん」をひと箱ください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, one pack of Suzuran, please.

examples.text: あいつも「すずらん」を吸ってるのか。北海道じゃ定番だからな。
examples.trans: He smokes Suzuran too, huh? Well, it's a classic up in Hokkaido.

meanings.note: Indicates a thorough change or complete forgetting.

examples.text: その通り！もうすっかりここの仲間だね。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in.

examples.text: あっ！スーツケースやボイラーや手紙の騒ぎで、すっかり忘れていました！
examples.trans: Oh! With all the commotion over suitcases, the boiler, and the letter, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Mimetic adverb for a tidy counter or refreshed feeling.

examples.text: カウンターの上をすっきり片づけました。
examples.trans: We tidied the countertop nice and neat.

examples.text: 窓を拭いたら部屋の中がすっきり明るくなりました。
examples.trans: Wiping the windows made the room look clean and bright.

meanings.note: Written 既に. Slightly more formal and emphatic than もう; indicates that an action or milestone has already been reached.

examples.text: すでに三十万部ほど売り上げてるのか。
examples.trans: Has it really sold around 300,000 copies already?

examples.text: 警察が事務所に踏み込んだ時には、テープはすでに出荷されていた。
examples.trans: By the time the police raided the office, the tapes had already been shipped out.

すねる.gloss: so it is..., isn't it? (in ～んですね); to sulk (拗ねる)

meanings.en: (in ～んですね / ～なんですね) so it is..., isn't it?; I see that...
meanings.note: In the dialogue, a tokenizer segmentation of んですね, the polite explanatory ending used when registering new information or warmly confirming a fact with someone.

meanings.en: to sulk, to pout, to be peevish
meanings.note: As a standalone ichidan verb written 拗ねる (すねる), means to sulk or act rebelliously out of hurt feelings.

examples.text: 出身、福島なんですね。道理で気が合うと思った。
examples.trans: You're originally from Fukushima, aren't you? No wonder we hit it off.

examples.text: どうしてここに？ご無沙汰してます。出てきたんですね。
examples.trans: What brings you here? Long time no see—so you got out!

related.gloss: to twist, to be perverse or sulky

meanings.note: Written 素晴らしい. One of Toru Muranishi's signature enthusiastic catchphrases of praise while directing behind the camera.

examples.text: すばらしい、いいね！そのままカメラを見て！
examples.trans: Magnificent—I love it! Keep looking right at the camera just like that!

examples.text: 起きてたんだね。すばらしいよ、これ。
examples.trans: You were awake, huh? This footage is truly wonderful.

meanings.note: Slightly more poised synonym of 全部 ('all').

examples.text: この曲のすべてが真ん中のレの音にかかっています。
examples.trans: The whole song rests on that middle D note.

examples.text: 準備はすべて整いましたから安心してください。
examples.trans: Everything is ready, so please rest easy.

meanings.note: Written 済まん. Contracted negative form of 済む (from すまない); a frank, informal apology used primarily by men toward peers or subordinates.

examples.text: すまん、すまん。待たせちまったな。
examples.trans: Sorry, my bad. Kept you waiting, huh?

examples.text: 急に呼び出してすまん。どうしても折り入って頼みたいことがあるんだ。
examples.trans: Sorry for calling you out on such short notice. There's a favor I really need to ask you.

すみません.gloss: excuse me; I'm sorry; thank you

meanings.en: excuse me; I'm sorry; thank you
meanings.note: Essential polite phrase used to get attention, apologize, or thank someone for trouble.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 読みますね。「間違えてすみません。青い鞄を金曜日まで預かってください。」
examples.trans: Let me read it: 'Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.'

すむ.gloss: to finish, to be settled (済む); assimilated form of する (すん)

meanings.en: (as すん-) colloquial assimilated form of する before ん or な
meanings.note: In the dialogue, する assimilates to すん before ん (何するんだ -> 何すんだ, 'what are you doing?!') and before negative imperative な (気にするな -> 気にすんな, 'don't worry about it!').

meanings.en: to end, to be settled, to be resolved without further trouble
meanings.note: As a standalone godan verb written 済む (すむ), means for a matter or payment to be settled or finished (or 住む, 'to live, reside').

examples.text: てめえ、何すんだ！カメラにさわるな！
examples.trans: Hey, what the heck are you doing! Keep your hands off the camera!

examples.text: まあまあ、細かいことは気にすんなよ。ここのおっきいのが後藤だ。
examples.trans: Now, now, don't sweat the small details! The big guy here is Goto.

meanings.note: To grate, to scrape down into small pieces or paste (using a grater).

examples.text: 大根をすりおろす。
examples.trans: Grate the daikon radish.

examples.text: 生姜をすりおろして料理に入れる。
examples.trans: Grate ginger and put it in the dish.

meanings.note: Glass ground to diffuse light softly without harsh glare.

examples.text: すりガラスの窓から柔らかい朝の光が入ります。
examples.trans: Soft morning light filters in through the frosted glass window.

examples.text: ランプの笠は古いすりガラスでできています。
examples.trans: The lamp shade is made of old frosted glass.

meanings.note: Compound verb of rubbing and decreasing.

examples.text: 床がすり減る前に、美央ちゃん、声をかけて来てあげて！
examples.trans: Mio, go talk to him before he wears out the floorboards!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにすり減ります。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully wear down.

meanings.note: Core irregular verb; turns action nouns (予約, 掃除, 電話) into verbs and marks sensory impressions (音がする, 香りがする).

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: じゃあ、この宿が自分で挨拶しているんですね？
examples.trans: So the inn is saying hello on its own?

examples.text: 今日来る四号室のお客さまは一週間泊まります。完璧にしましょう！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week. Let's make everything perfect!

meanings.note: Figurative sense of failing to connect in communication, timing, or feelings (noun form of すれ違う).
Literal sense of two people or vehicles moving past each other in opposite directions.

examples.text: 取引先とのちょっとしたすれ違いだ。
examples.trans: It's just a minor misunderstanding with our business partner.

examples.text: お互いの気持ちがすれ違い、二人は別れることになった。
examples.trans: Their feelings grew out of sync with each other, and the two ended up parting ways.

related.gloss: to pass by each other; to miss each other

examples.text: 傘を持たずに駅まで歩いたら、すっかり濡れてしまった。
examples.trans: When I walked to the station without taking an umbrella, I got completely soaked.

examples.text: 焦らずに一つずつ丁寧に原因を調べてみましょう。
examples.trans: Without rushing, let's carefully check the cause one step at a time.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a noticeable degree.

examples.text: 実は、洗面所の蛇口がずいぶん冷たかったので、聞きに下りて来たんです。
examples.trans: Actually, the washroom tap felt awfully cold, so I came down to ask why.

examples.text: ずいぶんお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (quite).

ずっと.gloss: far more; all along; the whole time

meanings.en: far more; all along; the whole time
meanings.note: Intensifies comparisons ('much more') or continuous duration ('all along').

examples.text: 正直に言うと、前の灰色のオフィスよりここの方がずっと好きです。
examples.trans: Honestly, I like this place far better than my old grey office.

examples.text: 二十ミリ、真鍮、ボイラーのバルブ……走りながらずっと唱えます！
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve... I will repeat it the whole way!

examples.text: よく顔を見せてちょうだい、陽翔くん！ピアノよりずっと背が高くなったわね！
examples.trans: Let me get a proper look at you, Haruto! You grew much taller than the piano!

meanings.note: Distributive particle after a counter (一本ずつ 'one each').

examples.text: 青いカップの横に、ナプキンを一枚と小さいスプーンを一本ずつ置いて。
examples.trans: Put one napkin and one small spoon beside every blue cup.

examples.text: 受付で「ずつ」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'ずつ' (apiece).

ずぶ濡れ.gloss: soaked to the skin, drenched through

meanings.en: soaked to the skin, drenched through
meanings.note: Compound of mimetic ずぶ + 濡れ ('wetting').

examples.text: 無塗装の木がずぶ濡れになったらペンキが塗れません。
examples.trans: If the bare wood gets drenched, we won't be able to paint it.

examples.text: 傘を忘れて帰りにずぶ濡れになってしまいました。
examples.trans: I forgot my umbrella and got soaked on the way back.

meanings.note: Describes glasses slipping down one's nose.

examples.text: 隆さん！嬉しい理由で、鼻から眼鏡がずり落ちましたよ！
examples.trans: Takashi! Your glasses just slipped down your nose for a happy reason!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにずり落ちます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully slip down.

related.gloss: calm down; feel at home; settle

meanings.en: the whole time, all along, continuously
meanings.note: Emphatic elongated form of ずっと, stressing unbroken duration.
Emphatic degree modifier used when comparing two things.

examples.text: ずーっと正常位見せられてもつまんないから、盛り上がってきたらこうやって体を起こして。
examples.trans: Showing the same position the whole time gets dull, so as the climax builds, lift her up like this.

examples.text: 朝からずーっと雨が降りっぱなしだよ。
examples.trans: It has been raining non-stop the entire time since morning.

related.gloss: continuously, all the time; by far

meanings.note: Attributes an unwelcome result to a cause (宿のせい 'the inn's fault').

examples.text: 宿のせいじゃありませんよ。でも、今着ているコートしかありませんわ！
examples.trans: It is not the inn's fault. Still, I only have the coat I am wearing right now!

examples.text: 受付にせいがあります。
examples.trans: There is fault at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Emphasizes that an effort or opportunity is valuable and should not go to waste.
Often paired with なのに to express regret over a wasted chance, or だから to encourage making the most of it.

examples.text: せっかく家族団らんの時間なのに。
examples.trans: And here we finally had some precious family time together.

examples.text: せっかくここまで来たんだから、美味しいものを食べて帰ろう。
examples.trans: Since we came all this way, let's eat something delicious before heading back.

related.gloss: expressly, going out of one's way

meanings.note: Expresses a minimum consolation or hope.

examples.text: 少なくとも、私のパンはもうオーブンの中よ。
examples.trans: My bread is already in the oven, at least.

examples.text: せめてお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (at least).

meanings.note: causative suffix

examples.text: 女将は笑顔で客を安心させる不思議な力を持っている。
examples.trans: The proprietress has a wonderful way of putting guests at ease with her smile.

examples.text: 温かいゆず茶の香りが、長旅の疲れをふっと忘れさせてくれる。
examples.trans: The aroma of warm yuzu tea makes you forget the fatigue of a long journey.

meanings.note: Standard Japanese cue spoken right before lifting or pulling together.

examples.text: せーの、で一緒に重い雨戸を引きましょう！
examples.trans: On 'one, two', let's pull the heavy shutter together!

examples.text: せーの、で大きな木箱をテーブルに乗せました。
examples.trans: With a 'one, two!', we lifted the big wooden crate onto the table.

ぜ.gloss: rough sentence-final emphasis particle ('tell you what, let's!')

examples.text: これはぜです。
examples.trans: This is emphasis particle.

examples.text: あのぜを見ます。
examples.trans: I see that emphasis particle.

meanings.note: Warmly encourages an action or invitation.

examples.text: ぜひ手帳に書いてください！「三階のお湯、十点満点中十点」と！
examples.trans: Please write that down in your notebook! 'Third-floor hot water: ten out of ten!'

examples.text: ぜひお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (by all means).

そ.gloss: yeah, right (clipped そう); classical focus particle

examples.text: これさ、おそらく伝説の作品になるけど興味ある？
examples.trans: Listen, this is probably going to become a legendary work—interested?

examples.text: そ、そういうこと。最初からそう言えばよかったんだよ。
examples.trans: Yeah, that's right. You should have just said so from the start.

meanings.note: Alone means 'so'; after an adjective stem means 'looks like'; after a plain clause means 'reportedly'.

examples.text: まだ連絡はないそうです、和子さん。本当に申し訳ありません。
examples.trans: They have no word yet, Kazuko. I am truly sorry.

examples.text: 本当にいいんですか？とても素敵で暖かそう！
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and warm!

examples.text: おかげさまで、今夜はぐっすり眠れそうです。
examples.trans: Thanks to your kindness, I think I will sleep soundly tonight.

そう-様態.gloss: looking like, seeming about to (-sō appearance suffix)

examples.text: これはそう-様態です。
examples.trans: This is so.

examples.text: あのそう-様態を見ます。
examples.trans: I see that so.

meanings.note: Prenominal phrase meaning 'such / like that'.

examples.text: 家族の家と昔の思い出か……そういう喧嘩は傷が深いからな。
examples.trans: A family house and old memories... arguments like that cut deep.

examples.text: 受付で「そういう」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'そういう' (that kind of).

そうしたら.gloss: if so, in that case, and then

meanings.en: if so, in that case, and then
meanings.note: If that happens, or then.

examples.text: そうしたら、次はどうする？
examples.trans: If so, what do we do next?

examples.text: ボタンを押して、そうしたらドアが開く。
examples.trans: Press the button, and then the door will open.

meanings.note: To do so, to do that (referring to a previously mentioned action or an action obvious from context).

examples.text: 「窓を開けようか」「うん、そうして」
examples.trans: Shall I open the window? - Yeah, do that.

examples.text: そうすれば、問題は解決する。
examples.trans: If you do so, the problem will be solved.

そうなると.gloss: if that happens, in that case

meanings.en: if that happens, in that case, when it comes to that
meanings.note: Compound expression formed from そう (that way) + なる (to become) + と (conditional particle).

examples.text: そうなると思ったよ。
examples.trans: I knew it would turn out that way.

examples.text: そうなると、計画を最初からやり直すしかないな。
examples.trans: In that case, we have no choice but to redo the plan from scratch.

meanings.note: Demonstrative place pronoun near the listener or just mentioned.

examples.text: 陽翔さんが乾いたタオルを受け取った時に、そこへ置いたんだよ！
examples.trans: Haruto set it down there when he took the dry towel from me!

examples.text: 陽翔さん！そこに立っていたんですか！？
examples.trans: Haruto! Were you standing right there?!

meanings.note: Conjunction introducing a solution or next step based on the preceding situation.

examples.text: そこで新しい方法を試しました。
examples.trans: So, we tried a new method.

examples.text: そこでこの道具が役に立ちます。
examples.trans: That is where this tool comes in handy.

meanings.note: Connects sentences or events in sequence.

examples.text: 大工のおじいさん……そして鞄の中には小さな木の汽車！
examples.trans: A carpenter grandfather... and inside the bag, a small wooden train!

examples.text: そしてお二人とも、十二番地の一番大切な宝物をちゃんと守っていましたね。
examples.trans: And you two boys kept the very dearest treasure of Number twelve safe right here.

examples.text: そして美央さん、今日は金曜日……五日間の試用期間の最終日ですね。
examples.trans: And now, Mio, today is Friday—the final day of your five-day trial week.

examples.text: 余計な口出しすんなよ。そちらさんの問題なんだからよ。
examples.trans: Stay out of it—that's none of your business.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Describes two things looking exactly alike.

examples.text: 外側はそっくりです！でも中を見てください！
examples.trans: The outside looks identical! Still, look inside!

examples.text: そっくりお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (identical).

meanings.note: Casual counterpart of そちら.

examples.text: そっちはどう？
examples.trans: How are things on your end?

examples.text: そっちこそ気をつけろ。
examples.trans: You be careful too.

meanings.note: Describes careful, light movement that avoids noise or damage.

examples.text: 赤ちゃんが起きないように、そっとドアを閉めました。
examples.trans: I closed the door gently so as not to wake the baby.

examples.text: 古い紙を破らないように、そっと持ち上げてください。
examples.trans: Lift it gently so you do not tear the old paper.

meanings.note: Prenominal determiner pointing to something near the listener or in context.

examples.text: その通り！もうすっかりここの仲間だね。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in.

examples.text: あ、待ってください！その通りはここから歩いて五分の近所ですよ！
examples.trans: Oh, wait! That street is right in this neighbourhood, a five-minute walk from here!

examples.text: どうしてその人は、自分の鞄を受け取らずに逃げたんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why did that person run away without taking back their own bag?

meanings.note: Without changing state.

examples.text: はい、由香さん。たとえ兄がそのまま門を出て帰ってしまっても。
examples.trans: Yes, Yuka. Even if my brother turns right around and walks back out the gate.

examples.text: お二人とも！？湯呑みはそのままでいいから、今すぐ中へ来て！
examples.trans: Both of you?! Leave your teacups right there and come inside this very second!

そのもの.gloss: the very thing itself, exact match

meanings.en: the very thing itself, exact match
meanings.note: Follows a noun directly to mean 'that very thing / to the letter'.

examples.text: 市の規則の一言一句そのものです！
examples.trans: It matches every single word of the city rule!

examples.text: この温かい雰囲気は昔の旅館そのものです。
examples.trans: This warm atmosphere is the old inn itself.

meanings.note: Numbering expression ('rule number one').

examples.text: ルールその一。まず温かいお茶を飲んで、それからベルに出ること。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: 受付にその一があります。
examples.trans: There is number one at the reception desk.

meanings.note: The third item, part, or point in a series or sequence.

examples.text: ルールのその三、走らないこと。
examples.trans: Rule number three: no running.

examples.text: この物語のその三を読みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's read part three of this story.

meanings.note: The second item or part in a series or sequence.

examples.text: 対策その二を説明します。
examples.trans: I will explain countermeasure number two.

examples.text: 物語のその二は来週公開されます。
examples.trans: Part two of the story will be released next week.

meanings.note: Relational location noun: Xのそばで ('right beside X').

examples.text: 窓の向こう、ピアノのそばで先生が笑っています。
examples.trans: Beyond the window, the teacher is smiling beside the piano.

examples.text: ストーブのそばは暖かくて気持ちがいいですね。
examples.trans: Right beside the stove is warm and cosy.

meanings.note: Poetic and everyday compound combining mimetic そよ ('softly rustling') with 風 ('wind').

examples.text: 窓を大きく開けて、午後のそよ風が入ってきます……いつでもどうぞ、和子先生！
examples.trans: Windows wide open, afternoon breeze coming in—whenever you are ready, Kazuko!

examples.text: 開けた窓から春のそよ風が入って、白いカーテンが揺れています。
examples.trans: A gentle spring breeze comes in through the open window, swaying the white curtains.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of それは (sore wa), used to acknowledge an obvious consequence or react to what was just said.
Casual topic-marked pronoun phrase referring to a preceding statement or situation.

examples.text: そりゃ約束できねえな。
examples.trans: Well, I can't make any promises about not coming after you.

examples.text: そんな無茶な条件を出されたら、そりゃ断るわな。
examples.trans: If they hand you such unreasonable terms, well of course you'd turn them down.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun for something near the listener or just mentioned.

examples.text: おはよう。いや、まず取っ手を上げて、それから押すんだ。
examples.trans: Morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: 砂糖なしの紅茶をお願いします。それと温かいパンを一切れ。
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 俺は安全を確認しているだけだ。それが仕事だからな。
examples.trans: I am simply checking safety. That is my job.

meanings.note: Links sequential steps ('first..., then...').

examples.text: ルールその一。まず温かいお茶を飲んで、それからベルに出ること。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

examples.text: 受付で「それから」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'それから' (and then).

meanings.note: Indicates applying something to each item individually.

examples.text: 蝶番にそれぞれ二滴ずつ油を差しました。
examples.trans: I put two drops of oil on each of the hinges.

examples.text: テーブルにそれぞれ白いカップを並べましょう。
examples.trans: Let's set white cups out on each table.

meanings.note: Individual

examples.text: それぞれの意見。
examples.trans: Each opinion.

examples.text: それぞれの道を進む。
examples.trans: Go our separate ways.

meanings.note: Prompts the next part of a story or conclusion.

examples.text: なるほど！それで、これが鍵ですか？
examples.trans: Fair enough! And are these the keys?

examples.text: ああ、よかった！それで、明日の朝のシャワーやお湯はどうなりますか？
examples.trans: Thank goodness! And what about tomorrow morning's showers and hot water?

meanings.note: Formal/polite transition; contracts to それじゃ or じゃあ in casual speech.

examples.text: それでは始めましょう。
examples.trans: Well then, let's begin.

examples.text: それでは失礼します。
examples.trans: Well then, excuse me.

meanings.note: Concessive conjunction meaning 'even knowing that / anyway'.

examples.text: えっ……私からだとわかっていて、それでも来てくれたの？
examples.trans: Wait... you knew it was from me and came anyway?

examples.text: 受付で「それでも」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'それでも' (even so).

meanings.note: Adds another item naturally in conversation.

examples.text: それと見てください。この柔らかいウールのカーディガン、新品なんです。着てみてください。
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is brand new and unworn. Please try it on.

examples.text: ただの幸運だよ……それと月曜の朝の電車で入れ替わった青いスーツケースのおかげさ！
examples.trans: Pure luck... plus one blue suitcase swapped on Monday morning's train!

meanings.note: Used between two question alternatives ('A, or B?').

examples.text: 素敵ですね。窓は通り側ですか、それとも中庭側ですか？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street side or the courtyard side?

examples.text: 十九の理由ですか！？お兄さんを迎えるんですか、それとも電車の時刻表を読むんですか？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

examples.text: 九本目の真鍮の鍵ですか！？今夜開けますか、それとも朝まで待ちますか！？
examples.trans: A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight, or wait until morning?!

meanings.note: Highlights a surprising contrast with what preceded.

examples.text: それなのに水曜の夜、本名でここにチェックインしたの？
examples.trans: And yet Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?

examples.text: 受付で「それなのに」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'それなのに' (and yet).

meanings.note: conditional conjunction

examples.text: それなら私が行く。
examples.trans: In that case, I will go.

examples.text: それなら大丈夫だ。
examples.trans: If so, it's fine.

meanings.note: Adds an additional reason or observation.

examples.text: それに兄貴って生き物は、落ち着いて見せたい時は絶対に早く来ないもんだ。
examples.trans: Besides, big brothers never show up early when they want to look cool and calm.

examples.text: 受付で「それに」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'それに' (besides).

それる.gloss: to deviate, to turn away, to go astray

examples.text: 台風の進路がそれた。
examples.trans: The typhoon's course deviated.

examples.text: 話が横道にそれる。
examples.trans: The conversation goes off on a tangent.

meanings.en: to deviate, to turn away, to go astray

examples.text: ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: soon, before long, it is about time to
meanings.note: Indicates that the appropriate moment for an action or change of state has arrived.
Onomatopoeic adverb describing gradual, cautious movement.

examples.text: ご高説賜りたいが、これ以上パーティーがシラけるのも困る。そろそろよろしいかな？
examples.trans: Much as I'd love your lecture, I hate to let the party sour any further — shall we wrap this up?

examples.text: 池沢さん、そろそろ本題の要件を聞きたいですね。
examples.trans: Mr. Ikezawa, it's about time we heard what business you came to discuss.

そんな.gloss: such; that sort of; oh no

meanings.en: such; that sort of; oh no
meanings.note: Prenominal determiner ('that kind of') or dismayed exclamation.

examples.text: 月曜日の時点ではそんな臆病な計画でした……皆さんに出会うまでは。
examples.trans: On Monday that was my cowardly plan... until I met all of you.

examples.text: えっ……そんな。椅子はどこですか？膝の力が抜けてしまいました。
