examples.trans: What... oh no. Where is my chair? My knees just went weak.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of そんな.

examples.text: そんなに昔のことなのに、まだ覚えていらっしゃるんですか？
examples.trans: After all these years, you still remember that?

examples.text: そんなにお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (so much).

meanings.note: Warm, assertive masculine/veteran sentence-final particle.

examples.text: ほら、ちょうど今、門の前にタクシーが来たぞ。
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just pulled up at the gate right now.

examples.text: 横の持ち手に小さな紙の札が付いているぞ。
examples.trans: There is a small paper tag tied to the side handle.

examples.text: 見ろ、持ち手に白い封筒がテープで貼ってあるぞ。
examples.trans: Look, a white envelope is taped onto the handle.

meanings.en: I tell you!, yeah! (emphatic sentence-ending particle)
meanings.note: Elongated form of the sentence-final particle ぞ, used in exclamations of triumph, determination, or rallying cries.

examples.text: やったぞー！
examples.trans: I did it!

examples.text: さあ、これから本番だ、気合入れていくぞー！
examples.trans: Alright, this is the real take now—let's give it everything we've got!

examples.text: 今朝早く届いた小包をフロントの棚に置いておきました。
examples.trans: I placed the parcel that arrived early this morning on the front desk shelf.

examples.text: 窓を開けると、雨上がりの涼しい風が部屋に入ってきた。
examples.trans: When I opened the window, a cool breeze after the rain drifted into the room.

meanings.note: Desiderative auxiliary attaching to a verb's masu-stem and inflecting like an i-adjective.

examples.text: この看板がどう響くか聞いてみたいです。
examples.trans: I want to hear how this sign sounds.

examples.text: 焼きたてのレモンタルトを早く食べたいです。
examples.trans: I want to eat the freshly baked lemon tart soon.

meanings.note: Quantity noun/adverb meaning 'many' or 'plenty'.

examples.text: 端っこの一切れをたくさん焼いてちょうだいね！
examples.trans: Please bake plenty of corner slices!

examples.text: 受付にたくさんがあります。
examples.trans: There is a lot at the reception desk.

meanings.note: 手をたたく is 'clap your hands'; ドアをたたく is 'knock on a door'.

examples.text: 手を一回たたいてみてください。外の音がほとんど聞こえないでしょう？
examples.trans: Try clapping your hands once. You can hardly hear the street, can you?

examples.text: 子どもたちが手をたたいて笑いました。
examples.trans: The children clapped their hands and laughed.

meanings.note: Used for folding paper, clothes, or umbrellas.

examples.text: 今すぐその紙をたたんで、ポケットにしまってください。
examples.trans: Fold that paper right now and put it away in your pocket.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにたたみます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully fold.

meanings.note: With の means 'merely / nothing more than'.

examples.text: 健二さん、ただの小さな空気の泡だと言ってください！お願いです！
examples.trans: Kenji, please tell me it was only a tiny air bubble! Please!

examples.text: ただの幸運だよ……それと月曜の朝の電車で入れ替わった青いスーツケースのおかげさ！
examples.trans: Pure luck... plus one blue suitcase swapped on Monday morning's train!

meanings.note: Standard greeting spoken upon returning home or to one's office (short for ただいま帰りました).

meanings.en: just now, right now, at present
meanings.note: Written 只今; used as a temporal noun or adverb in formal or polite speech.

examples.text: ただいま。みんな随分変わったな。
examples.trans: I am home. You have all changed quite a bit.

examples.text: ただいま戻りました、社長。
examples.trans: I have just returned, President.

examples.text: 正直、撮影も、ただのお金目当てだったのに、うれしいんだ。
examples.trans: Honestly, I only came to the shoot for the money, yet I feel so happy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to people nouns or pronouns (お客さんたち 'the guests', 私たち 'we').

examples.text: 時計は七時二十九分だ。お客さんたちが階段を下りて来るぞ。
examples.trans: My watch says seven twenty-nine. The guests are coming down the stairs.

examples.text: ちょっと聞いてよ！本当は健二さんが私たちの二倍気になっているくせに！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Kenji is actually twice as curious as we are!

examples.text: 由香さん、私たちのために無理をしないでくださいね。
examples.trans: Yuka, please do not go to extra trouble on our account.

meanings.note: Emphasizes how small a number or time span is (たった三十日 'only thirty days').

examples.text: 新しい買い手が建物を調査するまで、猶予はたった三十日しかありません！
examples.trans: We only have thirty days before new buyers inspect the building!

examples.text: たったお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (only).

meanings.note: Emphatic 'just a moment ago / right this instant'.

examples.text: 急げよ……たった今、二階の階段から足音が聞こえたぞ！
examples.trans: Hurry up... I just heard footsteps on the second-floor stairs!

examples.text: たった今、郵便屋さんに受領のサインをしました。不動産管理室の赤い印鑑が押してあります。
examples.trans: I just signed for it from the postman. It bears a red stamp from the property office.

examples.text: 二人とも懐中電灯を持ってください！私の二週目は、たった今から始まりますよ！
examples.trans: Grab the flashlight, both of you! My second week starts right this second!

related.gloss: at any moment; on the verge of

examples.text: 時間はたっぷりあるから焦らなくていいよ。
examples.trans: We have plenty of time, so there's no need to rush.

examples.text: シロップをたっぷりかけてパンケーキを食べる。
examples.trans: Eat pancakes with plenty of syrup poured on top.

meanings.en: to stand up, to rise, to be established
meanings.note: Written 立つ; godan intransitive verb for physical standing, rising, or occupying a position.
Written 経つ; describes the passage of time (note: the homophonous form たった also functions as an adverb meaning 'only, merely').

examples.text: カメラの前に立つと、彼女の表情が一変した。
examples.trans: When she stood in front of the camera, her expression transformed completely.

examples.text: 東京に出てきてから、もう三年がたつ。
examples.trans: Three years have already passed since I came out to Tokyo.

related.gloss: to stand up, to rise to action

meanings.note: Pairs with 〜ても to mean 'even supposing that'.

examples.text: はい、由香さん。たとえ兄がそのまま門を出て帰ってしまっても。
examples.trans: Yes, Yuka. Even if my brother turns right around and walks back out the gate.

examples.text: たとえお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (even if).

meanings.note: Transitive verb. Used for paths, history, clues.

examples.text: 記憶をたどって昔の家を思い出した。
examples.trans: Tracing my memory, I recalled my old house.

examples.text: 森の中の小道をたどる。
examples.trans: Follow the path in the forest.

meanings.note: With に after a verb (間違えるたびに 'every time he made a mistake').

examples.text: もちろん！毎週金曜日、ピアノの音を間違えるたびに壁を見てむっとしていたわ。
examples.trans: Of course! Every Friday whenever he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.

examples.text: 受付にたびがあります。
examples.trans: There is each time at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb for a likely guess.

examples.text: 小さい箱が三つだけですよ！たぶん四つかな！
examples.trans: Only three small boxes! Maybe four!

examples.text: たぶんお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (probably).

meanings.note: With に, means 'occasionally / once in a while'.

examples.text: あっ！古いパイプには、夜たまに空気が入ることがあるんです。
examples.trans: Oh! Sometimes a little air gets into old pipes at night.

examples.text: 受付にたまがあります。
examples.trans: There is occasional at the reception desk.

meanings.note: With の and に (お客さんのために 'for the guests').

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 美央ちゃん、救世主だね！コーヒーマシンのためにまず牛乳をちょうだい。
examples.trans: Mio, you are a lifesaver! Hand me the milk first for the coffee machine.

examples.text: 由香さん、私たちのために無理をしないでくださいね。
examples.trans: Yuka, please do not go to extra trouble on our account.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning drop.

examples.text: 私は毎日たらす。
examples.trans: I drop every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒にたらす。
examples.trans: I drop together with them.

examples.text: いつかステーキたらふく食べたいですね。
examples.trans: Someday it would be nice to eat our fill of steak.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: This is used as a part meaning even.

examples.text: たり、行きます。
examples.trans: even, I will go.

examples.text: それはたりですね。
examples.trans: That is even, isn't it.

meanings.note: Plain-style counterpart of です after nouns and na-adjectives.

examples.text: おはよう。いや、まず取っ手を上げて、それから押すんだ。
examples.trans: Morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.

examples.text: 俺は健二だ。十分も早いね。
examples.trans: I am Kenji. You are a whole ten minutes early.

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Friendly masculine question ending after wh-words (誰からだい？).

examples.text: 誰からだい？週末の新しい予約か？
examples.trans: Who is calling? Another reservation for the weekend?

examples.text: 受付にだいがあります。
examples.trans: There is casual question marker at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Connects a reason to its consequence.

examples.text: だからあのタブレットは罠だと言ったんだ。
examples.trans: Told you that tablet is a trap.

examples.text: だから昨夜、屋根裏部屋で車の音を聞いていたんですね！
examples.trans: That explains why you listened for car sounds up in the attic last night!

meanings.note: Limits a quantity or scope without requiring a negative verb.

examples.text: いいえ、ペンと古いレシートが三枚だけです！
examples.trans: No, only a pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: ワンピースと楽譜と、お気に入りのティーカップだけですわ！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 残念ながら電話番号はありません。イニシャルが二つと、古い通りの名前だけです。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number. Only two initials and an old street name.

examples.text: どうしてうちに？うちはアダルトのメーカーだけど。
examples.trans: Why join our place? You know we're an adult video studio, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Foundational savory cooking stock (出し / 出汁) extracted from kelp, bonito flakes, mushrooms, or vegetables.

examples.text: うん！甘くなるまで三分炒めて、それから赤いレンズ豆と熱いだしスープを入れて。
examples.trans: Yes! Saute them three minutes until sweet, then add the red lentils and hot broth.

examples.text: 昆布と椎茸から取った温かいだしが、キッチンじゅうに香っています。
examples.trans: The warm broth made from kelp and shiitake mushrooms fills the whole kitchen with aroma.

meanings.note: Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.

examples.text: だったら俺が行くよ。
examples.trans: In that case, I'll go.

examples.text: 暇だったら手伝って。
examples.trans: If you're free, help out.

meanings.note: Casual conjunction giving an enthusiastic reason; after wh-words (いつだって) means 'anytime'.

examples.text: 私にはいつだって気軽にしてね！丁寧な言葉はお客さんのために残しておこう。
examples.trans: Keep it casual with me anytime! Save the stiff polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: だって、おいしいコーヒーと温かいパンがあれば仲良くなれるもん！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

だと.gloss: if it is; that it is

meanings.en: if it is; that it is
meanings.note: Copula だ + conditional/quotative particle と.

examples.text: 明日が雨だと、ピクニックは中止だ。
examples.trans: If it rains tomorrow, the picnic will be canceled.

examples.text: 彼は自分が一番だと信じている。
examples.trans: He believes that he is the best.

meanings.note: Na-adjective used to refuse permission or say something will not work.

examples.text: ぬれた手でスイッチにさわってはだめですよ。
examples.trans: You must not touch the switch with wet hands.

examples.text: 今日は雨だから、外のペンキぬりはだめですね。
examples.trans: Since it is raining today, painting outside is out of the question.

meanings.note: copula + particle

examples.text: 本当だよ。
examples.trans: It's true, you know.

examples.text: 君の番だよ。
examples.trans: It's your turn.

meanings.note: Attaches directly to nouns like ほこりだらけ ('full of dust').

examples.text: 昨日の九号室はほこりだらけでしたね。
examples.trans: Yesterday Room Nine was covered in dust.

examples.text: 庭仕事で手袋が土だらけになりました。
examples.trans: My gloves got covered in soil from gardening.

examples.text: ちくしょう、二万やられた！
examples.trans: Damn it, I just lost twenty thousand yen!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

ちまう.gloss: to end up doing, to do completely

meanings.en: to end up doing, to do completely (often with regret)
meanings.note: Rough, colloquial contraction of てしまう attached to verb stems; common in blunt or masculine speech.

examples.text: どうしてこうなっちまったんだ？
examples.trans: How on earth did you end up like this?

examples.text: また余計なことを言っちまったか。
examples.trans: Did I go and say too much again?

related.gloss: to do completely; to end up doing
to end up doing (casual contraction of てしまう)

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of ては after a verb te-form; frequently followed by いけない, ダメ, or たまらない to express prohibition or inevitability.

examples.text: ここで諦めちゃ、今までの苦労が水の泡だ。
examples.trans: If we give up here, all our hard work up to now will go down the drain.

examples.text: そんな大事なことを他の人に言っちゃダメだよ。
examples.trans: You mustn't go telling something that important to other people.

related.gloss: if, well then (contraction of では)

ちゃう.gloss: to end up doing, to finish doing

meanings.en: to end up doing, to do inadvertently or completely
meanings.note: Casual spoken contraction of てしまう; expresses completion of an action or an unintended result.

examples.text: こんな本を出したら犯罪になっちゃうよ。
examples.trans: If we publish a book like this, it'll end up being a crime.

examples.text: もう我慢できなくて、お母さんに全部言ってきちゃった。
examples.trans: I couldn't hold it in anymore and ended up telling Mom everything.

related.gloss: to finish doing; to do regrettably

meanings.note: Warm, friendly suffix used with first names or family terms.

examples.text: こんにちは！あなたが美央ちゃんね。キッチンの由香だよ。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Mio. I am Yuka from the kitchen.

examples.text: 大変！隆さん、美央ちゃん、キッチンがピンチだよ！
examples.trans: Oh no! Takashi, Mio, we have a kitchen crisis!

examples.text: 美央ちゃん、救世主だね！コーヒーマシンのためにまず牛乳をちょうだい。
examples.trans: Mio, you are a lifesaver! Hand me the milk first for the coffee machine.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb meaning 'safe and sound / properly'.

examples.text: おでこの上にちゃんとありましたね。
examples.trans: Right there safe and sound on your forehead.

examples.text: 電話を代われ、俺がちゃんと聞いてやる！
examples.trans: Hand me the phone, I will ask him properly!

examples.text: ほら、朝の騒ぎも謎の電話もちゃんと乗り切ったじゃない！
examples.trans: Look, you made it right through the morning rush and the mystery phone call!

meanings.en: called, known as, what you call
meanings.note: Colloquial and dialectal contraction of という (often realized as ちゅう or っちゅう), used to define or generalize a topic.

examples.text: 人間っちゅうのはな、ホントはみんな裏が見たいんだよ。
examples.trans: Human beings, deep down, all want to see what's hidden underneath.

examples.text: 世間ちゅうもんは、そう甘くはないぞ。
examples.trans: This thing called the real world isn't that forgiving, you know.

related.gloss: called, saying (colloquial contraction of という)

meanings.note: Warm, friendly request word in casual speech.

examples.text: 美央ちゃん、救世主だね！コーヒーマシンのためにまず牛乳をちょうだい。
examples.trans: Mio, you are a lifesaver! Hand me the milk first for the coffee machine.

examples.text: よく顔を見せてちょうだい、陽翔くん！ピアノよりずっと背が高くなったわね！
examples.trans: Let me get a proper look at you, Haruto! You grew much taller than the piano!

examples.text: 端っこの一切れをたくさん焼いてちょうだいね！
examples.trans: Please bake plenty of corner slices!

meanings.note: Traditional collapsible Japanese lantern hung outside inns and shops.

examples.text: 健二さん、正午のためにその紙ちょうちんを吊るしているんですか？
examples.trans: Kenji, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?

examples.text: 夕空に映える金色のちょうちんを見上げてごらんなさい……なんて穏やかなんでしょう！
examples.trans: Look up at the golden lanterns glowing against the evening sky... how peaceful!

meanings.note: Marks exact time or fit (七時ちょうど 'seven sharp', ちょうど今 'right now').

examples.text: ほら、ちょうど今、門の前にタクシーが来たぞ。
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just pulled up at the gate right now.

examples.text: ちょうど理想的です。階段はどこですか？
examples.trans: Just what I hoped for. Where are the stairs?

examples.text: 八時ちょうどです！お客さまが着きました！
examples.trans: Eight o'clock on the dot! Our guest has arrived!

meanings.note: Softens requests (ちょっと待って 'wait a moment') or means 'a bit'.

examples.text: あ、ちょっと待ってください！カフェから由香さんが手を振っています！
examples.trans: Oh, wait one moment! Yuka is waving from the café with an idea!

examples.text: ちょっと待って、美央ちゃん……どのバターを取って来たの？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Mio... which butter did you grab?

examples.text: ちょっと聞いてよ！本当は健二さんが私たちの二倍気になっているくせに！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Kenji is actually twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Pre-noun adjectival (連体詞) modifying a noun to indicate something small or casual.
Can also mean 'no small' or 'fairly impressive' depending on the noun modified (e.g., ちょっとした財産).

examples.text: 取引先とのちょっとしたすれ違いだ。
examples.trans: It's just a minor misunderstanding with our business partner.

examples.text: ちょっとした一言が、大きなトラブルに発展することがある。
examples.trans: A single offhand remark can sometimes blow up into major trouble.

related.gloss: a little, a bit, just a moment

ちる.gloss: to fall, to scatter, to disperse

meanings.en: to fall, to scatter (of blossoms or leaves); to disperse
meanings.note: Written 散る; godan intransitive verb (note: in casual speech, 〜んち 'someone's house', from のうち, is sometimes mis-lemmatized under ちる).
Used in the common idiom 気が散る (one's attention wanders).

examples.text: 周りがうるさくて気がちるから、少し静かにしてくれ。
examples.trans: The noise around here is distracting me, so please keep it down a bit.

examples.text: 強い風が吹いて、桜の花びらが一斉にちった。
examples.trans: A strong wind blew, and the cherry blossom petals scattered all at once.

related.gloss: one's house, one's place (contraction of のうち)

meanings.note: Colloquial sentence-final particle used when trying to recall a detail.

examples.text: ふたを磨いた時に壺の向きを変えましたっけ？
examples.trans: Did I turn the jars around when I polished the lids?

examples.text: 会議は水曜日の三時からでしたっけ？
examples.trans: Was the meeting starting at three on Wednesday?

meanings.en: is, am, are (colloquial contraction of です)
meanings.note: Slangy semi-polite copula ending used mainly by younger speakers or subordinates addressing seniors in a friendly, streetwise tone.

examples.text: どうも旦那、随分もうかってるみたいじゃないっすか。
examples.trans: Hey boss, business sure looks like it's booming for you!

examples.text: 何か上品なもの吸ってるじゃないっすか。一本下さいよ。
examples.trans: Look at you smoking classy cigarettes now — let me bum one.

meanings.note: Casual spoken equivalent of と ('saying') or という ('such a thing as').

examples.text: ちょっと待って……今、金曜日って言った！？
examples.trans: Hold on... did he just say Friday?!

examples.text: 弾き終わるといつも、「どうして雨の日はピアノの音が温かいの？」って聞くのよ。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he always asked, 'Why does the piano sound warmer on rainy days?'

meanings.en: adverbial or quoting particle with gemination (っ + と)
meanings.note: Appears at the end of emphatic mimetic or degree adverbs (such as ちっとも, じっと, ざっと) or as a casual self-directed particle when initiating an action (さてっと).

examples.text: 私の作品を販売したらダメですか？私じっとしてられないんです。
examples.trans: Can't you sell my film? I cannot just sit still and do nothing.

examples.text: さてっと、そろそろ次の撮影の準備に取りかかろうか。
examples.trans: Alright then, let's get started on preparations for the next shoot.

つ.gloss: counter for general items (one to nine)

meanings.note: counter for things

examples.text: お盆の上に温かい蒸しタオルを二つ並べておきました。
examples.trans: I placed two warm steamed towels side by side on the tray.

examples.text: 角砂糖を一つだけ紅茶に入れて、ゆっくりとかき混ぜた。
examples.trans: I put just one sugar cube into the black tea and stirred it slowly.

meanings.note: Marks a culmination, either long-awaited or inevitable.

examples.text: 悪い知らせだ。古いボイラーの真鍮の圧力バルブがついに壊れた。
examples.trans: Bad news. The brass pressure valve on the old boiler finally gave out.

examples.text: ついにお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (at last).

meanings.en: that, called, saying (colloquial contraction of という)
meanings.note: Often preceded by a small っ (っつう); used in rough or casual speech to quote hearsay or define a clause (っつうことだ 'which means that').
Written 通; a noun or suffix describing someone deeply knowledgeable about a field.

examples.text: この間歌舞伎町でうちの刑事が斬られたんだよ。犯人が台湾マフィアだっつうんだよ。
examples.trans: The other day one of our detectives got slashed in Kabukicho. They say the culprit is Taiwanese mafia.

examples.text: 人を左右するのはよりどころだからな。ここに救われている人間がそれだけいるっつうことだ。
examples.trans: What moves people is having something to lean on. It means that many people feel saved here.

つかまる.gloss: to hold on to, to grab on

meanings.en: to hold on to, to grab on
meanings.note: Godan verb taking に for what one holds on to for support.

examples.text: 危ないですから私の腕につかまってください！
examples.trans: It's unsteady, so grab onto my arm!

examples.text: 階段を降りる時は手すりにつかまってくださいね。
examples.trans: Hold onto the railing when going down the stairs.

つきあう.gloss: to accompany, to associate with, to date

meanings.en: to accompany, to go along with, to keep someone company
meanings.note: Written 付き合う; takes に for the person or activity one goes along with.

meanings.en: to socialize with, to date, to go out with
meanings.note: Takes と when referring to romantic dating or maintaining an ongoing social or business relationship.

examples.text: ちょっとつきあってくれないかな？
examples.trans: Could you keep me company for a little bit?

examples.text: いつも教会につきあってくれてありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for always coming along with me to church.

examples.text: 勝手に衛星にお金をつぎ込んで、勝手にヤクザに借金して、あげくの果てにみんなを売ったんだ！
examples.trans: You poured our money into satellite, borrowed from the yakuza, and in the end sold everybody out!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb for lights, electricity, or flames catching.

examples.text: 日当たりのいい古い屋根裏の書斎だ……急いでついて来い！
examples.trans: The sunny old attic study... follow me, quickly!

examples.text: 隣の小さな洗面所はどうですか？電気はつきますか？
examples.trans: What about the small washroom next door? Does the light turn on?

examples.text: よし、バーナーの火もついた。きれいな青い炎だ、これでいい。
examples.trans: Good, the burner lit too. A steady blue flame, right as it should be.

meanings.note: Transitive counterpart of つく; in 気をつける means 'be careful'.

examples.text: 気をつけてください、隆さん、ピッチャーの注ぎ口が広いです！
examples.trans: Be careful, Takashi, the pitcher spout is wide!

examples.text: その角の椅子は気をつけろ。十秒待って、今このネジを締めるから。
examples.trans: Watch out for that corner chair. Wait ten seconds while I tighten this screw.

examples.text: 曲がり角に気をつけろよ、壁にぶつけるな！
examples.trans: Watch the corner on the stairs, do not bump the wall!

examples.text: えっ？なんとかします。他の諸経費からつじつま合わせときます。
examples.trans: What? I'll make it work somehow. I'll balance the shortfall out of other expenses.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Intransitive Godan verb (つながる -> つながります -> つながらない -> つながった -> つながって).

examples.text: 新しい電線が箱までしっかりつながりました。
examples.trans: The new wire is firmly connected all the way to the box.

examples.text: この細い道は駅前の広場につながっています。
examples.trans: This narrow lane leads straight to the station square.

meanings.note: Nominalized stem of つなぐ ('to connect'); used for a musical/narrative transition or a culinary binder (like egg or flour).

examples.text: ピアノで二十八小節目に入るつなぎを弾きますから、聴いていてくださいね……
examples.trans: Listen while I play the transition into bar twenty-eight on the piano...

examples.text: 前半と後半のつなぎをもう一度ゆっくり弾いてみましょう。
examples.trans: Let's try playing the transition between the first and second halves slowly once more.

meanings.note: Used for cables, hands (手をつなぐ) and for bringing people together.

examples.text: 素敵ですね。三十年前から、この家は近所の人をつないでいたんですね。
examples.trans: How lovely. Even thirty years ago, this house was bringing neighbours together.

examples.text: 二人は手をつないで歩きました。
examples.trans: The two of them walked hand in hand.

examples.text: つばを飲み込む。
examples.trans: I swallowed my saliva.

examples.text: 日本刀のつばには美しい装飾がある。
examples.trans: The tsuba of a Japanese sword has beautiful decorations.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning trip.

examples.text: 私は毎日つまずく。
examples.trans: I trip every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒につまずく。
examples.trans: I trip together with them.

examples.text: 明日は休業です。つまり、誰も会社に来ません。
examples.trans: Tomorrow is a holiday. In other words, no one is coming to the office.

examples.text: つまり、君は私が間違っていると言いたいんだね。
examples.trans: So, you're trying to say that I am wrong, right?

meanings.note: After a plain verb, expresses what someone intended or thought they were doing.

examples.text: えっ、じゃあ受付の人に鞄を渡させて、通りの向こうから見守るつもりだったんですか！？
examples.trans: Wait—you were planning to let the clerk hand him the bag and watch from across the street?!

examples.text: えっ！窓から隆さんが見えましたか？私、二倍広く笑ったつもりだったのに！
examples.trans: Oh! Did you spot Takashi through the window? Here I tried smiling twice as wide!

meanings.note: Na-adjective (艶やか) describing a rich, healthy sheen on glazes, custards, hair, or polished wood.

examples.text: 見てください、黄色いレモンカードがとろっとつややかになりました！
examples.trans: Look how thick and glossy the yellow lemon curd just turned!

examples.text: 焼きたてのパンの表面にバターを塗ると、つややかできれいになります。
examples.trans: Brushing butter over freshly baked bread makes the surface glossy and pretty.

meanings.note: Compound of つる ('vine tendril') + 草 ('plant').

examples.text: 古い壁に沿って緑のつる草が伸びています。
examples.trans: Green climbing vines have grown along the old wall.

examples.text: つる草を切らずにそっと木枠へ移しました。
examples.trans: Without cutting the vine, we moved it gently onto the wooden frame.

meanings.en: called, that is; or rather (in つーか)
meanings.note: Casual spoken contraction of という; very common in the hedging expression つーか (from というか, 'or rather / I mean').

examples.text: まあ確かにな、幼い顔して大胆つーか。
examples.trans: Yeah, no kidding — innocent-faced yet astonishingly bold.

examples.text: あいつは真面目つーか、ただ融通が利かないだけなんだよ。
examples.trans: He's what you'd call serious—or rather, he's just plain inflexible.

related.gloss: or rather, I mean, how should I put it
called, saying (colloquial contraction of という)

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken variant of と in 何て言っている ('what is he saying?').

examples.text: 相手は何て言っている？どうして眉をひそめているんだ？
examples.trans: What is he saying? Why are you frowning?

examples.text: 受付で「て」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'て' (saying).

meanings.note: Rough phonological shift from 手前 (temae); used in angry, confrontational, or vulgar speech.
Also used reflexively in rough speech (e.g., てめえのことはてめえでやれ 'handle your own business yourself').

examples.text: てめえ、何すんだ！
examples.trans: Hey, what the heck are you doing!

examples.text: てめえら裏切りやがってよ！
examples.trans: You bastards betrayed us!

examples.text: 外で雨が降っても、中庭の縁側は静かで落ち着きます。
examples.trans: Even if it rains outside, the veranda facing the courtyard is quiet and peaceful.

examples.text: 何度読んでも、祖父の残した手紙には温かい言葉が詰まっている。
examples.trans: No matter how many times I read it, the letter my grandfather left behind is full of warm words.

てる.gloss: is doing, has done (colloquial contraction of -ている)

examples.text: これはてるです。
examples.trans: This is is doing.

examples.text: あのてるを見ます。
examples.trans: I see that is doing.

meanings.en: is doing, are doing (colloquial contraction of ているの / てるの)
meanings.note: Attached to the te-form of a verb before だ, だよ, じゃねえ, or か in fast, blunt spoken Japanese.

examples.text: 何撮ってんだよ？
examples.trans: What is it you're shooting here?

examples.text: いちゃもんつけてんじゃねえよ！
examples.trans: Quit picking a fight over nothing!

related.gloss: is doing (casual contraction of ている)

meanings.note: Marks the place where an action happens, the tool/means used, or a total (全部で).

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: ありがとうございます！ここでは下の名前で呼びますか？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we call each other by first names here?

examples.text: じゃあ、この宿が自分で挨拶しているんですね？
examples.trans: So the inn is saying hello on its own?

meanings.note: Colloquial i-adjective corresponding to 大きい; used for physical size, scale of business, or bold talk (でかい口を叩く).

examples.text: アダルトビデオ市場がでかくなればなるほど、夢も広がる。
examples.trans: The bigger the adult video market grows, the wider the dream expands.

examples.text: サナギの状態でも、こいつはでかくなるなってのが分かるようになる。
examples.trans: Even in the pupa stage, you learn to tell which ones are going to grow big.

できる.gloss: can do; be ready; be made

meanings.en: can do; be ready; be made
meanings.note: Expresses ability, completion, or something new coming into existence.

examples.text: 十分で往復できますか？
examples.trans: Can you run there and back in ten minutes?

examples.text: できました！青いラグもベッドの横にぴったりです。
examples.trans: All done! And the blue rug fits right beside the bed.

examples.text: いやあ、大切なお客さまにうちの大家さんの悩みを相談するなんてできません！
examples.trans: Oh, I could never trouble a valued guest with our landlord worries!

meanings.note: Polite presumptive form of copula だ; with rising intonation, seeks agreement.

examples.text: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
examples.trans: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.text: とても便利でしょう？
examples.trans: It's very convenient, isn't it?

meanings.note: Core polite sentence ending after nouns and adjectives.

examples.text: あ、開きました！ありがとうございます。新しい受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Mio, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 初日はいつも早く歩きます。パソコンはどこですか？
examples.trans: I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 紙の帳面ですか？本当に？
examples.trans: A paper ledger? Really?

meanings.note: Conversational conjunction warning playful or practical consequences if not done.

examples.text: 一切れ残してください、でないと台所に入れてもらえませんよ！
examples.trans: Save one slice, or else we won't be let back in the kitchen!

examples.text: 早く閉めましょう、でないと雨が吹き込みます。
examples.trans: Let's shut it quickly, or else the rain will blow in.

meanings.note: A combination of particles indicating a location, state, or context modifying a following noun.

examples.text: 海外での生活は楽しい。
examples.trans: Life abroad is fun.

examples.text: 会議での発言が注目された。
examples.trans: The remarks made in the meeting were noticed.

meanings.note: Polite transition opening a conclusion or next step (casual じゃあ).

examples.text: では、水曜日のカフェメニューはこれで決定ですね！
examples.trans: Well then, Wednesday's café menu is set!

examples.text: では、最初のページから一緒に読んでみましょう。
examples.trans: So then, let's read together from the first page.

meanings.note: At the start of a sentence, means 'however / still'.

examples.text: 四号室が空っぽの時でも、古い配線が勝手に二回鳴るの。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice on its own.

examples.text: 静かで快適でしたよ。でも今日、このスーツケースがとても重いんです。
examples.trans: It was quiet and pleasant, though this suitcase feels very heavy today.

でる.gloss: to go out, to appear, to come out

meanings.en: to go out, to leave, to come out
meanings.note: Written 出る; ichidan intransitive verb indicating movement out of an enclosed space or emergence.

meanings.en: to appear (in media or on stage), to be published, to be served
meanings.note: Used for appearing in a film or show (ビデオに出る), books coming out, or food and drinks being served.

examples.text: うちの新しいビデオに女優として出てみないか？
examples.trans: How would you like to appear as an actress in our new video?

examples.text: 結果が出るまで、まだしばらく時間がかかりそうだ。
examples.trans: It looks like it will still take some time before the results come out.

related.gloss: to take out, to put out, to publish
to appear in a performance or film

meanings.note: Connects nouns ('A and B'), marks a partner ('with'), quotes speech/thought, or marks a natural consequence ('when/whenever').

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 由香はこの通りのみんなと昔からの友達みたいに話すんだ。
examples.trans: Yuka talks with everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: だって、おいしいコーヒーと温かいパンがあれば仲良くなれるもん！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

meanings.note: Links a quote or name to a noun (という意味 'meaning that').

examples.text: あの、隆さんが言いたいのは……どのお客さまにも十点満点の気分を、という意味です！
examples.trans: Um, what Takashi means is... we hope every guest feels ten out of ten here!

examples.text: お兄さんというものをよく分かっていらっしゃいますね、健二さん。
examples.trans: You understand older brothers very well, Kenji.

meanings.note: そのとおりです means 'Exactly! / That is quite right!'.

examples.text: そのとおりです、真ん中からメロディーが上がります。
examples.trans: Exactly right—from the middle, the melody climbs.

examples.text: 健二さんが言ったとおりにしたらすぐ直りました。
examples.trans: When I did it just as Kenji said, it was fixed right away.

meanings.note: Gives casual examples.

examples.text: どうせ通りの雨戸を塗り替えるとか、退屈なお知らせだよ。
examples.trans: It is probably some boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

examples.text: 受付で「とか」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'とか' (such things as).

meanings.note: Colloquial phrase for vague overheard talk (どうとかいう).

examples.text: 中庭まで、バターがどうとかいう大声が聞こえたぞ。
examples.trans: I heard loud voices about butter all the way out in the courtyard.

examples.text: 受付で「とかいう」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'とかいう' (something about).

meanings.note: After a plain verb or noun + の: 十歳のとき = 'when I was ten'.

examples.text: 思い出しました！私が十歳のとき、おじはここを「冬のお茶の部屋」と呼んでいました！
examples.trans: Now I remember! When I was ten, my uncle called this 'the winter tea room'!

examples.text: 学生のとき、毎日自転車に乗っていました。
examples.trans: When I was a student, I rode my bike every day.

とく.gloss: to do in advance (contraction of ておく)

meanings.en: to do in advance, to leave as is (colloquial contraction of ておく)
meanings.note: Attaches to verb stems (e.g., 入っておけ → 入っとけ, 買っておく → 買っとく) to express preparation for the future or maintaining a state.

meanings.en: to untie, to solve, to dissolve
meanings.note: As an independent verb written 解く or 溶く.

examples.text: 危ないから、お前は中に入っとけ！
examples.trans: It's dangerous out here, so get inside and stay there!

examples.text: 明日の撮影に備えて、機材は全部車に積んどくよ。
examples.trans: I'll load all the equipment into the van in advance for tomorrow's shoot.

related.gloss: to do in advance; to leave in a state
voiced contraction of でおく (after ん/む/ぶ/ぐ)

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of ところ (所), very common in casual spoken Japanese.
Used figuratively for an attribute or quality (e.g., いいとこ, 'good point').

examples.text: バカかお前、こんなとこ泊まったら目立つだろ。
examples.trans: Are you an idiot? Staying somewhere like this will stand right out.

examples.text: よう。見た目の割には広くていいとこだろ？
examples.trans: Hey there. Surprisingly spacious and nice for how it looks outside, isn't it?

meanings.note: After past verb + ところ means 'just finished doing'; after te-iru means 'right in the middle of'.

examples.text: 健二さん、聞こえますか？今、緑の薬局を過ぎたところです！
examples.trans: Kenji, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

examples.text: おはようございます、和子さん！シナモンロールが今オーブンから出たところです。
examples.trans: Good morning, Kazuko! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

examples.text: ちょうど今、網の上で冷ましているところ！黄金色の皮に甘いレモンシュガーだよ！
examples.trans: Cooling on the rack right now! Golden crust and sweet lemon sugar!

meanings.note: Marks capacity, role, or purpose (プロとして 'as professionals').

examples.text: いいえ美央さん、プロとして正直に言いましょう！当館は『大阪旅行ガイド』を尊敬しています！
examples.trans: No, Mio, let's speak honestly as professionals! Our inn deeply respects the Osaka travel guide!

examples.text: 「物件売却のお知らせ。中庭八番館を、商業オフィス用として売却いたします。」
examples.trans: 'Notice of Property Sale: Number Eight Courtyard Building is offered for commercial office sale.'

examples.text: 商業オフィスとして売却！？私たちの旅館とキッチンを灰色の事務所にする気！？
examples.trans: Commercial office sale?! Turning our inn and kitchen into grey offices?!

meanings.note: Emphatic conversational variant of とても, with the geminate consonant (っ) adding warmth or strong feeling.

examples.text: とってもおいしそう。
examples.trans: That looks absolutely delicious.

examples.text: 今日はとっても楽しかったよ、ありがとう。
examples.trans: I had such a great time today, thank you.

meanings.note: Clear, standard intensifier before adjectives.

examples.text: 静かで快適でしたよ。でも今日、このスーツケースがとても重いんです。
examples.trans: It was quiet and pleasant, though this suitcase feels very heavy today.

examples.text: 中庭側です。大きな木のすぐ上で、とても静かですよ。
examples.trans: The courtyard side. Right above the big tree, and it is very quiet.

examples.text: 本当にいいんですか？とても素敵で暖かそう！
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and warm!

meanings.note: Moves focus to practical immediate action.

examples.text: とにかく、あの鞄は鍵をかけて大切に保管しておきます。
examples.trans: For now, we will keep that bag safely under lock and key.

examples.text: とにかくお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (anyway).

meanings.note: Attaches to numbers like 二人とも / 二つとも ('both of them').

examples.text: お二人とも、どうもありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both very much.

examples.text: 真鍮のバルブ、両方とも見つけたわよ、健二さん！息を整える？とんでもない！
examples.trans: Here are both brass valves, {M1}! Catch my breath? Never!

examples.text: そしてお二人とも、十二番地の一番大切な宝物をちゃんと守っていましたね。
examples.trans: And you two boys kept the very dearest treasure of Number twelve safe right here.

meanings.note: Culinary texture mimetic (擬態語) for liquids thickening into a rich, velvety consistency or semi-melted cheese/custard.

examples.text: 見てください、黄色いレモンカードがとろっとつややかになりました！
examples.trans: Look how thick and glossy the yellow lemon curd just turned!

examples.text: 弱火でゆっくり混ぜると、カスタードがとろっと甘く仕上がります。
examples.trans: When you stir slowly over low heat, the custard finishes thick, silky, and sweet.

examples.text: お礼なんてとんでもない、困った時はお互い様ですよ。
examples.trans: Do not even mention thanking me—we all help each other out when in need.

examples.text: 朝早くからとんでもない大雨が降り出して驚きました。
examples.trans: I was surprised when an unthinkable downpour started early in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday question word asking about state or method.

examples.text: 中のティーカップはどうですか？割れていませんか？
examples.trans: How is your teacup inside? Is it still unbroken?

examples.text: 中庭まで、バターがどうとかいう大声が聞こえたぞ。
examples.trans: I heard loud voices about butter all the way out in the courtyard.

examples.text: 外は雨ですし、この通りのホテルはどこも満室です！どうしましょう？
examples.trans: It is raining outside and every hotel on this street is full! What shall we do?

meanings.note: Combines どう (how) + いう (say); どういうこと means 'what does this mean?'.

examples.text: どういうことだ？
examples.trans: What is the meaning of this?

examples.text: どういう意味ですか。
examples.trans: What does it mean?

meanings.note: Everyday conversational word for 'why'.

examples.text: どうして鏡に眼鏡が……あ！頭の上にあります！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in the mirror... oh! They are on top of my head!

examples.text: どうしてその人は、自分の鞄を受け取らずに逃げたんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why did that person run away without taking back their own bag?

examples.text: どうして金曜まで、靴や木の汽車を知らない宿に預けるんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why leave your shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?

どうしても.gloss: no matter what, by all means

meanings.en: by all means, at any cost, really
meanings.note: Expresses strong determination, insistence, or desire in affirmative sentences.

meanings.en: no matter how hard one tries, under no circumstances
meanings.note: Used with negative or impossibility predicates (e.g., どうしても無理, 'impossible no matter what').

examples.text: どうしても無理ですかね？
examples.trans: Is there really no way it can be done?

examples.text: 本日どうしてもご紹介したい人がいまして、ご挨拶だけでも…
examples.trans: I brought someone I really want to introduce today, even just a quick hello...

related.gloss: at all costs, no matter what

meanings.note: how to handle a situation

examples.text: 雨が降ってきたけど、どうする？
examples.trans: It started raining, what should we do?

examples.text: これからどうするつもりですか。
examples.trans: What do you plan to do from now on?

meanings.note: Dismissive or resigned expectation.

examples.text: どうせ通りの雨戸を塗り替えるとか、退屈なお知らせだよ。
examples.trans: It is probably some boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

examples.text: どうせお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (probably anyway).

どうぞ.gloss: please; go ahead; here you are

meanings.en: please; go ahead; here you are
meanings.note: Warmly invites someone in, offers a seat, or hands something over.

examples.text: どうぞ座ってください、和子さん。今すぐ名札を確認しましょう。
examples.trans: Please sit down, Kazuko. Let's check the luggage tag right away.

examples.text: どうぞ、和子さん。温かいミントティーと蜂蜜です。
examples.trans: Here you are, Kazuko: hot mint tea and honey.

examples.text: レジから五千円どうぞ。領収書をもらって来てくださいね！
examples.trans: Here is five thousand yen from the cash box. Please bring back a receipt!

meanings.note: Intensifies polite thanks (どうもありがとうございます).

examples.text: お二人とも、どうもありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both very much.

examples.text: どうもお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (very much).

meanings.note: Everyday question phrase asking about method or means.

examples.text: この重いテーブルをどうやって運びますか？
examples.trans: How shall we carry this heavy table?

examples.text: 駅までどうやって行くか教えてください。
examples.trans: Please tell me how to get to the station.

meanings.en: in accordance with, just as, following, the same way as
meanings.note: Voiced suffix form of 通り (とおり) attached directly to nouns or verb stems (e.g., 思いどおり 'as one wishes', 今までどおり 'as before').

examples.text: 思いどおりにはいかないもんだ。
examples.trans: Things rarely go the way you want them to.

examples.text: 今までどおり、持ちつ持たれつだ。
examples.trans: Just like always — you scratch my back and I scratch yours.

どかす.gloss: to move out of the way

meanings.en: to move out of the way, to clear aside, to shift
meanings.note: Transitive godan verb (kanji: 退かす), paired with the intransitive verb どく ('to step aside').

examples.text: トシ、ちょっと椅子をどかそうか。
examples.trans: Toshi, let's move the chairs out of the way for a second.

examples.text: 邪魔になるから、通路の荷物をどかしておいてくれ。
examples.trans: It'll get in the way, so clear the luggage out of the aisle.

related.gloss: to step aside, to move out of the way
to tidy up, to clear away

meanings.note: Onomatopoeia for a racing heartbeat from nerves or excitement.

examples.text: 心臓がどきどきします！美央さん、落ち着いて正直に説明してください！
examples.trans: My heart is pounding! Mio, please explain it calmly and honestly!

examples.text: どきどきお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (pounding).

meanings.note: Question pronoun for place; どこも means 'everywhere'.

examples.text: 初日はいつも早く歩きます。パソコンはどこですか？
examples.trans: I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: ちょうど理想的です。階段はどこですか？
examples.trans: Just what I hoped for. Where are the stairs?

examples.text: 小さいスプーンとナプキンはどこに置きますか？
examples.trans: Where should I place the small spoons and napkins?

meanings.note: This is used as a noun meaning somewhere.

examples.text: これはどこかです。
examples.trans: This is somewhere.

examples.text: そのどこかを見せてください。
examples.trans: Please show me the somewhere.

どこからも.gloss: from nowhere (with negative), from everywhere (with positive)

examples.text: どこからも返事が来ない。
examples.trans: No reply comes from anywhere.

examples.text: この山はどこからも見える。
examples.trans: This mountain can be seen from everywhere.

meanings.en: from nowhere (with negative), from everywhere (with positive)

examples.text: 鍵がどこにもない。
examples.trans: The keys are nowhere to be found.

examples.text: あんな美人はどこにもいない。
examples.trans: There is no beauty like her anywhere.

meanings.note: Emphasizes that reality goes far beyond what was asked.

examples.text: 知っているどころか！六年間、毎週金曜日にあの木の階段を上ってピアノを教えました！
examples.trans: Know it? Every Friday for six years I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

examples.text: 受付で「どころか」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'どころか' (far from).

meanings.note: Polite selector between two choices (coffee or tea, left or right).

examples.text: 改めておはようございます、和子さん！コーヒーと紅茶、どちらになさいますか？
examples.trans: Good morning again, Kazuko! Would you prefer coffee or black tea?

examples.text: いいえ、どちらもありません！静かな天井の梁を気に入って、お礼を言ってくれました。
examples.trans: Neither! He loved the quiet ceiling beams and thanked us.

examples.text: はい！左に細い道が二本あります。どちらを行けばいいですか？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two narrow lanes on the left. Which one should I take?

meanings.note: This is used as a pron meaning which way.

examples.text: どっち、行きます。
examples.trans: which way, I will go.

examples.text: それはどっちですね。
examples.trans: That is which way, isn't it.

meanings.note: Respectful counterpart of 誰.

examples.text: ひび一つありません！どなたが届けてくださったんでしょう？
examples.trans: Not a single crack! Who could have brought it back?

examples.text: 受付で「どなた」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'どなた' (who).

meanings.note: Prenominal question word directly before a noun.

examples.text: ちょっと待って、美央ちゃん……どのバターを取って来たの？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Mio... which butter did you grab?

examples.text: あの、隆さんが言いたいのは……どのお客さまにも十点満点の気分を、という意味です！
examples.trans: Um, what Takashi means is... we hope every guest feels ten out of ten here!

meanings.note: This is used as a adv meaning how long.

examples.text: それはとてもどのくらいです。
examples.trans: It is very how long.

examples.text: もっとどのくらいしてください。
examples.trans: Please do it more how long.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun in the こ・そ・あ・ど demonstrative series (これ・それ・あれ・どれ).

meanings.en: any one, whichever, all of them (with でも or も)
meanings.note: Combines with particles like でも to mean 'any of them' or 'whichever one'.

examples.text: どれがご入り用だい？
examples.trans: Which one do you need?

examples.text: はい。どれでもあるよ。
examples.trans: Sure, we have whichever one you want.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic adverb for rapid progression.

examples.text: 私、緊張すると文がどんどん長くて堅苦しくなってしまうんです！
examples.trans: Whenever I get nervous, my sentences grow longer and stiffer!

examples.text: どんどんお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (steadily).

meanings.note: Prenominal question word asking about qualities or type.

examples.text: そうだ、部屋が変わるお詫びに、どんな割引をしましょうか？
examples.trans: Wait—to apologise for changing rooms, what discount should we offer?

examples.text: お前は一体、どんな魔法みたいな旅館に迷い込んだんだ？
examples.trans: Just what kind of magical inn did you wander into, little brother?

どんなに.gloss: how very; how much; no matter how

meanings.en: how very; how much; no matter how
meanings.note: Degree adverb used in exclamations ('how effortlessly!') or concessive clauses with -ても ('no matter how...').

examples.text: 後半が前半からどんなに自然に流れているか聞こえる、陽翔さん？
examples.trans: Hear how effortlessly the second half flows from the first, Haruto?

examples.text: このサンルームが再び開いて、和子先生がどんなに嬉しいか分かりますよ。
examples.trans: I can tell just how happy Kazuko is that this sunroom is open again.

meanings.note: Links na-adjectives to nouns (静かな部屋), forbids after plain verbs (動くな 'don't move'), or muses at sentence end.

examples.text: 大きな茶色い紳士靴が二足と、灰色のセーターだな。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

examples.text: いいじゃないか。出す前に、この新鮮な緑のハーブを上に乗せなよ。
examples.trans: Sounds good. Put these fresh green herbs on top before serving.

examples.text: 誰かが中庭の鉢植えを世話しないといけないからな。
examples.trans: Somebody has to look after the potted plants in the courtyard.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: 今日は暑いなあ。
examples.trans: Man, it's hot today.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。
examples.trans: Must be nice, I'm jealous.

meanings.note: Plain negative of ある; なし means 'without' (砂糖なし 'without sugar').

examples.text: まだ連絡はないそうです、和子さん。本当に申し訳ありません。
examples.trans: They have no word yet, Kazuko. I am truly sorry.

examples.text: 金曜日まで？名前も署名もないじゃないか！
examples.trans: Until Friday? There is no name and no signature!

examples.text: 千円、百円、二百円。一円も狂いなくぴったりです。ありがとう！
examples.trans: One thousand, one hundred, two hundred yen. Exact to the very last yen—thank you!

meanings.note: Written 中々; indicates that something is better or more impressive than expected.

meanings.en: not easily, not readily (with negative verb)
meanings.note: With a negative predicate, indicates that something takes a long time or considerable effort to happen.

examples.text: なかなかかわいい絵本ですね。
examples.trans: That's quite a cute picture book, isn't it?

examples.text: 親御さんが毎年送ってきて、これがなかなかうまいんですよ。
examples.trans: Their parents send this tea every year, and it's really quite delicious.

meanings.note: Attaches to verb stems for simultaneous actions (走りながら) or 残念ながら ('unfortunately').

examples.text: 残念ながら電話番号はありません。イニシャルが二つと、古い通りの名前だけです。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number. Only two initials and an old street name.

examples.text: 二十ミリ、真鍮、ボイラーのバルブ……走りながらずっと唱えます！
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve... I will repeat it the whole way!

meanings.note: short for nakereba naranai

examples.text: 行かなきゃ。
examples.trans: I gotta go.

examples.text: やらなきゃ。
examples.trans: I have to do it.

meanings.note: Lose an object such as keys or glasses; S1 also writes it 失くす.

examples.text: 隆さん、「はい」って言って！また眼鏡をなくす前に！
examples.trans: Say yes, Takashi! Before you lose your glasses again!

examples.text: 駅で傘をなくしました。
examples.trans: I lost my umbrella at the station.

meanings.note: Godan verb from 無い + なる (なくなる -> なくなります -> なくならない -> なくなった -> なくなって).

examples.text: 人気のパンはお昼の前にすぐなくなります。
examples.trans: Popular bread sells out quickly before noon.

examples.text: 机の上の鉛筆がいつのまにかなくなりました。
examples.trans: The pencil on the desk disappeared before I knew it.

meanings.note: Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to form a firm but polite command.

examples.text: 早く寝なさい。
examples.trans: Go to sleep early.

examples.text: 二人ともやめなさい！
examples.trans: Both of you, stop it!

meanings.note: Respectful counterpart of する used with guests (どちらになさいますか 'which would you like?').

examples.text: 改めておはようございます、和子さん！コーヒーと紅茶、どちらになさいますか？
examples.trans: Good morning again, Kazuko! Would you prefer coffee or black tea?

examples.text: いいえ、お気になさらないでください！陽翔さまですね。
examples.trans: Not at all, please do not worry! You must be Haruto.

examples.text: 夕空に映える金色のちょうちんを見上げてごらんなさい……なんて穏やかなんでしょう！
examples.trans: Look up at the golden lanterns glowing against the evening sky... how peaceful!

meanings.note: Used after a noun (Xなしで 'without X') to mark absence.

examples.text: 砂糖なしの温かい紅茶を一杯ください。
examples.trans: One cup of hot black tea without sugar, please.

examples.text: 地図なしで古い通りを歩くのは楽しいです。
examples.trans: Walking the old streets without a map is fun.

なじむ.gloss: to sink in, blend in, settle nicely

meanings.en: to sink in, blend in, settle nicely
meanings.note: Godan verb used when oil penetrates metal or flavours meld.

examples.text: 油が蝶番になじむまで十秒待ちましょう。
examples.trans: Let's wait ten seconds until the oil works into the hinge.

examples.text: 新しい椅子がもう部屋の空気にすっかりなじんでいます。
examples.trans: The new chairs already blend right into the room.

meanings.en: why, how come, for what reason
meanings.note: Standard interrogative adverb (kanji: 何故), slightly more formal or direct than なんで or どうして.

examples.text: 恵美ちゃんは、なぜビデオに出演したいの？
examples.trans: Megumi, why do you want to appear in an adult video?

examples.text: なぜうちを？
examples.trans: Why come to us?

meanings.note: Na-adjective for smooth motion, texture, or sound.

examples.text: ドのハンマーがなめらかに上がって弦を打ちます。
examples.trans: The C hammer rises smoothly and strikes the strings.

examples.text: 温かいスープがとてもなめらかでおいしいです。
examples.trans: The warm soup is wonderfully smooth and delicious.

meanings.en: to lick, to lap, to wash over
meanings.note: Ichidan verb (kanji: 舐める / 嘗める); used literally for the tongue or figuratively for waves or flames lapping at a surface.

meanings.en: to underestimate, to look down on, to mess with
meanings.note: Very common colloquial idiom (e.g., なめるなよ, 'don't underestimate me / don't mess with me').

examples.text: 荒波にもまれて方々にぶつかって、なめられてできたこのきれいなフォルム、非常にセクシーでございましょ？
examples.trans: Tossed by rough waves and licked smooth millions of times into this lovely form—isn't it remarkably sexy?

examples.text: 俺たちをなめると痛い目を見るぞ。
examples.trans: If you underestimate us, you're going to regret it.

related.gloss: to lick; to look down on

meanings.note: Conditional particle highlighting a topic ('if it's paper...').

examples.text: 心配しないで！冷たい炭酸水なら、オレンジジュースがすぐ落ちますよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes orange juice right out.

examples.text: 受付で「なら」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'なら' (if it is).

meanings.note: Takes に after nouns/na-adjectives and -く after i-adjectives (温かくなる 'grow warm').

examples.text: まあ、ありがとう、由香さん。びっくりして手が冷たくなっていたの。
examples.trans: Oh, thank you, Yuka. My hands had turned cold from the surprise.

examples.text: 木の汽車のことで緊張だと？一時間ごとに話が妙になるな。
examples.trans: Nervous over a wooden toy train? This story grows stranger every hour.

examples.text: ちょっと聞いてよ！本当は健二さんが私たちの二倍気になっているくせに！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Kenji is actually twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: なるべく早く来てください。
examples.trans: Please come as early as possible.

examples.text: なるべく丁寧な言葉を使う。
examples.trans: Use the politest words possible.

meanings.note: Shows understanding and agreement with someone's explanation.

examples.text: なるほど！それで、これが鍵ですか？
examples.trans: Fair enough! And are these the keys?

examples.text: なるほど！自分の名前を書いたら、頑固な兄貴が来ないと思ったんだな！
examples.trans: Aha! You figured if you signed your own name, your stubborn big brother would stay home!

meanings.note: Potential form of なる (仲良くなれる 'can become good friends').

examples.text: だって、おいしいコーヒーと温かいパンがあれば仲良くなれるもん！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいになれます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully can become.

meanings.en: what, what kind of; how many
meanings.note: Pronoun 何 (なん), the euphonic form of なに used before t, d, and n sounds or counters.

meanings.en: it is that..., the thing is... (in なんだ)
meanings.note: In casual speech, なんだ is a contraction of なのだ (adnominal copula な + explanatory particle の + copula だ), used to state a reason or emphasis.

examples.text: 自由と秩序のバランスがいいからなんだ。
examples.trans: It's because there's a good balance between freedom and order.

examples.text: うち、今から仕事なんだからさ。そこ邪魔なの。
examples.trans: I have to go to work right now, so you're in the way there.

meanings.note: Casual particle downplaying or expressing emotion toward a noun.

examples.text: 当たり前だろ。どうして謎のメモなんかに隠れたんだ？
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

examples.text: 受付で「なんか」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'なんか' (things like).

meanings.note: Describes a hard-to-pinpoint feeling.

examples.text: 不思議ですね！あの名札の字、なんだか見覚えがあったんです。
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt strangely familiar to me.

examples.text: なんだかお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (somehow).

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, modesty, or emphatic dismissal.

examples.text: 私は二十八センチの靴なんて履きませんわ！
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear twenty-eight centimetre shoes!

examples.text: 大阪の最初の夜に、お部屋で寂しく過ごすなんて駄目ですよ！
examples.trans: You cannot spend your first evening in Osaka feeling lonely upstairs!

examples.text: 朝のコーヒーの前に、大変なんて言わないでください！
examples.trans: Please do not say the word crisis before my morning coffee!

なんてことだ.gloss: Oh my god!; What a thing!

meanings.en: Oh my god!; What a thing!
meanings.note: exclamation of surprise

examples.text: なんてことだ、財布を忘れた。
examples.trans: Oh my god, I forgot my wallet.

examples.text: なんてことだ、信じられない。
examples.trans: What a thing, I can't believe it.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで遅れたの？
examples.trans: Why were you late?

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。
examples.trans: How come you know?

meanings.note: Exclamatory adverb before adjectives or nouns.

examples.text: なんと大変な間違いでしょう！眼鏡をかけて名札を見ますね。
examples.trans: What a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and read the tag.

examples.text: なんとお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (what a...!).

examples.text: 私はどうしようもない男なんです。自分一人じゃなーんにもできない。
examples.trans: I am a hopeless man. All by myself I cannot do a single thing.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Core particle marking static location (with ある/いる), destination, recipient, or specific point in time.

examples.text: おはようございます！すみません、ドアに鍵がかかっていますか？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: ああ、部屋は八室、真鍮の鍵も八つだ。今日は四号室にお客さんが来る。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: ルールその一。まず温かいお茶を飲んで、それからベルに出ること。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.

meanings.note: Covers pleasant food/flower scents as well as general smells.

examples.text: キッチンからコーヒーのいいにおいがします。
examples.trans: A wonderful smell of coffee is coming from the kitchen.

examples.text: 雨のあとの土のにおいが好きです。
examples.trans: I love the smell of earth after rain.

meanings.note: Na-adjective for cheerful bustle and activity.

examples.text: ええ。表の大通りはにぎやかなのに、この中庭では葉っぱと鳥の声だけが聞こえます。
examples.trans: Yes. The main street out front is lively, yet inside this courtyard you only hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: 大阪で一番にぎやかで静かな場所……ひだまり旅館に乾杯！
examples.trans: To the liveliest quiet place in Osaka... cheers to the Hidamari Inn!

meanings.note: Mimetic adverb used with する for a happy, silent smile.

examples.text: 二階の踊り場から隆さんがにこにこしています。
examples.trans: Takashi is beaming down from the second-floor landing.

examples.text: ピアノの前で和子さんがにこにこ笑っています。
examples.trans: Kazuko is smiling warmly in front of the piano.

にっこり.gloss: beamingly; with a warm, silent smile

meanings.en: beamingly; with a warm, silent smile
meanings.note: Mimetic adverb (擬態語) describing a bright, affectionate smile breaking across someone's face; often paired with 笑う or 微笑む.

examples.text: ミントティーを一杯全部飲んで、レモンタルトを最後のひとかけらまで食べて、にっこり笑いました！
examples.trans: She drank a whole cup of mint tea, ate every crumb of lemon tart, and smiled!

examples.text: 美央さんがにっこり笑って、旅のお客様に部屋の鍵を渡しました。
examples.trans: Mio smiled warmly and handed the room key to the traveling guest.

meanings.note: Compound topic/subject-matter particle attached directly to a noun (Nについて話す/聞く/考える).

examples.text: おめでとうございます、隆さん！担当者の方は九号室について何とおっしゃいましたか？
examples.trans: Congratulations, Takashi! What did the clerk say about Room Nine?

examples.text: 金曜日のお茶会のメニューについて、由香さんと相談しました。
examples.trans: I talked with Yuka about the menu for Friday's tea gathering.

meanings.note: Marks the person for whom something holds meaning (私にとって 'for me').

examples.text: 小さい頃、二つ先の通りに。金曜日は……私にとって大切な日なんです。
examples.trans: When I was small, two streets over. Friday is... an important day for me.

examples.text: 受付で「にとって」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'にとって' (for).

meanings.note: Marks legal authority, cause, or means (条例によって 'under the bylaw').

examples.text: 市の条例によって、旅館の賃貸契約はあと十年間しっかり守られます！
examples.trans: Under city bylaw, your inn's lease is firmly protected for another ten years!

examples.text: 受付で「によって」という言葉をよく使います。
examples.trans: At the front desk we often use 'によって' (by).

meanings.note: Everyday culinary vegetable (人参), usually written in hiragana.

examples.text: スープに入れるにんじんを細かく刻みます。
examples.trans: We chop the carrots finely for the soup.

examples.text: 甘いにんじんとレンズ豆の温かいスープです。
examples.trans: It is a warm soup of sweet carrots and lentils.

meanings.note: Paint a wall, spread butter, put on cream.

examples.text: 六日でガラスを洗って、雨戸をぬって、レモンタルトを焼く！
examples.trans: Six days to wash the glass, paint the shutters and bake lemon tarts!

examples.text: パンにバターをぬって食べます。
examples.trans: I spread butter on bread and eat it.

meanings.note: Describes bathwater, tap water, or tea that isn't hot enough.

examples.text: ラジエーターを触ってみてください。下は温かいのに、上が冷たくなっています。
examples.trans: Feel the radiator—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: 今日はとてもぬるいですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very lukewarm, isn't it?

meanings.note: Gentle warm water ideal for washing glass or hands.

examples.text: ぬるま湯にスポンジを浸して窓を拭きました。
examples.trans: I dipped the sponge in warm water and wiped the windows.

examples.text: ぬるま湯で洗うと古い陶器も傷みません。
examples.trans: Washing in warm water keeps old pottery safe too.

meanings.note: Sentence-final particle inviting shared agreement or softening a request.

examples.text: 俺は健二だ。十分も早いね。
examples.trans: I am Kenji. You are a whole ten minutes early.

examples.text: 紙なら、停電になっても使えるからね。
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.

examples.text: こんにちは！あなたが美央ちゃんね。キッチンの由香だよ。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Mio. I am Yuka from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Friendly attention-getter at the start of a remark.

examples.text: ねえ陽翔さん、本当に正午に中庭で大輝さんを迎えるのね？
examples.trans: Hey Haruto, so you are really staying in the courtyard to greet Daiki at noon?

examples.text: ねえ、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Hey — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Metal screw used in woodwork and electrical fixtures.

examples.text: 小さい真鍮のねじを二本しめました。
examples.trans: I tightened two small brass screws.

examples.text: ゆるんだ椅子のねじをドライバーで直しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's fix the loose chair screw with a screwdriver.

ねる.gloss: to sleep, to lie down; (as ねって) right? [quote]

meanings.en: to sleep, to go to bed, to lie down
meanings.note: Ichidan verb 寝る (ねる); homophonous with the godan verb 練る ('to knead; to polish a plan').

meanings.en: right?, okay? (followed by quotative って)
meanings.note: In casual dialogue like 帰ってきてねってさ, ねって is the sentence-ending particle ね plus the quoting particle って ('said to...'), which resembles the te-form of ねる.

examples.text: いつでも帰ってきてねってさ。
examples.trans: She told you to come back anytime.

examples.text: 昨日は遅くまで編集していたから、少し寝るよ。
examples.trans: I was editing until late last night, so I'm going to get some sleep.

related.gloss: to sleep, to go to bed
to knead; to work out (a plan)

meanings.note: This is used as a part meaning explanatory.

examples.text: ねん、行きます。
examples.trans: explanatory, I will go.

examples.text: それはねんですね。
examples.trans: That is explanatory, isn't it.

meanings.note: Links nouns (紙の帳面 'paper ledger'), stands in for 'one' (誰の 'whose'), or softens casual statements/questions.

examples.text: あ、開きました！ありがとうございます。新しい受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Mio, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 紙の帳面ですか？本当に？
examples.trans: A paper ledger? Really?

meanings.note: Casual explanatory question ending (plain form + のか), common in male/brotherly speech.

examples.text: 金曜日の夜まで大阪に残るのか！？
examples.trans: You're staying in Osaka until Friday night?!

examples.text: もう全部一人で片付けたのか？
examples.trans: Did you tidy up the whole thing by yourself already?

meanings.note: A colloquial sentence-ending particle used to ask a question, often expecting an explanation.

examples.text: もう帰るのかい？
examples.trans: Are you going home already?

examples.text: それが君の答えなのかい？
examples.trans: Is that your answer?

meanings.note: Godan verb (覗く) for looking through a window or down from a landing.

examples.text: 二階の踊り場から中庭をのぞいてみました。
examples.trans: I peered down into the courtyard from the upstairs landing.

examples.text: ロビーの窓から外をそっとのぞきました。
examples.trans: We peeked quietly outside through the lobby window.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
examples.trans: She is definitely coming, right?

examples.text: ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Polite, objective clause connector giving a smooth reason.

examples.text: はい、ここです！全部で三千八百円だったので、おつりは千二百円です。
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost three thousand eight hundred yen, so the change is twelve hundred yen.

examples.text: 暖かい毛布がありますし、今夜のお風呂はもう済ませたので大丈夫ですよ。
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, and I already washed up tonight, so I am fine.

meanings.note: Connects clauses where the outcome goes against expectation.

examples.text: 隆さん！七号室はもう埋まっているのに、七号室にもう一人予約が入っています！
examples.trans: Takashi! Room seven is already occupied, and a second guest is booked into room seven!

examples.text: ラジエーターを触ってみてください。下は温かいのに、上が冷たくなっています。
examples.trans: Feel the radiator—the bottom is warm, while the top is turning cool.

examples.text: 氷みたいに冷たいシャワー！？三階に『大阪旅行ガイド』の調査員がいるのに！？
examples.trans: Ice-cold showers?! With the Osaka Travel Guide inspector on the third floor?!

のね.gloss: right?, I see, so it's that...

examples.text: 明日は休みじゃないのね。
examples.trans: So you aren't off tomorrow, huh.

examples.text: そういうことだったのね。
examples.trans: So that's what it was.

meanings.en: right?, I see, so it's that...

examples.text: これ、すごく美味しいのよ。
examples.trans: This is really delicious, you know.

examples.text: 私は行かないのよ。
examples.trans: I'm not going, just so you know.

meanings.note: Pronounced ワ; sets the topic ('as for X') or contrasts two items.

examples.text: 俺は健二だ。十分も早いね。
examples.trans: I am Kenji. You are a whole ten minutes early.

examples.text: 初日はいつも早く歩きます。パソコンはどこですか？
examples.trans: I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 引き出しの中だよ。ここではこの大きな紙の帳面と鉛筆を使う。
examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Audible breath of relief or amazement.

examples.text: 市の条例によって、旅館の賃貸契約はあと十年間しっかり守られます！
examples.trans: Under city bylaw, your inn's lease is firmly protected for another ten years!

examples.text: はあ、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Gasp — nice weather again today!

はい.gloss: yes; here you go; hello (on phone)

meanings.en: yes; here you go; hello (on phone)
meanings.note: Polite affirmative reply, prompt when handing something over, or answering the desk phone.

examples.text: おはようございます！はい、受付はきれいですし、鍵も揃っています。
examples.trans: Good morning! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.

examples.text: はい、二階の四号室ですね！電車の旅はいかがでしたか？
examples.trans: Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?

examples.text: はい、ここです！全部で三千八百円だったので、おつりは千二百円です。
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost three thousand eight hundred yen, so the change is twelve hundred yen.

meanings.note: Repeated はい, used to reassure someone or casually acknowledge what they said.

examples.text: はいはい、分かりました。
examples.trans: Yes, yes, I understand.

examples.text: はいはい、任せとけ。
examples.trans: Yeah, yeah, leave it to me.

meanings.note: Standard word for a postal card (kanji 葉書).

examples.text: 木箱の中からはがきが一枚見つかりました。
examples.trans: A postcard was found inside the wooden chest.

examples.text: 旅先から祖母へ季節のはがきを送りました。
examples.trans: I sent a seasonal postcard to my grandmother from my trip.

はき違える.gloss: to misunderstand, to get the wrong idea

meanings.en: to misunderstand, to get the wrong idea about, to confuse
meanings.note: Ichidan compound verb (kanji: 履き違える); literally 'to put on the wrong footwear', used figuratively for misinterpreting a principle like freedom or authority.

examples.text: 村西、自由をはき違えるなよ。
examples.trans: Muranishi, don't get the wrong idea about what freedom means.

examples.text: 自由をはき違えたかな。
examples.trans: Maybe I misunderstood what freedom really is.

related.gloss: to misunderstand, to make a mistaken assumption

meanings.note: A structure consisting of two side pieces joined by a series of rungs or steps, used for climbing up or down.

examples.text: 屋根に上るためにはしごをかける。
examples.trans: Put up a ladder to get on the roof.

examples.text: 消防車が長いはしごを伸ばした。
examples.trans: The fire engine extended a long ladder.

meanings.note: Set phrase used only the very first time you meet someone.

examples.text: はじめまして、由香さん。すごくいい匂いですね！
examples.trans: Nice to meet you, Yuka. Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: はじめまして、今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.trans: Nice to meet you — nice weather again today!

meanings.note: Expresses logical expectation based on known facts.

examples.text: いいところに気づいたな、美央。陽翔さんなら毎週、市の建築規則を読んでいるはずだ。
examples.trans: Sharp catch, Mio. Haruto must read municipal building rules every single week.

examples.text: 受付にはずがあります。
examples.trans: There is supposed to at the reception desk.

examples.text: パンにはちみつを塗る。
examples.trans: I spread honey on the bread.

examples.text: 喉が痛いので、はちみつを舐めた。
examples.trans: My throat hurts, so I licked some honey.

meanings.note: Hearing or seeing sharply and unmistakably.

examples.text: はっきり聞こえるぞ。小さな石の噴水の横に立っているか？
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you standing beside the small stone fountain?

examples.text: はっきりお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (clearly).

examples.text: 自分の意見をはっきりと伝える。
examples.trans: Express one's opinion clearly.

examples.text: 遠くの山がはっきりと見える。
examples.trans: The distant mountains can be seen distinctly.

meanings.note: Light, cheerful laugh in conversation.

examples.text: はは、白いシャツには一滴もついていませんよ！
examples.trans: Ha, not a single drop got on my white shirt!

examples.text: はは、また額に眼鏡を乗せていましたね。
examples.trans: Haha, you had your glasses on your forehead again.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb for a screw, lid, or piece clicking cleanly into place.

examples.text: 一回、二回……見ろ、新しい真鍮のネジ山が気持ちよくはまったぞ。
examples.trans: One turn, two turns... look how cleanly the new brass threads fit.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにはまります。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully fit snugly into place.

meanings.en: be in fashion; spread; be prevalent
meanings.note: Godan verb used for trends, songs, or things happening frequently.

examples.text: 今この曲がはやっています。
examples.trans: This song is popular right now.

examples.text: 最近風邪がはやっているみたいです。
examples.trans: It seems a cold is going around lately.

meanings.en: all right!, okay!, got it!, coming!
meanings.note: Elongated, projecting variant of はい, used to call attention on a film set or to answer someone cheerfully.

examples.text: はーい、カット！すばらしかったぞ。
examples.trans: All right, cut! That was magnificent.

examples.text: はーい、ただいま行きますので少々お待ちください。
examples.trans: Coming! I'll be right there, so please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.

examples.text: 安ければ買います。
examples.trans: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Affectionate, casual form of おばあちゃん (婆ちゃん); also used warmly to address or refer to an elderly woman.

examples.text: おばあちゃん、パパが帰ってきたよ。
examples.trans: Grandma, Dad is back home!

examples.text: うちのばあちゃんが作った漬物は世界一うまいんだ。
examples.trans: The pickles my grandma makes are the best in the world.

meanings.note: Written 倍; used as a noun meaning 'double' or as a counter suffix for multiples (e.g., 二倍 'twice as much').

meanings.en: should, had better (in ～ばいい / ～ばいけない)
meanings.note: In conditional expressions like 作ればいい ('should make') or 守っていかなければいけません ('must protect'), ばい spans the conditional particle ば and the start of いい or いけない.

examples.text: 恵美もそろそろ恋人ぐらい作ればいいのに。ちょっと奥手すぎるんじゃない？
examples.trans: It's high time you got yourself a boyfriend too — aren't you being way too shy?

examples.text: 今月は先月の倍の売り上げを達成したぞ。
examples.trans: This month we achieved double last month's sales!

meanings.note: I-adjective.

examples.text: そんなばかばかしい話は信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe such an absurd story.

examples.text: ばかばかしくて聞いていられない。
examples.trans: It's so ridiculous I can't keep listening.

meanings.note: Indicates focusing repeatedly on one thing (時計ばかり見ている 'keep looking at your watch').

examples.text: バターを少しだけお願いします。……隆さん、どうして時計ばかり見ているんですか？
examples.trans: Just a little butter, please. ...Takashi, why do you keep looking at your watch?

examples.text: 小さな灰色の数字ばかりですよ！一枚目で心臓が止まってしまいました！
examples.trans: It is nothing except tiny grey numbers! My heart stopped at page one!

examples.text: 観光客が馬車に乗っている。
examples.trans: Tourists are riding in a horse-drawn carriage.

examples.text: 昔は馬車が主な交通手段だった。
examples.trans: In the past, carriages were the main means of transportation.

meanings.note: Lively colloquial adverb meaning everything is in top shape.

examples.text: 先週、新しい電球に替えたし、石鹸もお湯もばっちりだ。
examples.trans: I put in a new lightbulb last week, and soap and hot water are all set.

examples.text: ばっちり清潔です、隆さん！眼鏡もおでこじゃなくてちゃんと鼻の上にありますよ。
examples.trans: Spotless and sharp, Takashi! Even your glasses are on your nose instead of your forehead.

ぱ.gloss: geminated bound morpheme (-ppa / -pa, as in いっぱい)

examples.text: 回線がいっぱいでね。
examples.trans: All of our satellite lines are already full.

examples.text: 両手いっぱいに荷物を抱えて階段を上った。
examples.trans: She climbed the stairs with both arms full of luggage.

ひ.gloss: day, sun (日); fire (火); verb stem hi-

examples.text: ウソじゃないよ。お前は風邪ひくんじゃないよ。
examples.trans: It's not a lie. Don't you go catching a cold.

examples.text: 冬の晴れた日は、中庭の石畳まで暖かくなる。
examples.trans: On sunny winter days, even the courtyard flagstones grow warm.

meanings.note: Written 贔屓; frequently used in the polite set greeting どうぞごひいきに ('Thank you for your continued patronage / Please show me your favor').
Used with する to mean showing special favor or bias toward someone.

examples.text: 麗華です。どうぞごひいきに。
examples.trans: I'm Reika. I look forward to your kind patronage.

examples.text: 特定の俳優ばかりをひいきするのはよくない。
examples.trans: It's not good to play favorites with only certain actors.

meanings.note: Used in 眉をひそめる ('furrow one's brow').

examples.text: 相手は何て言っている？どうして眉をひそめているんだ？
examples.trans: What is he saying? Why are you frowning?

examples.text: 毎日ていねいにひそめます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully knit.

meanings.note: Sunny courtyard inn in Osaka where Mio works alongside Takashi, Kenji, and Yuka.

examples.text: ひだまり旅館へようこそ、美央。二日目も退屈しないぞ。
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hidamari Inn, Mio. Your second day won't be boring either.

examples.text: はい、ひだまり旅館でございます！受付の美央です。
examples.trans: Hello, Hidamari Inn! This is Mio at reception.

examples.text: いいえ、「金曜日の正午、祖父の物がひだまり旅館で待っている」とだけ書きました。
examples.trans: No, I only wrote, 'Friday at noon, something of Grandfather's is waiting at Hidamari Inn.'

examples.text: お願いします。革命だよ、革命。ひっくり返すんだよ。
examples.trans: We're counting on you. It's a revolution—we're going to turn the whole industry upside down!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

ひとかけら.gloss: one small piece; a single fragment; a cube/crumb

meanings.en: one small piece; a single fragment; a cube/crumb
meanings.note: Native compound combining ひと- ('one') + かけら ('fragment, chip, small piece'); used both literally (a cube of butter, a crumb) and figuratively.

examples.text: すぐ火から下ろして！冷たい無塩バターをひとかけら混ぜて！
examples.trans: Off the flame immediately! Stir in one cold cube of unsalted butter!

examples.text: 焼きたてのパンが美味しすぎて、お皿にひとかけらも残りませんでした。
examples.trans: The freshly baked bread was so delicious that not a single crumb was left on the plate.

meanings.note: Native counter phrase combining ひと ('one') and さじ ('spoon').

examples.text: 温かい紅茶に蜂蜜をひとさじ入れました。
examples.trans: I put one spoonful of honey into my hot tea.

examples.text: スープに塩をほんのひとさじ足してください。
examples.trans: Please add just a tiny spoonful of salt to the soup.

ひとつまみ.gloss: a pinch (of salt, sugar, or spice)

meanings.en: a pinch (of salt, sugar, or spice)
meanings.note: Compound of ひと ('one') + つまみ ('pinch between thumb and two fingers').

examples.text: 焼く前に清潔なスプーンでひとつまみ味見します。
examples.trans: Before baking, we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon.

examples.text: 甘い生地に海塩をひとつまみ加えると味が引き立ちます。
examples.trans: Adding a pinch of sea salt to sweet dough brings out the flavour.

ひと続き.gloss: one continuous whole; an unbroken stretch

meanings.en: one continuous whole; an unbroken stretch
meanings.note: Native compound (一続き) joining ひと- ('one') and 続き ('continuation, sequence').

examples.text: 三十年離れていても、ひと続きのワルツですね。
examples.trans: Thirty years apart, one continuous waltz.

examples.text: 中庭と九号室は、ガラスの扉を開けるとひと続きの空間になります。
examples.trans: When you open the glass doors, the courtyard and Room Nine become one continuous space.

meanings.note: Strong i-adjective for a harsh review or bad situation.

examples.text: あと三十五分です！ひどい一つ星の口コミを書かれてしまいます！
examples.trans: Thirty-five minutes left! He will write a terrible one-star review!

examples.text: 今日はとてもひどいですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very terrible, isn't it?

ひねる.gloss: to twist, to sprain; to turn (a knob)

meanings.en: to twist, to sprain; to turn (a knob)
meanings.note: Godan verb (捻る) used both for twisting an ankle and turning taps.

examples.text: 踏み台を降りる時に足首を少しひねりました。
examples.trans: I slightly twisted my ankle stepping off the stool.

examples.text: 古い蛇口をゆっくり右へひねってください。
examples.trans: Turn the old tap slowly to the right.

meanings.note: Fine crack in porcelain, glass, or wood.

examples.text: ひび一つありません！どなたが届けてくださったんでしょう？
examples.trans: Not a single crack! Who could have brought it back?

examples.text: 受付にひびがあります。
examples.trans: There is crack at the reception desk.

examples.text: 壁にひび割れができている。
examples.trans: There is a crack in the wall.

examples.text: 乾燥でかかとにひび割れができた。
examples.trans: Cracks formed on my heels due to dryness.

び.gloss: voiced bound suffix -bi (-日 'day', -火 'fire', たび 'each time')

examples.text: 再生されるたびに新鮮で、いわば永遠の処女でございます。
examples.trans: Every time the tape is played I am fresh and alive—in other words, I am an eternal virgin.

examples.text: 記念日には毎年、家族でこの宿に泊まります。
examples.trans: Every year on our anniversary, our family stays at this inn.

meanings.note: Expressive mimetic compound (びしょ + 濡れ) for wet sleeves or hair.

examples.text: 急な雨でシャツの袖がびしょ濡れです！
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves are soaking wet from the sudden rain!

examples.text: タオルをどうぞ、肩がびしょ濡れですよ。
examples.trans: Here's a towel—your shoulders are dripping wet.

meanings.note: Pairs with する (びっくりする 'be startled').

examples.text: まあ、ありがとう、由香さん。びっくりして手が冷たくなっていたの。
examples.trans: Oh, thank you, Yuka. My hands had turned cold from the surprise.

examples.text: デシベルのことで一晩じゅう慌てていたなんて、隆さんが聞いたらびっくりするよ！
examples.trans: Takashi will be stunned when he hears he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: 北風がびゅうと吹く。
examples.trans: The north wind blows with a whoosh.

examples.text: 風がびゅうびゅうと音を立てている。
examples.trans: The wind is making a howling sound.

meanings.note: Mimetic word for a gleaming surface; ぴかぴかの床 = 'a sparkling floor'.

examples.text: 一、二……わあ！黒くて、ぴかぴかの木です！
examples.trans: One, two... wow! Dark, shiny wood!

examples.text: 新しい車はぴかぴかです。
examples.trans: The new car is sparkling.

meanings.note: Matches an amount, spot, or purpose to perfection.

examples.text: 千円、百円、二百円。一円も狂いなくぴったりです。ありがとう！
examples.trans: One thousand, one hundred, two hundred yen. Exact to the very last yen—thank you!

examples.text: できました！青いラグもベッドの横にぴったりです。
examples.trans: All done! And the blue rug fits right beside the bed.

examples.text: 全然構いません！窓の下の広い机も、私の仕事にぴったりです。
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

examples.text: 髪にぴんを留める。
examples.trans: Fasten a pin in the hair.

examples.text: コルクボードにぴんを刺す。
examples.trans: Stick a pin into a corkboard.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeia for pulling bedsheets or posture taut (ぴんと張る).

examples.text: シーツの角をぴんと張ってね、美央ちゃん！柔らかい枕を二つ置くよ。
examples.trans: Pull the sheet corner tight, Mio! Here go the two soft pillows.

examples.text: ぴんとお茶を飲みましょう。
examples.trans: Let's drink tea (taut).

meanings.note: Breath exhaled in relief after finishing a rush job.

examples.text: ふう、雨が強くなる前に全部運べましたね！
examples.trans: Whew, we carried everything inside before the rain got heavy!

examples.text: ふう、熱いお茶を飲んで少し落ち着きました。
examples.trans: Phew, a sip of hot tea helped me settle down.

examples.text: やはり村西さんが社長にはふさわしいんじゃないかと。
examples.trans: Honestly, I think you are the one best suited to be president, Mr. Muranishi.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: The lid of a box, pot or bottle.

examples.text: カチッと鳴りました！健二さん、木のふたを開けてください！
examples.trans: It clicked! Kenji, please open the wooden lid!

examples.text: ふたに気をつけて。何十年も閉まっていましたから。
examples.trans: Careful with the lid. It has been closed for decades.

examples.text: 鍋のふたを開けてください。
examples.trans: Please take the lid off the pot.

meanings.note: Two people; a pair or couple.

examples.text: ふたりで映画を見に行った。
examples.trans: The two of us went to see a movie.

examples.text: 彼らはとても仲の良いふたりだ。
examples.trans: They are a very close pair.

meanings.note: Gentle, warm laugh.

examples.text: ふふ、朝七時の温かいシナモンパンを断る人なんていませんわね。
