examples.text: やっぱりワインは赤ですね。ご令嬢もいかがですか？
examples.trans: When it comes to wine, red really is best. Would you care for some, madam?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: I-adjective for red tags, umbrellas, or stamps.

examples.text: 私の鞄には、上のポケットに赤いリボンが入っていると伝えてください！
examples.trans: Please tell them my bag has a red ribbon inside the top pocket!

examples.text: 私のスーツケース！上のポケットを開けますね……ああ、赤いリボンです！
examples.trans: My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, my red ribbon!

examples.text: 牛乳を三本、卵を二十個、バターとチーズと赤いりんご！
examples.trans: Three cartons of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

examples.text: いや、監督も今走り回ってますから。
examples.trans: Look, the director is running all over town right now trying to fix this.

examples.text: 走り回ってるんじゃなくて逃げ回ってるんだろ！
examples.trans: He's not running around working—he's running away!

meanings.note: Godan verb (はしる -> はしります -> はしらない -> はしった -> はしって).

examples.text: ええっ！走っていたから、包みが全部同じに見えました！
examples.trans: Oh no! Because I was running, all the wrappers looked identical!

examples.text: 座って、美央ちゃん！今朝は町じゅう走ったんだから、コーヒーを飲んで。
examples.trans: Sit down, Mio! You ran all across town this morning, so drink some coffee.

examples.text: 二十ミリ、真鍮、ボイラーのバルブ……走りながらずっと唱えます！
examples.trans: Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve... I will repeat it the whole way!

meanings.note: Ichidan verb for getting out of bed or events occurring.

examples.text: 急いで走れよ、美央。四号室は七時十五分に起きるぞ！
examples.trans: Run fast, Mio. Room four wakes up at seven fifteen!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに起きます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully wake up.

meanings.note: Transitive partner of 起きる ('wake up').

examples.text: じゃあ、由香さんのカフェも和子さんのピアノも、上のお客さまを起こしませんか？
examples.trans: So Yuka's café and Kazuko's piano won't wake the guests upstairs?

examples.text: 明日の朝、六時に起こしてください。
examples.trans: Please wake me up at six tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: To occur, take place, or come into existence.

examples.text: 予期せぬ問題が起こった。
examples.trans: An unexpected problem occurred.

examples.text: 地震が起こった時のために備える。
examples.trans: Prepare for when an earthquake happens.

examples.text: ビザ詐欺の容疑で逮捕しておいて、古い法律で起訴してるんですよ。
examples.trans: They arrested him on visa fraud suspicions, then indicted him under an archaic law.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: でもみんな村西さんを超えてかなきゃダメなんですって！
examples.trans: Still, everyone needs to surpass Mr. Muranishi!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: あの作品を超えるのはそう簡単じゃありません。
examples.trans: Surpassing that debut film of ours won't be easy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 監督の村西だ。今回の作品は悪の組織と戦う超大作だ。
examples.trans: I'm Director Muranishi. This film is a blockbuster about fighting an evil organization.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Suffix meaning 'through the window / over the counter'.

examples.text: 美央ちゃん、ガラス越しに見て！二人が木の下で向かい合って立っているよ！
examples.trans: Mio, look through the glass! The two of them are standing face to face under the tree!

examples.text: 受付に越しがあります。
examples.trans: There is across at the reception desk.

examples.text: 伸ばしちゃいました。これね、三田村君の趣向で。
examples.trans: We stretched it right out—this one comes from our young director's own taste.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 先代の趣味だ。生き物が好きな人でな。
examples.trans: It was my predecessor's hobby. He was a man who loved living creatures.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Core native noun (あし).

examples.text: もう一つの椅子に足を乗せておいてください。
examples.trans: Please keep your foot propped up on the second chair.

examples.text: 床に足をつけるのは今夜は厳禁ですよ。
examples.trans: Touching your foot to the floor is strictly forbidden tonight.

meanings.note: Transitive Godan verb (足す -> 足します -> 足さない -> 足した -> 足して).

examples.text: 白いミルク入れも一つ足して包んでもらいましょう。
examples.trans: Let's add one white milk jug too and have them wrapped.

examples.text: ポットに熱いお湯をもう少し足してください。
examples.trans: Please add a little more hot water to the pot.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb taking が ('have enough chairs/flour').

examples.text: 乾いているし、暖かいし、静かだ。さあ、足りない物を言ってみろ。
examples.trans: It is dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに足ります。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully be enough.

examples.text: のれん分けってのは信用に足る店かどうかの目安になるからな。
examples.trans: A proper branch pedigree serves as a reliable measure of whether an establishment can be trusted.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Area around one's feet ('watch your step').

examples.text: 待てよ。足元の石段を見てごらん。
examples.trans: Hold on. Look down at the stone step.

examples.text: 受付に足元があります。
examples.trans: There is at one's feet at the reception desk.

examples.text: 大雪で空港で足止めを食った。
examples.trans: We were stranded at the airport due to heavy snow.

examples.text: 警察は犯人の足止めを図った。
examples.trans: The police tried to block the suspect's movement.

examples.text: 給料は取っ払いで足跡がないから、正直難しいですよ。
examples.trans: Since wages were paid in cash with no paper trail, frankly it will be difficult.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Sound of someone walking.

examples.text: 急げよ……たった今、二階の階段から足音が聞こえたぞ！
examples.trans: Hurry up... I just heard footsteps on the second-floor stairs!

examples.text: 受付に足音があります。
examples.trans: There is footsteps at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Native anatomical compound 足 ('foot') + 首 ('neck/narrow joint'), read あしくび.

examples.text: 足首の外側をちょっとひねっただけです。
examples.trans: I just twisted the outside of my ankle slightly.

examples.text: 腫れた足首を冷たいタオルで優しく冷やしました。
examples.trans: She gently cooled the swollen ankle with a cold towel.

examples.text: 水たまりを跨いで歩く。
examples.trans: To walk stepping over puddles.

examples.text: 国境を跨ぐ問題。
examples.trans: An issue that crosses international borders.

meanings.note: Quiet side lane paved with stone.

examples.text: 狭い路地じゃなくて、花屋の横の二番目の道を行け。
examples.trans: Not the cramped alley—take the second street beside the flower shop.

examples.text: 受付に路地があります。
examples.trans: There is alley at the reception desk.

examples.text: こっちは踊りに恋して、客の視線をこの体で受け止めてきたんだ。
examples.trans: I fell in love with dance and have met the audience's gaze head-on with this body.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Platform halfway up a staircase.

examples.text: 階段を上がって、踊り場を左に曲がった一番奥のドアだ。
examples.trans: Go up the stairs, turn left at the landing, and it is the farthest door.

examples.text: 受付に踊り場があります。
examples.trans: There is stair landing at the reception desk.

examples.text: おお、すばらしい劇場だ！伝説の踊り子、先生に習えば必ず光り輝ける。
examples.trans: What a magnificent theater! Learning under a legendary dancer, you will all surely shine.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: これまでどれだけ信じてたか分かってますか？それ全部踏みにじったんですよ。
examples.trans: Do you understand how deeply she trusted you all this time? You trampled over every bit of it!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 未知の世界に足を踏み入れる。
examples.trans: To step into an unknown world.

examples.text: この森には誰も足を踏み入れたことがない。
examples.trans: No one has ever set foot in this forest.

examples.text: でも最初の一歩を踏み出すのは難しいですよね。私もそうでした。
examples.trans: Still, taking that very first step is hard, isn't it? It was the same for me.

examples.text: 誰にでも一歩踏み出すべき時には、今だってお知らせが来るの。
examples.trans: For everyone, when it's truly time to take a step forward, a notice arrives saying now is the moment.

meanings.note: Compound of 踏み ('stepping on') + 台 ('stand'), read ふみだい.

examples.text: 一番上の棚に届くように木の踏み台を使いました。
examples.trans: She used a low wooden stepstool to reach the top shelf.

examples.text: 手を伸ばす間、その木の踏み台をしっかり押さえますね。
examples.trans: While you reach up, let me hold that wooden stool steady.

examples.text: どんなに威勢のいい人間も、足を踏み外したとたん恐怖に支配される。
examples.trans: Even the boldest man is ruled by fear the moment he loses his footing.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning stepped on.

examples.text: 私は毎日踏む。
examples.trans: I stepped on every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒に踏む。
examples.trans: I stepped on together with them.

examples.text: 身にまとった恥を捨てることが重要なんでございます。
examples.trans: Casting off the shame draped around oneself is what truly matters.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: あと、身元引受人が必要なんだけど、母親でいいな？
examples.trans: Also, we need a guarantor to sign you out — your mother works, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 硬くなる必要ないだろう、みんな身内なんだから。
examples.trans: No need to stiffen up like that; everyone at this table is family.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 最近は小遣い欲しさに身分を偽る未成年も多い。
examples.trans: Lately many minors fake their age using an older sister's ID for pocket money.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Automobile or wheeled cart (くるま).

examples.text: ちょっと聞いてください……通りの車の音が、一台も聞こえませんね。
examples.trans: Listen for a moment... you cannot hear a single car from the street.

examples.text: だから昨夜、屋根裏部屋で車の音を聞いていたんですね！
examples.trans: That explains why you listened for car sounds up in the attic last night!

examples.text: 二人とも動くな。今、縁石の前に車のエンジンが止まる音が聞こえたぞ。
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. I just heard a car engine stop by the kerb.

meanings.note: Small rolling wheel on a suitcase or cart.

examples.text: 車輪の裏を見て。兄さんと私の名前が、今も鉛筆で書いてあるよ。
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels: your name and mine are still written there in pencil.

examples.text: 受付に車輪があります。
examples.trans: There is wheel at the reception desk.

examples.text: ねえ、あんたが転がり込んできて結構たつじゃない。
examples.trans: Hey, quite some time has passed since you came crashing in here.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Opposite of 重い ('heavy'); adverb form 軽く.

examples.text: 一番上の棚からだ。そうすれば、本棚が軽くなる。
examples.trans: Start with the top shelf. That way the bookcase gets lighter.

examples.text: このかばんはとても軽いです。
examples.trans: This bag is very light.

meanings.note: Na-adjective formed from 軽い ('light') + -やか.

examples.text: 朝の足音みたいに軽やかなワルツの始まりです。
examples.trans: It is a light, dancing waltz opening, like morning footsteps.

examples.text: 春の風みたいに軽やかなリズムで弾いてみましょう。
examples.trans: Let's play it with a buoyant rhythm like a spring breeze.

載る.gloss: to be placed on, to be published

examples.text: 私の記事が新聞に載った。
examples.trans: My article was published in the newspaper.

examples.text: 机の上に本が載っている。
examples.trans: There is a book on the desk.

meanings.en: to be placed on, to be published

examples.text: 私たちが一億カラットの輝きを生み出すのです。
examples.trans: We will create the brilliance of a hundred-million-carat diamond.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning shining.

examples.text: 私は毎日輝く。
examples.trans: I shining every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒に輝く。
examples.trans: I shining together with them.

meanings.note: Metal washer/ring or circle of people.

examples.text: 中の真鍮の輪が幅二十ミリか、必ず確かめろよ。
examples.trans: Make sure the brass ring inside is twenty millimetres wide.

examples.text: 受付に輪があります。
examples.trans: There is ring at the reception desk.

meanings.note: A colloquial or informal term for a ring, loop, or circle.

examples.text: 煙の輪っかを作って遊んだ。
examples.trans: I played around making smoke rings.

examples.text: 紐の端に輪っかを作る。
examples.trans: To make a loop at the end of a string.

examples.text: 隣見てみろ、中国がある。十一億もの人口、ここに世界一のエロを輸出するんだよ。
examples.trans: Look right next door—one point one billion people! We'll export the world's finest erotica right there!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

辞める.gloss: to quit, to resign, to step down

meanings.en: to quit (a job or school), to resign, to step down from a post
meanings.note: Read やめる (yameru); transitive ichidan verb (一段). Specifically spelled 辞める when leaving an occupation, company, or role (as opposed to 止める for stopping an activity).

examples.text: この仕事、今すぐ辞めてもらえますか？
examples.trans: Could we get you to quit this job right away?

examples.text: さっき会社辞めてきた。これのせいで！
examples.trans: I just quit my company—all because of this!

related.gloss: to stop, to give up (an activity)

examples.text: とっくよ。うち農家なの、お忘れ？
examples.trans: Long ago! Have you forgotten our family runs a farm?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: area, vicinity, neighborhood, point (in a process)
meanings.note: Read へん (hen) after demonstratives like この辺 (around here / at this point) or その辺. When written with okurigana as 辺り, it is read あたり (atari) and attaches to nouns or time words to mean 'around/approximately'.

examples.text: 車はとりあえずこの辺でいいですかね？
examples.trans: Is it okay if I pull over right around here?

examples.text: 今週か来週辺りでご都合のいい時間があれば教えてください。
examples.trans: If there is a convenient time for you sometime around this week or next week, please let me know.

meanings.note: Neighborhood or surroundings (あたり).

examples.text: 冷たいですか？あ、はい！この辺りの水道管は、朝ゆっくり目を覚ますんです！
examples.trans: Cold? Ah—yes! Water pipes in this neighbourhood wake up very gently in the morning!

examples.text: 受付に辺りがあります。
examples.trans: There is area around at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb for welcoming guests at the entrance or station.

examples.text: ねえ陽翔さん、本当に正午に中庭で大輝さんを迎えるのね？
examples.trans: Hey Haruto, so you are really staying in the courtyard to greet Daiki at noon?

examples.text: 十九の理由ですか！？お兄さんを迎えるんですか、それとも電車の時刻表を読むんですか？
examples.trans: Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a train timetable?

meanings.note: Read ちかい (chikai); i-adjective (形容詞). Describes physical proximity (駅から近い) or closeness in relationship/similarity.
Used temporally, especially in the set phrase 近いうちに ('in the near future' / 'before long').

examples.text: 需要があるから、一番近いところに出店したまでです。
examples.trans: There was demand, so I simply opened a shop in the nearest spot available.

examples.text: もう少しの辛抱だ。近いうちに腹いっぱい食えるようになる。
examples.trans: Just hang in there a little longer. Before long, we'll be able to eat our fill.

meanings.note: Noun/adverb for a place close by.

examples.text: 二十五年前、この近くでピアノを教えていたの。もう遠い昔だけど。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano near here, though that was long ago.

examples.text: ああ……この雨の中でですか？駅の近くのホテルはどこも満室でしたよ。
examples.trans: Ah... in this rain? Every hotel near the station was completely full.

examples.text: えっ？昔、ご家族がこの近くに住んでいたんですか？
examples.trans: Oh? Did your family live near here once?

meanings.note: Transitive Ichidan verb (近づける -> 近づけます -> 近づけない -> 近づけた -> 近づけて).

examples.text: ぬれた手を壁のスイッチに近づけないでください。
examples.trans: Please do not bring wet hands near the wall switch.

examples.text: 暗い文字が読めるようにランプを少し近づけました。
examples.trans: I moved the lamp a little closer so we could read the faint writing.

meanings.note: Surrounding houses and shops.

examples.text: あ、待ってください！その通りはここから歩いて五分の近所ですよ！
examples.trans: Oh, wait! That street is right in this neighbourhood, a five-minute walk from here!

examples.text: 築八十年以上の中庭建築は、一階が毎日近所の人々に開かれていれば、専用オフィスに変えられません。
examples.trans: No courtyard building over eighty years old can be turned into private offices if its first floor serves neighbours daily.

examples.text: 「毎日近所の人々に開かれている」……地域の朝カフェみたいにですか！？
examples.trans: 'Open to neighbours every day'... like a neighbourhood morning café?!

meanings.note: a shorter route

examples.text: 近道をして帰ろう。
examples.trans: Let's take a shortcut home.

examples.text: 森を抜けるのが近道だ。
examples.trans: Going through the forest is a shortcut.

meanings.note: to return (something)

examples.text: チェックアウトの際に、部屋の鍵をフロントへお返しください。
examples.trans: When checking out, please return your room key to the front desk.

examples.text: 借りていた古い建築図面を、市役所の担当者に無事返した。
examples.trans: I safely returned the borrowed old architectural blueprints to the city hall official.

examples.text: 元本の返済に充てますか？それとも衛星の電波料に充てますか？
examples.trans: Will you apply this money toward loan principal, or toward the satellite broadcast fee?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 相変わらず不謹慎な男だ。正式に返答を申し上げる。答えはノーだ。
examples.trans: As indiscreet as ever. Let me give you our official reply: the answer is no.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Returning money paid.

examples.text: どうでしたか？怒鳴られましたか？返金してほしいと言われましたか？
examples.trans: Well, how did it go? Did he shout? Did he ask for a refund?

examples.text: 受付に返金があります。
examples.trans: There is refund at the reception desk.

examples.text: それじゃ迫力が出ないだろ。世界初の映像を撮るんだ。
examples.trans: That wouldn't have any impact, would it? We're shooting world-first footage.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

迷い込む.gloss: wander into; lose one's way into

meanings.en: wander into; lose one's way into
meanings.note: Compound Godan verb.

examples.text: お前は一体、どんな魔法みたいな旅館に迷い込んだんだ？
examples.trans: Just what kind of magical inn did you wander into, little brother?

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに迷い込みます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully wander into.

迷う.gloss: to hesitate, to waver, to get lost

meanings.en: to hesitate, to waver, to be torn between choices
meanings.note: Read まよう (mayou); intransitive godan verb (五段). Used when unable to make up one's mind.

meanings.en: to lose one's way, to get lost
meanings.note: Used with に (道に迷う, to lose one's way / get lost).

examples.text: チャンスは今しかない。迷ってる暇はねえだろ。
examples.trans: Now is our only chance. We don't have time to hesitate, do we?

examples.text: あっそうそう！言おうかどうか迷ったんだけどさ、ちょっと聞いた話があって。
examples.trans: Oh, right! I hesitated over whether to mention it, but I heard a rumor...

meanings.note: Read めいわく (meiwaku). Functions as a noun and na-adjective (迷惑な話). Very common in apologies with かける: 迷惑をかける (to cause trouble for someone) and its polite form ご迷惑をおかけします.

examples.text: もう落ち着いています。ご迷惑をおかけしました。
examples.trans: She has calmed down now. I'm sorry for all the trouble I caused.

examples.text: みんな、今まで本当に迷惑かけたな。
examples.trans: Everyone, I'm really sorry for all the trouble I put you through.

examples.text: 幻想を追いかけても意味がない！真実にたどり着くのです！
examples.trans: Chasing illusions is pointless! Watch these and reach the truth!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: じきに時代が追いついてくる。
examples.trans: The times will catch up with us before long.

examples.text: 暴走には誰も追いつけません。衛星への過剰投資で借金はまもなく四十億を超えますよ。
examples.trans: Nobody can catch up to a runaway train! Overinvestment in satellite will push your debt past four billion soon.

meanings.note: Compound godan verb from 追う (chase) + 出す (put out).

examples.text: 騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すからね。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion, I'll throw you out.

examples.text: 家から追い出される。
examples.trans: Get kicked out of the house.

meanings.note: Compound Godan verb ('turn a guest away').

examples.text: 雨の中へ追い返さず、正直に話してくれてありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you both for speaking honestly instead of sending me back into the rain.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに追い返します。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully turn away.

meanings.en: to chase, to pursue, to run after
meanings.note: Read おう (ou). Godan transitive verb; the passive 追われる means 'to be chased/pursued' or 'to be pressed (for time)'.

meanings.en: to follow (with a camera or one's eyes), to track
meanings.note: Commonly used in filmmaking and photography for tracking a moving subject.

examples.text: ラグビー、大丈夫ね？カメラちゃんと追うんだよ、全部収めるんだ。
examples.trans: Rugby, are you ready? Follow the action steadily with the camera and capture everything.

examples.text: 追われてんだよ。かくまってくれよ、頼む！ちょっとでいいんだよ。
examples.trans: People are chasing us—please hide us! Just for a little bit.

追っかけっこ.gloss: game of cat and mouse, chasing

meanings.en: game of cat and mouse, chasing

examples.text: 裏本作ってたお前らと追っかけっこしてた時は平和だったね。懐かしいよ。
examples.trans: Back when I chased you guys around for making underground porn books, things were peaceful. I miss it.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: ここに五億円あります、これは前金ですね。残り十四億円は追ってお支払いいたします。
examples.trans: Here is 500 million yen as a down payment. I will pay the remaining 1.4 billion shortly.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: used in letters

examples.text: 手紙に追伸を書く。
examples.trans: Write a postscript in a letter.

examples.text: 追伸：明日行きます。
examples.trans: P.S. I will go tomorrow.

examples.text: 今月だけ追加で融資をお願いしようと思ってるんです。ほら、いい話でしょ。
examples.trans: So just for this month, I'd like to ask for an extra loan. Sounds great, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: そのうちお前も追放してやるからな。
examples.trans: Before long I'll banish you from this garden too.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: これたまに動かさないと、マヒして退化しちまうんだと。
examples.trans: The doctor says if I don't move this leg once in a while, it'll go numb and wither away.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: こないだ正式に退学しました。
examples.trans: I officially withdrew from university the other day.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Feeling bored when nothing happens.

examples.text: ひだまり旅館へようこそ、美央。二日目も退屈しないぞ。
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hidamari Inn, Mio. Your second day won't be boring either.

examples.text: どうせ通りの雨戸を塗り替えるとか、退屈なお知らせだよ。
examples.trans: It is probably some boring notice about repainting the street shutters.

meanings.note: Godan verb (おくる).

examples.text: 乾いた室内の空気を小窓の方へ送ります。
examples.trans: We blow dry indoor air toward the transom window.

examples.text: 扇風機で廊下に優しい風を送りました。
examples.trans: We sent a gentle breeze down the hallway with a fan.

examples.text: おい急げ、逃がすな！
examples.trans: Hurry up—don't let him get away!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 裏ビデオのことも薬のことも、バレたら逃げきれない。
examples.trans: Underground tapes and drugs—if that comes out, there is no escape.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: どうしてその人は、自分の鞄を受け取らずに逃げたんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why did that person run away without taking back their own bag?

examples.text: どうして夜に私の鞄を石段に置いて、逃げてしまったの？
examples.trans: Why did you set my bag on the stone step at night and run away?

逃げ出す.gloss: to run away, to bolt out

meanings.en: to run away, to bolt out
meanings.note: Compound godan verb 逃げる ('flee') + 出す ('burst out').

examples.text: タルトに海塩を四杯も入れたら担当者が逃げ出すぞ！
examples.trans: If you whisk four spoons of sea salt into the tarts, the clerk will run!

examples.text: 雷の音に驚いて庭の鳥が逃げ出しました。
examples.trans: Startled by the thunder, the garden birds flew off.

meanings.en: the opposite, the reverse, the contrary
meanings.note: Read ぎゃく (gyaku). Functions as a noun and na-adjective (逆な / 逆の).
Used adverbially as 逆に to turn the tables in a conversation or highlight an ironic outcome.

examples.text: では逆に質問させていただきます。
examples.trans: Allow me to ask you a question in return instead.

examples.text: うちは景気がいい時ほど入信者が減るんですよね、逆に。
examples.trans: At our order, the better the economy is, the fewer new believers we get, ironically.

examples.text: 絵が逆さまにかかっている。
examples.trans: The picture is hanging upside down.

examples.text: 順序が逆さまやで。
examples.trans: The order is backwards.

examples.text: これね、透けるとね街ゆく皆様にご迷惑がかかりますからね。少しでもね、エチケット。
examples.trans: If people on the street could see right through my briefs, it would trouble them—call it basic etiquette.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Allowing light to pass through so that objects behind can be distinctly seen.

examples.text: このガラスは完全に透明だ。
examples.trans: This glass is completely transparent.

examples.text: 透明な水が流れている。
examples.trans: Clear water is flowing.

meanings.note: In the middle of a page, task, or journey.

examples.text: どうして二ページ目の途中で書くのを止めたんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why did she stop writing halfway through page two?

examples.text: 駅へ行く途中にとてもいいパン屋さんがあります。
examples.trans: On the way to the station there is a wonderful bakery.

meanings.note: Transitive Godan verb ('guide a guest in / run hot water through').

examples.text: 素晴らしいですね……待っている間に、大家さんからの手紙にざっと目を通しましょう。
examples.trans: How wonderful... while we wait, let me glance through this letter from the landlord.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに通します。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully let through.

meanings.note: Reads とおり or どおり in street names.

examples.text: 由香はこの通りのみんなと昔からの友達みたいに話すんだ。
examples.trans: Yuka talks with everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: その通り！もうすっかりここの仲間だね。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in.

examples.text: 素敵ですね。窓は通り側ですか、それとも中庭側ですか？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street side or the courtyard side?

meanings.note: To pass through, to go through, or to make one's way through.

examples.text: トンネルを通り抜ける。
examples.trans: Pass through a tunnel.

examples.text: 人混みを通り抜けて駅に向かった。
examples.trans: I made my way through the crowd and headed to the station.

meanings.note: Compound Ichidan verb.

examples.text: ああ、橋を渡ったら、右手にある緑の薬局を通り過ぎる。
examples.trans: Yeah, once you cross the bridge, pass the green pharmacy on your right.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに通り過ぎます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully walk past.

通る.gloss: to pass by, go down (a street)

meanings.en: to pass by, go down (a street)
meanings.note: Intransitive godan verb taking を for the path traversed.

examples.text: 今、けやき通りを大きなトラックが通りましたか？
examples.trans: Did a heavy truck just drive down Keyaki Lane?

examples.text: 毎朝この雨戸の前を通っていたのに気づきませんでした。
examples.trans: Even though I walked past these shutters every morning, I stopped noticing them.

examples.text: これは宇宙空間にある通信衛星だ。
examples.trans: This right here is a communications satellite floating in outer space.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 通報を受けてからパトカーが到着するまで二十分かかる。
examples.trans: Once a call goes in, it takes twenty minutes for police cars to arrive.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 通達は届いてますよね？
examples.trans: You received our official notice, didn't you?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: I-adjective for rapid speed.

examples.text: 見事な速さです！お店の人から領収書をもらいましたか？
examples.trans: Impressive speed! Did you get a receipt from the shopkeeper?

examples.text: 青いハンドルを左へゆっくり回せ。速すぎるなよ。
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel slowly to the left. Not too fast.

meanings.note: Deadjectival measurement noun formed from 速い ('fast, quick') + -さ ('-ness; rate of').

examples.text: 同じ角切りなら、まったく同じ速さで火が通るんだよ、兄さん。基本の物理さ！
examples.trans: Even cubes cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!

examples.text: 風の速さがちょうどよくて、廊下のペンキがきれいに乾きました。
examples.trans: The speed of the breeze was just right, and the paint in the hallway dried nicely.

examples.text: 地震の速報が流れた。
examples.trans: A breaking news report about the earthquake was broadcast.

examples.text: 試合の速報をお伝えします。
examples.trans: We bring you a live update of the match.

meanings.note: fast mail

examples.text: 速達で送る。
examples.trans: Send by special delivery.

examples.text: 速達料金。
examples.trans: Express delivery fee.

meanings.note: This is used as a verb meaning take.

examples.text: 私は毎日連れていく。
examples.trans: I take every day.

examples.text: 彼らと一緒に連れていく。
examples.trans: I take together with them.

examples.text: そんなこといいから連れてこい。
examples.trans: Never mind that, just bring her over here.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; 連れてくる means 'bring someone along'.

examples.text: 来週は市役所の半分を由香さんのテーブルへ連れて来ますよ、約束します。
examples.trans: Next week we will bring half of City Hall to Yuka's tables, I promise.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに連れます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully bring along.

meanings.note: Read れんちゅう (renchū). Informal collective noun referring to a group of people, often carrying a rough, familiar, or slightly dismissive tone.
Attaches directly to nouns like 幹部連中 ('the executive crowd/brass').

examples.text: ちょっと幹部連中と話してきます。
examples.trans: I'm going to go have a quick word with the executive brass.

examples.text: 面白いね君。ここにいる連中は国の経済を支えている連中なんだよ。
examples.trans: You are funny. The people in this room are the ones propping up the nation's economy.

examples.text: 姉妹でピアノの連弾を披露した。
examples.trans: The sisters performed a piano duet together.

examples.text: 連弾の楽譜を買った。
examples.trans: I bought sheet music for a duet.

meanings.note: Used with する ('contact / notify').

examples.text: まだ連絡はないそうです、和子さん。本当に申し訳ありません。
examples.trans: They have no word yet, Kazuko. I am truly sorry.

examples.text: 受付に連絡があります。
examples.trans: There is contact at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Read たいほ (taiho). Combines with する to form the transitive verb 逮捕する ('to arrest').

examples.text: よし、逮捕しろ。
examples.trans: All right, arrest him.

examples.text: ビザ詐欺の容疑で逮捕しておいて、古い法律で起訴してるんですよ。
examples.trans: They arrested him on visa fraud suspicions, then indicted him under an archaic law.

meanings.note: Sino-Japanese 週 (しゅう).

examples.text: この踏み台には週に十回は乗っていますよ。
examples.trans: I climb onto this stool at least ten times a week.

examples.text: 週の半ばの水曜日にカフェを再開します。
examples.trans: We reopen the café midweek on Wednesday.

meanings.note: Saturday and Sunday (しゅうまつ).

examples.text: 誰からだい？週末の新しい予約か？
examples.trans: Who is calling? Another reservation for the weekend?

examples.text: 受付に週末があります。
examples.trans: There is weekend at the reception desk.

meanings.note: Usually intransitive

examples.text: 前に進む。
examples.trans: Go forward.

examples.text: 計画が進む。
examples.trans: The plan advances.

examples.text: 新しい年号になる準備進めろ。
examples.trans: Move ahead with preparations for the new imperial era name.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Stepping forward compared to before.

examples.text: 進歩ですね！今日は中庭で家族の再会がありますから、皆さん静かな品格を保ちましょう！
examples.trans: Progress! Today our courtyard hosts a family reunion, so let us all keep quiet dignity!

examples.text: 受付に進歩があります。
examples.trans: There is progress at the reception desk.

meanings.note: I-adjective for late hours or slow pace.

examples.text: あっ、遅かったです！「ありがとうございます」と言って切れました！
examples.trans: Oh, too late! He said 'Thank you' and the line clicked off!

examples.text: 今日はとても遅いですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very late, isn't it?

meanings.note: Arriving past the scheduled time.

examples.text: どうぞ一緒に座ってください、和子先生！レッスンに二十五年遅刻したなんて言わないでくださいね！
examples.trans: Please sit down with us, Miss Kazuko! Just do not tell me I am twenty-five years late for my lesson!

examples.text: 受付に遅刻があります。
examples.trans: There is lateness at the reception desk.

examples.text: おい、お前ら遊びに行くんじゃねえからな。
examples.trans: Hey, you guys aren't going over there to play around.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Te-form 遊んで before きていい asks permission to go play and come back.

examples.text: 外で遊んできます。
examples.trans: I am going outside to play.

examples.text: 子供たちが庭で遊んでいます。
examples.trans: Children are playing in the yard.

examples.text: 今日は運がいい。
examples.trans: I am lucky today.

examples.text: 試験に受かったのは運が良かっただけだ。
examples.trans: I only passed the exam because I was lucky.

meanings.note: Noun from 運ぶ ('carry'); テーブル運び = 'carrying tables'.

examples.text: それに、陽翔さんと大輝さんが、テーブル運びを無料で手伝ってくれるって！
examples.trans: And Haruto and Daiki say they'll help carry the tables for free!

examples.text: 引っ越しの荷物運びを手伝いました。
examples.trans: I helped carry the boxes for the move.

meanings.note: Godan verb for carrying luggage or trays.

examples.text: この奥です。青い鞄は私が上まで運びますよ。
examples.trans: Right through here. I will carry the blue bag upstairs for you.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに運びます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully carry.

meanings.note: Potential form of 運ぶ.

examples.text: 四つの箱なら五分で運べます。今すぐ見に行きましょう！
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes. Let's go look right now!

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに運べます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully can carry.

meanings.note: Professional driver of a delivery van, bus, or taxi.

examples.text: 配達の運転手さんに木曜日の午後と伝えたはずです。
examples.trans: I thought I told the delivery driver Thursday afternoon.

examples.text: バスの運転手さんが親切に降りる場所を教えてくれました。
examples.trans: The bus driver kindly told me where to get off.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb (すぎる -> すぎます) for passing a time or 'too ...'.

examples.text: 健二さん、聞こえますか？今、緑の薬局を過ぎたところです！
examples.trans: Kenji, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

examples.text: 隆さん、開けるのは十二時過ぎてからにして！時計を見て、正午まであと五分だよ！
examples.trans: Takashi, open it after twelve! Look at the clock: five minutes to noon!

meanings.note: Transitive Godan verb ('spend a quiet afternoon').

examples.text: 大阪の最初の夜に、お部屋で寂しく過ごすなんて駄目ですよ！
examples.trans: You cannot spend your first evening in Osaka feeling lonely upstairs!

examples.text: 外の人にはまだ一言も言わないで！まずはあの兄弟に金曜日の午後を過ごさせてあげましょう！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let those brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

examples.text: 暴走には誰も追いつけません。衛星への過剰投資で借金はまもなく四十億を超えますよ。
examples.trans: Nobody can catch up to a runaway train! Overinvestment in satellite will push your debt past four billion soon.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 想像以上だよ。これからは過激な本番シリーズをどんどん作っていく。
examples.trans: Sales are beyond imagination. From here on we will crank out bold real-action series.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 美しすぎるといっても過言ではないでしょう！
examples.trans: It is no exaggeration to call this breathtakingly beautiful!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Path or street (みち).

examples.text: はい！左に細い道が二本あります。どちらを行けばいいですか？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two narrow lanes on the left. Which one should I take?

examples.text: 狭い路地じゃなくて、花屋の横の二番目の道を行け。
examples.trans: Not the cramped alley—take the second street beside the flower shop.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for carpentry tools, kitchen utensils, or craft implements (どうぐ).

examples.text: 昼は私が静かな部屋を設計して、市役所の仕事が終わったら兄さんが祖父の木の道具を持って来ます！
examples.trans: By day I design quiet rooms, and after work at City Hall my brother brings Grandfather's wood tools!

examples.text: 健二さんはいつも大工の道具をきれいに磨いて箱に入れています。
examples.trans: Kenji always polishes his carpentry tools clean and keeps them in a box.

meanings.note: Box holding wrenches, washers, and repair tools.

examples.text: 道具箱の中に、予備の真鍮バルブはありませんか？
examples.trans: Is there no spare brass valve inside your toolbox?

examples.text: 現金で払いました！道具箱を開けて待っていてください、走って帰ります！
examples.trans: Paid in cash! Keep your toolbox open, I am running back now!

meanings.note: Read どうけい (dōkei). Abbreviation of 北海道警察 (Hokkaidō Keisatsu), as Hokkaido is the only 道 (circuit/territory) in Japan's prefectural system.

examples.text: 道警の森だ。責任者はいるか？
examples.trans: I'm Mori from the Hokkaido Prefectural Police. Is the person in charge here?

examples.text: 道警の捜査員が朝から事務所に踏み込んできた。
examples.trans: Investigators from the Hokkaido Police raided the office first thing in the morning.

meanings.note: Paved public road.

examples.text: あと数分待ちましょう、陽翔さん。お昼の町の道路はいつも混んでいますから。
examples.trans: Let's wait a few more minutes, Haruto. City roads at lunchtime are always crowded.

examples.trans: The children are running in the park.

examples.text: 君は素養があるね、違いが分かるってことは。

違いない.gloss: there is no doubt; must be

meanings.en: there is no doubt; must be
meanings.note: Expression functioning as an i-adjective. Attaches to clauses.

examples.text: 犯人はあの男に違いない。
examples.trans: The culprit must undoubtedly be that man.

examples.text: 彼女は私のことを怒っているに違いない。
examples.trans: She must be angry at me.

meanings.note: Alone as 違う！ or 違います, means 'No, that's wrong!'.

examples.text: いいえ、違います。
examples.trans: No, that is wrong.

examples.text: 番号が違いますよ。
examples.trans: The number is different / wrong.

meanings.en: to change, to alter, to mistake, to break (a promise)
meanings.note: Read ちがえる (chigaeru). Ichidan transitive verb, frequently used in compounds like 見違える ('to look completely different') or 履き違える ('to misunderstand').

meanings.en: to be different, to make a difference (colloquial contraction of 違う)
meanings.note: In rough colloquial speech, 違うな ('it really makes a difference') contracts to 違えな (ちげえな / ちがえな), which tokenizers map to 違える.

examples.text: 連れてきたぞ。やっぱ人がいると違えな。
examples.trans: I brought helpers along! Having extra people really makes a difference.

examples.text: 約束を違えるような男は絶対に信用するな。
examples.trans: Never trust a man who goes back on his word.

examples.text: 中には違法な制作をし、モザイクを付けずに販売する業者などが増えてきております。
examples.trans: Among new entrants, more and more operators are producing illegally and selling tapes without mosaics.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: I-adjective for long distance.

examples.text: 二十五年前、この近くでピアノを教えていたの。もう遠い昔だけど。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano near here, though that was long ago.

examples.text: 今日はとても遠いですね。
examples.trans: Today it is very far, isn't it?

examples.text: 犬に餌をやる。
examples.trans: I feed the dog.

examples.text: 一緒にテニスをやろう。
examples.trans: Let's play tennis together.

examples.text: 川田さんが適任です。

examples.trans: Heard you got robbed by your own staff. Man, you really are hilarious.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan verb (えらぶ -> えらびます -> えらばない -> えらんだ -> えらんで).

examples.text: 本当を言うと、この町を選んだのには昔の家族の理由もあるんです。
examples.trans: To tell the truth, I also chose this neighbourhood for an old family reason.

examples.text: 毎日ていねいに選びます。
examples.trans: Every day I carefully choose.

examples.text: 今度は選挙に出馬かい。村西君ってホント面白えよな。
examples.trans: Running in an election this time? Muranishi really is hilarious.

examples.trans: Permission from the Heritage Department is necessary.

examples.trans: That porn director's commotion came up at the board meeting. Avoid any needless reputational damage.

meanings.en: hindrance, obstacle, nuisance, being in the way
meanings.note: Read じゃま (jama). Functions as a noun, na-adjective (邪魔な), and suru-verb (邪魔する, 'to disturb or get in the way').
Used in the set greeting お邪魔します ('Excuse the intrusion' / 'May I come in?').

examples.text: うち、今から仕事なんだからさ。そこ邪魔なの。
examples.trans: I have to go to work right now, so you're in the way there.

examples.text: お邪魔します。少しだけお時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Pardon the intrusion. Could you spare me just a moment of your time?

meanings.en: counter for copies of a newspaper, magazine, book, or publication
meanings.note: Read ぶ (bu), e.g., 三十万部 ('300,000 copies').

meanings.en: department, division, club, or component part
meanings.note: Also serves as a bound root in compounds such as 部外者 (ぶがいしゃ, 'outsider') or 営業部 ('sales department').

examples.text: すでに三十万部ほど売り上げてるのか。
examples.trans: So it has already sold around three hundred thousand copies?

examples.text: 俺は部外者じゃない、アダルトビデオの監督だ。
examples.trans: I am no outsider; I am an adult video director.

meanings.note: Read ぶぶん (bubun). Refers both to physical segments (of a video, body, or text) and abstract aspects of a situation.

examples.text: この部分をよく見ろ。
examples.trans: Look closely at this part right here.

examples.text: 報道機関が都合の悪い部分をモザイクで隠しているほうが問題です。
examples.trans: Media outlets hiding inconvenient truths behind pixelation is a bigger problem.

meanings.note: Guest room or interior room (へや).

examples.text: ああ、部屋は八室、真鍮の鍵も八つだ。今日は四号室にお客さんが来る。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 落ち着いてよ、隆さん。部屋はきれいだし、タオルも新しい。
examples.trans: Relax, Takashi. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.

meanings.note: Compound of 部屋 ('room') + 番号 ('number').

examples.text: 宿帳には日付と部屋番号とお名前が並んでいます。
examples.trans: Date, room number, and guest name are lined up in the ledger.

examples.text: 鍵の札に書いてある部屋番号を確かめました。
examples.trans: I checked the room number written on the key tag.

meanings.note: Standard noun for postal mail or letters delivered by post (ゆうびん).

examples.text: 金曜日の夜に郵便ですか？受付へ持っていきましょう！
examples.trans: Mail on a Friday night? Let us take it to the front desk!

examples.text: 今朝の郵便で、遠くに住む友人から絵はがきが届きました。
examples.trans: In this morning's mail, a picture postcard arrived from a friend living far away.

meanings.note: Friendly polite term for the person delivering mail.

examples.text: たった今、郵便屋さんに受領のサインをしました。不動産管理室の赤い印鑑が押してあります。
examples.trans: I just signed for it from the postman. It bears a red stamp from the property office.

examples.text: 受付に郵便屋さんがあります。

meanings.note: things delivered by post

examples.trans: Send by mail.

meanings.note: Read さけ (sake), or おさけ with the polite prefix お-. Refers both to alcoholic drinks in general and specifically to brewed rice wine.

examples.text: お酒、飲んでないですね？
examples.trans: You haven't been drinking any alcohol, have you?

examples.text: こんなに飲んだの久しぶり。お酒強いのね。
examples.trans: It's been ages since I drank this much. You really hold your liquor well.

examples.trans: This lemon is very sour.

examples.text: 酸っぱい梅干しを食べる。
examples.trans: Eat a sour pickled plum.

examples.text: このレモンは酸っぱすぎて食べられない。

examples.text: 土曜日の市場で新鮮な野菜をたくさん買いました。
examples.trans: We bought lots of fresh vegetables at Saturday's market.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat and a cup of hot vegetable soup.

examples.trans: Your palate is barbaric! I'm the type who likes clear boundaries on things like this.

examples.trans: We will spend five times our previous budget and mass-produce!

examples.trans: Hey, you guys are ramping up mass production too, right?

meanings.note: A gold medal, typically awarded for first place in a competition.

examples.text: 彼はオリンピックで金メダルを獲得した。

meanings.note: Compound of 金 ('metal') and 具 ('fitting, hardware').

examples.text: 譜面台の折りたたみの金具をそっと開きました。
examples.trans: We gently opened the folding metal hinge on the music desk.

examples.text: 古い箱の真鍮の金具を布で磨きました。
examples.trans: I polished the brass fittings on the old box with a cloth.

meanings.note: Metallic material like brass, iron, or copper.

examples.text: 早く閉じて！上へ届けましょう……えっ、今の大きな金属の音は何ですか？
examples.trans: Close it quickly! Let's take it upstairs—wait, what was that loud metallic clank?

examples.text: 本当に静かですよ！……でも今、洗面所の方から変な金属の音がしませんでしたか？
examples.trans: Truly peaceful! ...Though did a strange metallic knock just come from the washroom?

examples.text: 箱を傾けると音がするぞ。中で何か金属が滑った。
examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the box: something metal slid inside.

meanings.note: Compound noun combining 金 (money/gold) and 庫 (storehouse).

examples.text: 大切な書類を金庫にしまいました。
examples.trans: I put the important documents in the safe.

examples.text: 金庫が空っぽになっています。
examples.trans: The safe is empty.

meanings.note: Shortened form of 金曜日.

examples.text: どうして金曜まで、靴や木の汽車を知らない宿に預けるんでしょう？
examples.trans: Why leave your shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?

examples.text: もしもし？「白い紙の包みは開けないでください。金曜の正午に行きます」と……
examples.trans: Hello? He says, 'Please do not open the white paper parcel. I will come Friday at noon'...

examples.text: 金曜まで近くに静かな場所が必要で、正直、自分の鞄を返してと頼むのが恥ずかしかったんです！
examples.trans: I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly felt too shy to ask for my bag!

meanings.note: Fifth day of the workweek; reads きんようび.

examples.text: 読みますね。「間違えてすみません。青い鞄を金曜日まで預かってください。」
examples.trans: Let me read it: 'Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.'

examples.text: 金曜日まで？名前も署名もないじゃないか！
examples.trans: Until Friday? There is no name and no signature!

examples.text: 金曜日まで預かってほしいと、短いメモがありました。
examples.trans: There was a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Neighborhood shop selling tools, valves, and keys.

examples.text: 最後の一個を冬に使ったんだ。橋の向こうの古い金物屋にしか、このサイズはない。
examples.trans: I used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

examples.text: その金物屋は、朝何時に開きますか？
examples.trans: What time in the morning does that hardware shop open?

examples.text: 入れました。さあ、金物屋への行き方を教えてください。
examples.trans: Got it. Now please tell me how to get to the hardware shop.

examples.text: 監督、今日一日金策で帰れないって。きっと何とかしてくれるよ。
examples.trans: The director won't be back all day raising funds. I'm sure he'll work something out.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Gold that has been beaten into a very thin foil, used for gilding.

examples.trans: Only a painted golden key above the door. Show this valve to the clerk.

examples.text: 今歩いています……あっ、金色の鍵の看板と青いドアが見えました！
examples.trans: Walking now... oh, I can see the golden key sign and the blue door!

meanings.note: This is used as a noun meaning gold coin.

examples.text: これは金貨です。
examples.trans: This is gold coin.

examples.trans: With this, swear you will never have anything to do with us again!

examples.trans: Then I suppose it depends on the price. How much are you offering?

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: Inside the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.
